cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing (including forming most printed upper- and lower-case letters), cursive, or typing.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce individual or group writing. With guidance and support from adults, produce writing through printing (including letter- like marks or forming some printed letters).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use digital tools like computers or tablets to publish my writing and work with classmates to create shared projects, while also practicing both printing and typing letters.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use digital tools like computers or tablets to create and publish my writing with help, and I can print most upper- and lower-case letters correctly.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a computer or tablet with help to write and try forming some printed letters.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use a variety of digital tools to produce writing, including in collaboration with peers.
I can work with peers at an interactive whiteboard, select from an array of pictures and type some letters using the onscreen keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
I can work with peers, select words and pictures from an alternative keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce writing, including in collaboration with peers.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher while working with peers at an interactive whiteboard, select from an array of pictures and types some letters using the onscreen keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher while working with peers, selects words and pictures from an alternative keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, explore digital tools to produce writing, including in collaboration with peers.
I can explore teacher-selected form of technology appropriate to the individual student to produce a product for the teacher to print and post on the bulletin board.
I can explore technology that supports writing and communication with peers (e.g., use a switch or touchscreen to communicate meaningfully).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, explore various means of accessing digital tools.
I can activate a switch to scan through the letters of the alphabet.
I can touch, bang, or swipe over the surface of an alternative keyboard to produce a product for the teacher to print and post on the bulletin board.
I can touch a touchscreen on a computer or tablet device for a peer to print to include in a class book entitled, This Week’s Writing.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Participate in shared inquiry and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of “how-to” books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).
ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in shared inquiry and writing projects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can work with others to explore different books and write detailed instructions or a project plan using what we’ve learned.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can work with others to explore “how-to” books and write a sequence of instructions for a project or activity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can work with others and write simple steps for a project or activity with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate to share research and writing projects with others.
I can identify pictures and words to include in a shared research project on a familiar topic (e.g., “what we know about whales,” point to relevant pictures and words from a book about whales).
I can select the topic of the research project and choose words or ideas to include.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can participate in shared research and writing projects.
I can select a book on a topic related to a shared research project from a collection identified by peers and identifies pictures that relate to the topic being researched.
I can type letters as they are dictated by a peer to add content to a shared writing project.
I can Recall information from a shared school experience and participate in a shared writing project to list details from that experience.
I can listen to an electronic book appropriate to the research and writing project, and share one fact with the group to include in the project.
I can listen with a peer to electronic books selected by the teacher in a digital reading environment and with a keyboard with alphabet and whole word access, type letters, words, or sentences about what they learn.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, participate in shared research and writing projects.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher, select a book from a choice of two related to the shared research project and identifies pictures that relate to the topic being researched.
I can given a premade set-up on an alternative keyboard or onscreen keyboard, select words and pictures to add to a shared research and writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with prompts and support, explore pictures, words, or objects related to a shared research project.
I can given a multimedia presentation of words and pictures related to a shared research project, use a switch to advance through the pictures looking and/or listening to the words and pictures.
I can use a touchscreen to scroll through pictures related to the topic of a shared research project.
I can explore a bin full of objects and artifacts related to a shared research project.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can gather information from different sources or my own experiences to answer questions and explain my answers in detail.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can remember or find information to answer a question with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can remember or find some information to answer a question with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can work with the teacher, recall information from a recent school book fair for the teacher to write down (e.g., “book,” “money,” “library”) and then answer the teacher’s question when she asks, “Do you like the book?”
I can work with a small group and the teacher, recall information from a just completed group project, telling the teacher what they used (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, paper) so she can write a list, and then respond to the teacher’s question when she asks, “Did you finish?”
I can listen to an electronic book with a peer and select answers from a picture or word bank to who and what questions about the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can work with the teacher, select a book purchased at a recent book fair so the teacher can write down the name and then answer the teacher’s question when she asked, “Do you like the book?,” and place a check in the like column.
I can work with a small group and the teacher, identify supplies from those assembled on the table that were used in completing a group project (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, paper) so the teacher can add them to the list and then respond to the teacher’s question when she asks, “Did you finish?”
I can use a picture/label schedule to identify the next activity of the day by answering what questions (e.g., What is after math? What is next? What is first today?).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences.
I can work with the teacher, identify the centers completed that day and the teacher will write them in the student’s home-school notebook.
I can work with a small group and the teacher, identify supplies from those assembled on the table that were used in completing a group project (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, and paper) so the teacher can create a list.
I can with guidance and support, complete open-ended statements about personal experiences when provided with an array of two or more relevant responses (e.g., Playing outside is <fun, hot>).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify personal objects.
I can with guidance and support, select own backpack from two presented at the end of the day which the teacher adds to a chart story (e.g., This sign says Allen. This is Allen’s backpack. This sign says Brian. This is Brian’s backpack.).
I can with guidance and support, select own lunchbox when presented with an array of two or more which the teacher adds to a chart story (e.g., Allen’s lunchbox is blue. Brian’s lunchbox is red.)

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: With guidance and support from adults, recall and use facts from literary and informational text to support reflection and inquiry on characters, setting, key details, specified information, and ideas presented in a text.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use facts from stories or informational texts to answer questions about characters, settings, and ideas, and explain how these facts support my thinking.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can remember and use facts from stories or informational texts to answer questions about characters, settings, or ideas with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can remember and use simple facts from stories or informational texts to answer questions with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can remember one fact from a story or informational text when someone helps me.
I can talk about the characters or setting of a story with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can remember important details from a story or text.
I can retell key information from a story with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say one important thing I remember from a story with support.
I can recall a detail from a story or text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures or words to show something I remember from a story.
I can point to something in the book that helps me remember the story with guidance.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups. a. With guidance and support, follow agreed-upon norms for discussions and participate by actively listening, taking turns, and staying on topic.
ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in conversations with adults. a. Engage in multiple-turn exchanges with supportive adults.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can participate in discussions by listening carefully, taking turns, and staying on topic without reminders, and help others follow discussion rules.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can follow the rules for discussions by listening, taking turns, and staying on topic with some reminders.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can listen and take turns in a discussion with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can initiate multiple-turn exchanges with peers.
I can during a literacy center activity, hold up own work to show peer and say, “look.” When peer responds, the student continues in the exchange for at least one more turn.
I can when getting ready to read with a partner, initiate an interaction saying, “Read?” The peer responds “Sure, where should we go?” and the student says, “corner” while pointing to the reading corner. The interaction continues so that both students have at least two turns.
I can during snack time, use a multiple message voice output device to say, “Scooby Doo!” and then looks directly at a peer. The peer responds, “Scooby Doo!” The student uses the device to link together, “You - Scooby Doo!” and the peer responds, “No, you - Scooby Doo.” The interaction continues with the two playfully teasing one another.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers.
I can while at a literacy center working with letters and words, participate in multiple-turn exchanges (e.g., one of the peers hands the student a letter and says, “You need this one?” The student replies, “No, b!” The peer finds a b and says, “This one?” The student replies, “Yeah, b.”).
I can when the snack helper asks, “What do you want?” and holds up the white milk and chocolate milk, look directly at the chocolate milk. When the peer acknowledges, “Okay, chocolate,” use sign language to say, “Thank you.” The peer replies, “You’re welcome.”
I can use a sequenced message device to communicate a social script with a peer such as: Student activates switch to say, “Wanna hear a joke?” Peer says “Okay.” Student activates switch to say, “What number does a pig call when he’s in trouble?” Peer says, “I don’t know” and student activates switch to say “Swine 1-1.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can communicate directly with a peer.
I can use a sequenced message device to call students’ names to line up to leave the room.
I can use a single message voice output device to say “hi” to a peer when travelling down the hall.
I can call a peer by name to ask him to come play.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate with a peer.
I can during morning meeting, use a single message voice output device to say, “Good morning” to each classmate when the teacher prompts, “What do you want to say to John?” while pointing to the single message device.
I can during P.E., sit next to the P.E. teacher and use a sequenced message device to call the names of peers in a game like Red Rover. The P.E. teacher prompts by telling when it is time to “Tell them who to send now!”

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.
ee_text: Build on comments or topics initiated by an adult.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can add my own thoughts to conversations by responding to what others say and keeping the discussion going with multiple exchanges.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can respond to what others say in conversations and add my own ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add a simple response to what others say in conversations with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can build on comments or topics initiated by an adult and peers.
I can during shared reading, the teacher points to an illustration and comments, “Look at that dog!” Another peer comments, “I have a dog like that!” The student adds, “big dog,” and the teacher acknowledges, “Yes, this is a big dog in the picture.”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can build on comments or topics initiated by an adult.
I can during shared reading, when the teacher points to an illustration and comments, “Look at that dog!,” the student responds using sign language to communicate, “Me!” The teacher replies, “Me? Do you have a dog?” and the student nods.
I can reply “Sunny?” when an adult comments about the weather saying, “It sure is hot out there. It feels like summer.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, build on comments or topics initiated by an adult.
I can during shared reading, the teacher points to an illustration and comments, “Look at that dog!” Then she says, “You have a dog, don’t you?” The student responds by saying, “Me.” The teacher adds, “I have seen your dog. You have a big dog.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate with an adult about the current topic.
I can during morning meeting, the teacher looks out the window and says, “It looks rainy out there!” then shows the students a picture of rain saying, “This is rain. Look at the picture of rain.” The student looks at the picture of rain.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.
ee_text: Use one or two words to ask questions related to the topic or text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask questions to make sure I understand everything being discussed and clarify any confusion during conversations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions when I don’t understand something in a discussion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask for help if I don’t understand something with support from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can combines three or more words to ask questions related to personally relevant topics.
I can during shared reading, point to a page in the book and ask, “What doggie doing?”
I can during literacy centers, use a multiple message communication device to link together words and ask, “What you do?”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use one or two-words to ask questions related to personally relevant topics.
I can at lunchtime, use sign to ask for “More?” of a preferred food item.
I can after lunch, ask if they are going outside for recess (i.e., “Go outside?”).
I can select a single picture symbol from a communication display of four or more symbols during a shared reading activity to ask a question (e.g., The message says one of the following: “I have a question,” “Who,” or “Why.”). Teacher responds according to the question (e.g., “Who? Do you want to know who did it? Let’s see.”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, use one or two-words to ask questions related to personally relevant topics.
I can during snack time, the student grabs for more crackers but the teacher stops him and supports him in pointing to a picture symbol representing the word more. As the child touches more the teacher says, “Can I have more?”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use gestures, vocalizations, symbols, or words to communicate about personally relevant topics.
I can on the playground, vocalize or hit a single message voice output device to signal “go fast” so that someone will push him fast across the yard.
I can during snack time, touch own mouth to indicate a desire for more food.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.
ee_text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can adjust how I speak depending on who I am talking to, taking into account others' feelings, needs, or language differences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can think about how others feel or what they need when I speak to them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show kindness when talking to others with reminders from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can listen to others and share my thoughts when someone helps me.
I can think about how others feel when talking to them with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can listen to others and think about how they feel before talking.
I can communicate with others in a way that is kind and respectful.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can listen to what someone says and respond with help.
I can think about how others feel when I talk with support.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to others using gestures or words with help.
I can show care for others when I communicate with guidance.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
ee_text: During shared reading activities, answer questions about details presented orally or through other media.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask and answer detailed questions about important parts of a story or information I’ve heard to show I understand.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask and answer questions about important details in a story or information I’ve heard.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can answer simple questions about important details from a story or information I’ve heard with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can during shared reading activities, ask and answer questions about key details presented orally or through other media.
I can ask, “What’s that?” in reference to a picture in the book and answers the teacher when she responds, “What do you see?”
I can use a multiple message voice output device to respond to the teacher’s question, “What did the boy do?,” saying, “play.” Then, asks the teacher, “Why?”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can during shared reading activities, answer questions about details presented orally or through other media.
I can answer yes/no questions about key details presented in a story read aloud.
I can point to a picture in the book to respond when asked a question such as, “Where is the brick house?”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support during shared reading activities, provides responses to open-ended statements.
I can after asking the question, “What did the boy see?” and not getting a response, the teacher transforms the question and says, “The boy saw____,” and the student selects a symbol that finishes the sentence.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support during shared reading activities, follow simple directives.
I can during shared reading, reaches out when the teacher comes close, holds out the book, and says, “Turn the page.”
I can during shared reading, the student looks at the illustration when the teacher says, “look” and shines a flashlight on the page.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.
ee_text: Communicate confusion or lack of understanding ("I don't know.").

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask detailed questions to get more information or to better understand what someone is saying, and answer others' questions with clear explanations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask and answer questions to better understand what someone says.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask simple questions when I don’t understand something with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can ask for help when needed using words.
I can use communication device, conventional sign, or spoken words to ask for assistance when needed.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask for help when needed.
I can indicate a need for assistance through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can use a switch to gain attention.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, ask for help when needed.
I can when asked, “Do you need help?” respond to indicate need for assistance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, respond to offer of assistance when needed.
I can when teacher offers assistance, respond by attending to teacher.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Presentation of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas clearly.
ee_text: Identify familiar people, places, things, and events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can describe people, places, things, and events with many details to help others understand exactly what I mean.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe people, places, things, and events with details that help others understand my ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe people, places, and things with some details with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify familiar people, places, things, and events.
I can identify people through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can identify a photograph or drawing of a birthday party or other event held in the classroom.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support, identify familiar people, places, things, and events.
I can with guidance and support, identify familiar people through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can identify a desired objects from choices (e.g., During a before-reading activity, the teacher introduces a number of objects that will be found in the story; during reading, the teacher offers the student a choice of two when the item appears in the book and the student points or gazes to the correct object when asked.).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, identify favorite people and things.
I can with guidance and support, identify a favorite toy or comfort item from a display of two or more.
I can with guidance and support, identify a favorite person by eye contact, eye gaze, vocalizations, etc.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to familiar people, places, things, and events with guidance and support.
I can with guidance and support, respond to familiar people through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can with guidance and support, respond to a photo, drawing, or object about a classroom event.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Presentation of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Create an original or utilize existing visual displays to support descriptions to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
ee_text: Add or select drawings or other visual or tactile displays that relate to familiar people, places, things, and events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create my own drawings or use existing pictures to help explain my ideas and make them easier to understand.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use drawings or pictures to help explain my ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use pictures or drawings with help to show what I mean.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can combine three or more words, signs, or symbols to communicate own thoughts, feelings, or ideas.
I can when asked “What do you want?,” respond, “I want more.”
I can when asked to make a prediction during shared reading, “What do you think will happen?,” reply, “Boy go fast.”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can communicate own thoughts, feelings, or ideas.
I can select a drawing or other visual display that represents own ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
I can, given a communication device with an array of symbols representing feelings, select a symbol to tell how he or she is feeling.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, communicate own thoughts, feelings, or ideas.
I can when asked, “Are you happy today?,” repeats, “happy.”
I can use picture exchange cards (PECS) indicate how they are feeling or how an activity makes them feel.
I can use symbols, switches, etc., choose from pictures how an event makes the students feel.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, respond when asked about feelings.
I can when asked “How are you feeling today?” respond by focusing on the person asking.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Knowledge of Language
text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures and contexts; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening; and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. a. Recognize and appreciate the linguistic diversity of peers, teachers, and other members of the school community.
ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. Notice linguistic diversity.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can recognize and explain how people in different cultures and languages express themselves, and I can adjust how I communicate when talking with diverse people.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize and appreciate that people in my school and community speak different languages.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize that people may speak differently from me with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write all letters in own first name.
I can use a standard pencil, student writes own first name.
I can use a keyboard, student writes own name
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write first letter of own first name.
I can use a standard pencil, student writes first letter of own first name.
I can use a keyboard, student writes first letter of own name.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can demonstrate emerging understandings of letter writing.
I can write letter-like shapes (a series of disconnected circles) top to bottom and/or left to right of page when writing a story or a note.
I can select letters from a keyboard, eye gaze chart, or using partner-assisted scanning without apparent connection to own name.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, explore writing using a pen/pencil or access to the full alphabet.
I can use a keyboard to write and randomly select keys including letters, punctuation, and other characters.
I can make marks with pens, pencils, markers, etc.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can share and compare how words are said in different languages in my class.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can recognize and appreciate that people in my school and community speak different languages.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name a language someone in my class speaks with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can notice that people speak in different ways with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can notice that people around me use different languages.

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. a. Use inflexional forms as clues to the meaning of unknown words (e.g., looks, looked).
ee_text: Demonstrate emerging knowledge of word meanings. a. Demonstrate understanding of words used in every day routines.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use clues from word endings like "-s" or "-ed" to figure out what unfamiliar words mean in different sentences and explain how their meanings change.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use word endings like "-s" or "-ed" to figure out what unfamiliar words mean.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use word endings to help me figure out new words with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can figure out the meaning of a new word if someone helps me.
I can use parts of a word I know to help me understand it with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can locate first letter in own name when presented with name.
I can identify first letter of name (e.g., Given her name, point to or identify through partner-assisted scanning the “S” in “Sarah”.).
I can point to first letter of own name in environment (e.g., When walking down the hall, the student points to first letter of own name on a bulletin board and says own name (e.g., Jasmine sees the letter “J” on a bulletin board, points to it and says, “Jasmine.”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can locate first letter in own name when presented with name.
I can point to first letter of name when name is presented (e.g., When presented with his name printed on a sentence strip, the student can point to the first letter.).
I can locate first letter of own name in Braille (e.g., When presented with name in Braille, the child locates the beginning of the word and points to the first letter.).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to own name when called.
I can turn to look at the speaker when his or her name is called.
I can smile in response to someone calling own name.
I can get visibly excited when teacher signs my name to indicate it is my turn.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words. I know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams. descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes distinguish between long and short vowels when reading simple one-syllable words. descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some vowel sounds in simple one-syllable words, but I struggle to distinguish between long and short vowels. I have limited knowledge of spelling-sound correspondences for common vowel teams, and I have difficulty decoding and encoding regularly spelled one, two, and three syllable CVC pattern words.

subject: ELA
cluster: Phonics & Word Recognition
text: Recognize and read grade- appropriate irregularly spelled words.
ee_text: Demonstrate emerging use of letter-sound knowledge to read words. f. Recognize 10 or more written words.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can confidently recognize and read a wide range of grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words. I can apply my knowledge of these words to fluently read and comprehend more complex texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize and read some grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words with support, but my knowledge is limited.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some common sight words, but I struggle to recognize and read most grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recognize 10 or more written words.
I can when asked, reads 10 or more words on the classroom word wall (can point to words as they teacher calls them or reads them orally).
I can when given a list of familiar consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words, successfully reads 10 or more words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize two or more written words.
I can point to the correct word when read by someone else.
I can match written word to an object.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize symbols that represent two or more common words.
I can recognize symbols that are part of the daily schedule.
I can recognize symbols that represent lunch item choices.

subject: ELA
cluster: Fluency
text: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension. a. Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
ee_text: Attend to words in print. a. Read familiartext comprised of known words.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fluently read a wide range of grade-level texts with a deep level of purpose and understanding. My oral reading is consistently accurate, with an appropriate rate and expressive delivery. I can seamlessly use context to quickly confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, and I rarely need to reread.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can read grade-level text with purpose and understanding. I can read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings. I can use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read some grade-level texts with basic purpose and understanding. My oral reading is somewhat accurate, with an appropriate rate and some expression. I can sometimes use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, but I may need to reread frequently.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read some simple grade-level texts, but I often lack purpose and understanding. My oral reading is inaccurate and lacks appropriate rate and expression. I struggle to use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recognize 10 or more written words.
I can when asked, reads 10 or more words on the classroom word wall (can point to words as they teacher calls them or reads them orally).
I can when given a list of familiar consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words, successfully reads 10 or more words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize two or more written words.
I can point to the correct word when read by someone else.
I can match written word to an object.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize symbols that represent two or more common words.
I can recognize symbols that are part of the daily schedule.
I can recognize symbols that represent lunch item choices.

subject: ELA
cluster: Fluency
text: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
ee_text: Not applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read a text aloud smoothly, with the right speed and expression, without help.
I can improve my fluency each time I reread a text, sounding more like natural speech.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level text aloud with good speed and expression.
I can read a text more accurately and with better expression when I practice reading it again.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read aloud with some expression and at a good speed with guidance.
I can read better and more smoothly after practicing a text several times.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can read aloud with help and improve my reading speed when someone supports me.
I can practice reading a text and get better each time with guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

subject: ELA
cluster: Fluency
text: Use context to confirm or self- correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
ee_text: With support, monitor for and identify errors that disrupt comprehension

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use the context in a sentence to figure out or correct difficult words without help.
I can reread parts of a text on my own to understand and correct my reading mistakes.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use context clues to figure out or fix a word when reading.
I can reread parts of a text to help me understand words and meaning.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use clues from the text to help me understand or fix words when someone guides me.
I can reread parts of a text with help to make sure I understand it.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use help to understand or fix a word I don’t know while reading.
I can reread parts of a story or text when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recognize when I make a mistake while reading and fix it with help.
I can check if what I read makes sense and ask for help if I don’t understand.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can notice when something I read doesn’t sound right and ask for help.
I can correct a mistake in reading with guidance when someone helps me notice it.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can stop when I don’t understand something while reading and ask for help with support.
I can recognize when a word I read doesn’t match the story with guidance.

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Develop and answer questions to demonstrate an understanding of key ideas and details in a text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: hen given guidance and support, answer “who”, “what” and “where” questions in familiar texts. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently and thoughtfully develop a range of questions to deeply explore and demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of key ideas and details in a text. I can analyze important information, explain the central message or theme, and make insightful connections, inferences, and intertextual links.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and answer questions to demonstrate an understanding of key ideas and details in a text. I can identify important information, explain the main message or events, and make relevant connections.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can develop and answer some basic questions about key ideas and details in a text, but my understanding is limited. I can identify a few important details, but I have trouble explaining the main message or events.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty developing and answering questions to demonstrate an understanding of key ideas and details in a text. I struggle to identify important information and understand the main message or events.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can answer who and what questions to demonstrate understanding of details in a familiar text.
I can when given a set of familiar directions, answer questions about who follows the directions and what is one thing to do to complete the task.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can answer what questions to demonstrate understanding of details in a text.
I can when given the instructions for a model plane/car, birdhouse, or other craft project, identify what would happen if they did not use glue (or another key ingredient).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and supports, identify a detail in a text or illustration.
I can Shown a calendar, point to any date.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Summarize portions of a text in order to identify a main topic or central idea and key details in a text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify the topic of a text (RI) and use details to recount events from familiar stories (RL).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and coherently summarize portions of a text, accurately identifying the main topic or central idea and carefully selecting and explaining the most salient supporting details. My summaries demonstrate a deep comprehension of the text and an ability to discern the most important information.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can summarize portions of a text in order to identify a main topic or central idea and key details in a text. I can concisely capture the essential information and explain how the details support the main idea.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can summarize some portions of a text, but I have trouble consistently identifying the main topic or central idea and the most important supporting details. My summaries may be incomplete or lack focus.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to summarize portions of a text in order to identify the main topic or central idea and key details. I have difficulty distinguishing important information from less relevant details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the topic of the text.
I can From three options, identify the topic of a series of directions (e.g., Would the title be Making a Cake, Building a Birdhouse, or Riding the Bus?).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can retell the title of a text.
I can after reading the title and steps for a series of directions, repeat the title.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can indicate a portion of a text.
I can when given a set of directions, point to any step or the title.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Describe how characters respond to major events and challenges. (RL) Describe the connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events. (RI)
ee_text: Identify the actions of characters (RL) or important details and events (RI) in familiar and unfamiliar texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can thoroughly and insightfully describe how characters respond to major events and challenges, analyzing their motivations, emotions, and character development.
I can expertly describe complex connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events in an informational text, demonstrating a deep comprehension of the relationships and their significance.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can describe how characters respond to major events and challenges in a story, explaining their motivations and reactions.
I can describe the connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events in an informational text.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can describe how characters respond to some major events and challenges, but my explanations may be incomplete or lack depth.
I can identify and describe some connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events in an informational text, but my understanding is still developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I have difficulty describing how characters respond to major events and challenges in a story. I struggle to identify the characters' motivations and reactions.
I can identify some basic connections between ideas, concepts, or events in an informational text, but I have trouble explaining the relationships in detail.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the actions and feelings of the characters in a familiar story.
I can during shared reading sessions, share with peers how characters feel in a familiar story? “How does the pig feel when the wolf says, ‘I will huff and puff and blow your house down?’”
I can during shared reading sessions, will share with peers what characters did and how that made them feel (e.g., “How did the wolf get into the brick house and how did that make the pig feel?”).
I can when given an array of symbols, selects a symbol that reflects the characters’ feelings on each page of a familiar story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with prompting, identify the actions and feeling of characters in a familiar story.
I can With prompting during shared reading of a familiar story, tell what characters are doing on each page.
I can with prompting during shared reading of a familiar story, act out feelings or actions of the characters in the story.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with prompting, identify a character in a familiar story.
I can when given an array of pictures of characters from the book and classmates, chooses a picture of the character in the story.
I can With prompting during shared reading of a familiar story, use a two location voice output device programmed with happy and sad to label the feelings of characters in the story.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Explain how specific words and phrases express feelings, appeal to the senses, or determine the meaning of content-specific words within a text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Use a text’s structure (e.g., repetition, rhyming, etc.) to identify specific content, sensory, or feeling words that meaningfully relate to the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully explain how the author's strategic use of specific words and phrases in a text express complex emotions, vividly appeal to the senses, and provide essential context for understanding content-specific vocabulary. I can make sophisticated connections between the language use and the text's meaning, tone, and effect on the reader
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how specific words and phrases in a text express feelings, appeal to the senses, or determine the meaning of content-specific words. I can analyze the impact of the author's language choices on the reader's understanding and experience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some ways that specific words and phrases in a text express feelings, appeal to the senses, or provide context for understanding content-specific vocabulary, but my explanations are basic and lack depth.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty explaining how specific words and phrases in a text express feelings, appeal to the senses, or determine the meaning of content-specific vocabulary. I struggle to analyze the impact of language on the reader's understanding.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify words that describe feelings or senses in a text that uses rhyming or repetition.
I can find important words that help me understand a story’s structure, like repeated or rhyming words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize rhyming or repeating words in a story with help.
I can find one word that shows a feeling or idea in a text with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can listen for a word that sounds the same or repeats in a story with support.
I can point to or say a word that describes something I hear or feel in the text with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Describe the overall structure of a text, including describing how the beginning introduces the text and the ending concludes the text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify the beginning and end of a familiar sequential text (RL) or identify relevant graphics in an informational text (RI).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully describe the complex structure of a text, expertly explaining how the beginning effectively introduces the topic, theme, or narrative, and the ending powerfully concludes it. I can analyze the author's strategic use of organizational elements and their impact on the text's meaning and impact.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe the overall structure of a text, including how the beginning introduces the text and the ending concludes it. I can analyze the purpose and effectiveness of the text's organizational choices.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic elements of a text's structure, but I have trouble fully explaining how the beginning introduces the text and the ending concludes it. My understanding of the text's organization is still developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty describing the overall structure of a text, including how the beginning and ending sections function. I struggle to identify key organizational features and the connections between different parts of the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell where a story begins and ends in a book I know.
I can find pictures or graphics that give important information in an informational text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can show where a story starts or finishes with help.
I can find one important graphic in an informational text with some guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to the first or last part of a story with support.
I can point to a picture or graphic that goes with a story or information with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: I can identify examples of how illustrations, text features, and details support the point of view or purpose of the text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: With guidance and support, identify words and graphic representations that connect to the point of view, topic, or important details of the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully identify a wide range of examples demonstrating how the strategic use of illustrations, text features, and details powerfully support and enhance the point of view or purpose of a text. I can make sophisticated connections between the visual and textual elements, and analyze their collective impact on the reader's understanding and experience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify multiple examples of how illustrations, text features, and details support the point of view or purpose of a text. I can explain how these elements contribute to the overall meaning and effectiveness of the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some basic examples of how illustrations, text features, and details relate to the point of view or purpose of a text, but my understanding is still developing. I may not be able to fully explain the connections or their significance.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty identifying examples of how illustrations, text features, and details support the point of view or purpose of a text. I struggle to make connections between the visual and textual elements and the overall meaning or message.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can find words or pictures in a text that show the main idea or a character’s point of view.
I can identify words and images that are important to understanding the story or topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find one word or picture that shows how a character feels or what the story is about with help.
I can recognize one important word or image in the text with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to a picture or say a word that shows what the story or topic is about with support.
I can identify a word or picture related to the main idea with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Demonstrate understanding of story elements and/or topics by applying information gained from illustrations or text features. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify illustrations or objects/tactile information in text that depict characters. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully demonstrate a deep understanding of complex story elements and/or topics by expertly applying a wide range of detailed information gained from the strategic use of illustrations and text features. I can make sophisticated, nuanced connections that enhance my interpretation and analysis of the text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can demonstrate a clear understanding of story elements and/or topics by effectively applying relevant information gained from illustrations and text features. I can make thoughtful connections between the visual/textual details and my overall comprehension of the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can demonstrate a basic understanding of some story elements or topics by applying information gained from illustrations or text features, but my connections may be limited or lack depth
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty demonstrating understanding of story elements or topics by using information from illustrations or text features. I struggle to connect visual and textual details to my overall comprehension of the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use illustrations in print or digital text to identify characters and settings.
I can when given three illustrations, select the one that depicts the setting in the story.
I can find an illustration in the book that shows a specified character.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find the character in an illustration from a familiar text.
I can during shared reading of a familiar text when the teacher stops at a page with an illustration that includes a specified character, point to the character.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can attend to illustrations in the text during shared reading.
I can visually attend to the illustration when the teacher holds up the book for the student to see.
I can visually attend to the book during shared reading.

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Explain how specific points the author or illustrator makes in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. (RI)
ee_text: Identify points the author makes in text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully explain how the author's or illustrator's specific, complex points in an informational text are powerfully supported by a rich array of relevant, well-chosen reasons and evidence. I can make sophisticated, nuanced connections that demonstrate a deep understanding of the author's or illustrator's purpose and the impact of the supporting information.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can clearly explain how the specific points made by the author or illustrator in an informational text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. I can analyze the purpose and effectiveness of the supporting information in strengthening the author's or illustrator's claims.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some basic connections between the specific points made by the author or illustrator and the supporting reasons and evidence, but my explanations are limited. I may not fully understand the purpose or significance of the supporting details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty explaining how the specific points made by the author or illustrator in an informational text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. I struggle to identify and analyze the connections between the claims and the supporting information.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell one or two important points the author makes in a text.
I can explain what the author wants me to know about the topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or point to one important point the author makes with guidance.
I can recognize one key idea the author gives in the text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond when asked about an important point the author makes with support.
I can point to or say one thing the author talks about with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Compare and contrast key points or perspectives presented in two texts; recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Compare details in two texts; recognize that texts reflect one’s own and other’s culture. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully compare and contrast the complex, nuanced key points and perspectives presented in two texts. I can make sophisticated, well-supported connections between the texts and their reflections of one's own and others' cultures, demonstrating a deep understanding of how cultural influences shape the content and portrayal of information and narratives.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively compare and contrast the key points or perspectives presented in two texts. I can also recognize how the texts may reflect the author's or characters' cultural backgrounds and experiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some basic similarities and differences between the key points or perspectives in two texts, but my comparisons are limited. I may not fully understand how texts can reflect cultural influences.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty comparing and contrasting the key points or perspectives presented in two texts. I also struggle to recognize that texts can reflect one's own and others' cultures.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell how details from two texts are the same or different.
I can explain how stories reflect different cultures, including my own.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find one detail that is the same or different in two stories with help.
I can recognize one thing that shows a story is from a different culture with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say something that is the same or different in two stories with support.
I can use pictures or words to show something about a story from another culture with help.

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can expertly compose sophisticated, nuanced examples of reflective, formal, and creative writing that seamlessly address a wide array of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes. I can fluidly integrate these various modes of writing and demonstrate a deep understanding of how to strategically compose for different objectives and audiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compose reflective, formal, and creative writing that serves a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes. I can effectively address the appropriate objectives and integrate these different modes of writing as needed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compose some basic examples of reflective, formal, and creative writing, but my ability to do so for a range of purposes is limited. I may have difficulty balancing high-stakes and low-stakes objectives in my writing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty composing reflective, formal, and creative writing for a variety of purposes. I struggle to produce writing that effectively addresses high-stakes or low-stakes objectives.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a book and write, draw, or dictate to state an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, use a multiple message communication device to say, “good book” and then add a reason, “funny.”
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, draw a picture of a sad face to show that he or she doesn’t like it and then ask the teacher to write “too hard” under the picture.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a book and write, draw, or dictate to state an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, then the teacher will navigate through the student’s multiple message communication device to reveal messages that express an opinion, then select a message communicating an opinion (e.g., “It’s really good!”). The teacher asks, “What makes it good?,” and the student will use the device to answer (e.g., says “boy”) which the teacher interprets to mean the student liked the main character who was a boy.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, state an opinion about a book.
I can look at, touch, or take a book from a selection of two when the teacher asks, “Show me your favorite,” which the teacher writes (e.g., Maria’s favorite is Goodnight Moon.).
I can after the media specialist shows the students two books they might want to check out, look at one of them and indicate a preference (e.g., smiles).

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or text they are writing about; state an opinion; supply reasons that support the opinion using words for emphasis, addition, contrast, or order to connect opinion and reasons; and provide a concluding statement or section.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion about a topic or text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write sophisticated, nuanced examples of opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives, expertly using the required elements and structure for each mode. My writing demonstrates a thorough understanding of how to effectively introduce topics/texts, state opinions with well-chosen supporting reasons, use facts and details to develop points, and provide meaningful, cohesive conclusions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write proficient examples of opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives, incorporating the necessary elements and structure for each mode. My writing introduces topics/texts, states opinions with supporting reasons, uses facts and details to develop points, and provides appropriate conclusions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write some basic examples of opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives, but my ability to effectively use the required elements and structure for each mode is limited. My writing may lack cohesion or development.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to write text in a variety of modes, including opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives. I have difficulty introducing topics, stating opinions, using supporting reasons and details, and providing appropriate conclusions.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a topic and use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose a message with one fact about the topic.
I can select a topic based on a bulletin board in the classroom about life cycles, then draw a picture of a frog, tell a peer to write frog next to the picture or add a picture of a tadpole and writes tp.
I can look through a photo album parents have sent in from home and select a picture of the beach and then dictate a fact about the picture for the teacher to write: “The beach is hot.” or “The beach has water.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic and use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose a message with one fact about a topic.
I can when given a familiar topic such as a favorite TV show, draw a picture of a character in the show and complete a frame sentence using a word bank: “<Name of character> is <one fact>.” (e.g., “Barney is purple.” or “Barney is happy.”).
I can when given a topic from a recently completed classroom activity, within a small group tell the teacher one thing that happened during the activity as the teacher writes a repeated line of text, One thing we did was . . . . Another thing we did was . . . . We also did . . . .
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic.
I can Working with a group of peers, select the topic each peer will write about from a choice of two or more.
I can Select the topic for a shared writing activity from two or more choices offered by the teacher.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Informative or explanatory text in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.
ee_text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they provide at least 1 fact about a predetermined or self chosen topic
