I can independently write an informative text that introduces a topic, uses clear facts, and ends with a strong conclusion.
I can connect facts and definitions in my writing to fully explain a topic.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write an informative text that introduces a topic, uses facts, and provides a clear conclusion.
I can use definitions and facts to explain the points I make in my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write a simple informative text with some facts and a conclusion, with help.
I can try to include facts and definitions in my writing, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can introduce a topic and include one fact in my writing, with help.
I can add a sentence to finish my writing when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or say one fact about a topic I know.
I can give one important piece of information about a chosen topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can give a simple fact about a topic with help.
I can say one thing I know about a topic with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say a word about a topic I know with support.
I can share information using pictures or words with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Convey events, real or imagined, through narratives in which they recount a well elaborated event or short sequence of events; include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings; and use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.
ee_text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write a detailed narrative that describes actions, thoughts, and feelings, using temporal words to clearly order events and bring the story to a satisfying close.
I can write a story with rich details that show how characters feel and what they are thinking.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write a narrative with details that describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, using temporal words like "first" and "then" to order events and provide a conclusion.
I can tell a story that shows what characters are doing and feeling.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write about a sequence of events using some details and temporal words like "next" and "after," with help.
I can try to describe what characters do or feel in my story with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about one or two events in order using simple words like "first" or "then," with help.
I can try to describe what happened in my story with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or talk about something that happened, including details about what happened.
I can tell a story about one event or several events that are linked together.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or write about one event from a story or my own experience with some help.
I can share a few details about what happened with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to a picture or say a word about something that happened with support.
I can use pictures or words to show what happened in one part of a story with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Provide a beginning, middle and ending that works cohesively to promote the central theme of the text.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses words familiar to the student and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create sophisticated, nuanced writing that expertly organizes a complex, central theme with a seamlessly cohesive beginning, middle, and ending. I use a variety of well-chosen transitions to build strong, sophisticated connections between ideas and events. I demonstrate a command of descriptive, domain-specific vocabulary to provide rich, vivid examples that enhance the overall effectiveness of the writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create writing that effectively organizes a central theme with a cohesive beginning, middle, and ending. I use transitions to link ideas and events, and incorporate descriptive, domain-specific vocabulary to provide vivid details and examples.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can create some basic writing that attempts to organize a central theme and use transitions and descriptive vocabulary, but my execution is limited. My writing may lack cohesion or fully developed ideas, details, and connections.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to create writing that effectively organizes a central theme with a cohesive beginning, middle, and ending. I also have difficulty using transitions to connect ideas and events, and incorporating descriptive, domain-specific vocabulary to provide vivid details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select an event or personal experience and use drawing, writing, or dictating to compose a message about it.
I can draw a picture about his or her brother’s soccer game, asks the teacher to write his or her brother’s name, and then signs own name to the picture.
I can look through digital photos that the teacher took while the children completed a class project, select a photo and dictate a message for the teacher to write.
I can following an in-class cooking experience, name the activity (e.g., “Mkg Ckes” [Making Cookies]), describing what was done (e.g., “Mak sgr ckz” [We make sugar cookies.]), describing how it felt (e.g., “Do stke” [The dough was sticky.]), and telling how they liked it (e.g., “Likem.” [I liked them.]).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can draw, write, or dictate to compose a message about a personal experience.
I can tell the teacher about a trip to the pet shop and draw a picture of it when asked.
I can when the teacher displays a picture of the student working with peers to complete a class project, dictate a message to go with it.
I can following an in-class cooking experience, use a teacher-provided template to name the activity (e.g., “Mkg Ckez” [Making Cookies]), and tell how they liked it (e.g., “Likem.” [I liked them.]).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate about a personal experience.
I can after the teacher talked with the student about going to an activity (e.g., his or her brother’s soccer game) and asks, “Was it good?” The student indicates answer (e.g., indicate no by looking down) and the teacher writes in the student’s journal (e.g., Tamika went to her brother’s soccer game. It was not fun.).
I can after the teacher works with the student to review the events in his or her schedule for the day, points to and labels each of the visual supports, and asks, “Did you do it?” The student indicates an answer (e.g., indicate yes by smiling), and the teacher writes Brian did art, in his home-school journal.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Transitions: use transitions to link and build connections between ideas, text, and events.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use a variety of transitions to smoothly connect ideas and events in my writing.
I can choose transitions that make my writing flow naturally and clearly.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use transitions like "because," "then," and "next" to connect ideas and events in my writing.
I can make my writing flow better by using simple transitions.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use basic transitions like "and" or "then" to link ideas and events, with some support.
I can try to connect events in my writing with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use simple words like "and" or "next" to connect ideas in my writing, with help.
I can try to link two ideas in my writing with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Word Choice (including domain specific): use descriptive words to demonstrate creativity and to providevivid examples of feelings, events, and images.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use creative and descriptive words to vividly describe characters’ feelings, actions, and settings in my writing.
I can paint a clear picture with words to help readers imagine the events in my story.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use descriptive words to show how characters feel or what is happening in my writing.
I can describe events and images in my story using words that help readers understand.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use a few descriptive words to describe characters’ feelings or actions, with some support.
I can try to use words that make my story clearer with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can try to use simple words to describe how someone feels or what happens in my writing, with help.
I can name feelings or describe an event in basic terms with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: I can with guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task and purpose. (Grade- specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)
ee_text: (Begins in grade 3)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write about a topic in a way that reflects my culture and is authentic to the task, without help.
I can organize and develop my writing to show who I am and what is important to me.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write about a topic that shows my culture or experiences, and organize my ideas clearly, with some guidance.
I can make sure my writing matches the task and purpose with help.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write about something important to me, and with support, make sure it fits the task and purpose.
I can try to organize my writing and include details about my experiences with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about my ideas or culture with help, and organize my writing with support from an adult.
I can get help to make my writing match the task or purpose, while sharing something about my experiences.
descriptors.ee_at_target: (Begins in grade 3)

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, focus their own drawing, dictation, or writing on a topic and add more details to strengthen their drawing, dictation, or writing as needed.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can with minimal guidance and support, I can independently focus on a topic and masterfully strengthen my writing through sophisticated revision and editing. I demonstrate a deep understanding of the revision and editing process, and can make strategic, well-informed decisions to significantly improve the focus, organization, content, and mechanics of my writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, I can focus on a topic and successfully strengthen my writing by revising and editing as needed. I am able to make meaningful improvements to the focus, organization, content, and mechanics of my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can focus on a topic and make some attempts to revise and edit my writing, but I require significant guidance and support from adults and peers to do so effectively. My revisions and edits may be limited in scope or impact.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty focusing on a topic and strengthening my writing through the revision and editing process, even with guidance and support from adults and peers.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more information to own drawing, dictating, or writing to strengthen the message.
I can add information created in science center and add information with peer assistance (e.g., The student shares a picture he or she has drawn of the leaves in a science center with some peers. The peers point out details on the leaves and suggest that the student adds the details to the picture and he or she does.).
I can dictate a sentence for the teacher to write. when the teacher asks for clarification (e.g., “Tell me when that happened.”), dictates more to clarify.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults or peers, add more information to own drawing, dictating, or writing when asked.
I can add information to drawing with peer assistance (e.g., The student shares a picture he or she has drawn with some peers when they make suggestions that he or she add more and the student adds more random marks to the picture.).
I can dictate a sentence for the teacher to write. when the teacher asks, “Tell me more,” adds more.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults or peers, use drawing, communication, or writing tools to communicate a message.
I can use a single message voice output device to tell a peer, “Read it to me.” while students are sharing group writing and when invited to contribute his ideas, makes marks on the paper.
I can use a computer-based paint program to draw about a favored activity.
I can select keys on an alternate keyboard to write a note to a friend.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: I can with guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing (including forming most printed upper- and lower-case letters), cursive, or typing.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology (including assistive technologies) to produce and publish writing. Learn to produce writing through printing (including forming upper and lower case letters).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can with minimal guidance, I can independently and skillfully use a wide range of digital tools to produce and publish sophisticated, collaborative writing. I have mastered producing writing through printing, cursive, and typing, and can fluidly switch between these methods as needed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can with guidance and support from adults, I can use a variety of digital tools to effectively produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. I have learned to produce writing through printing, cursive, and typing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With some guidance and support from adults, I can use a limited range of digital tools to produce and publish basic writing, sometimes in collaboration with peers. My ability to consistently produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing is developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to use digital tools to produce and publish writing, even with guidance and support from adults. I also have difficulty learning to produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology (including assistive technologies) to produce and publish writing.
I can use an alternative keyboard preprogrammed by the teacher with words and phrases to write a response to a book to publish in the class’ book of book reviews.
I can work with a peer to choose words from word banks and spell words to write about himself or herself for inclusion in a class book, when We Were Babies.
I can with guidance and support, use assistive technology to write back and forth with a parent volunteer in a digital written conversation environment (e.g., e-mail, text message).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology to produce writing.
I can work with a peer, use an alternative keyboard preprogrammed by the teacher with words and phrases to write about a book.
I can work with a peer to choose words from word banks and spell words to write about himself or herself.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, explore writing technologies.
I can take turns selecting preprogrammed messages from an alternative keyboard and listen as the message is read/typed by a talking word processing program.
I can use a single switch with scanning to select letters of the alphabet on an onscreen keyboard.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Participate in shared and independent inquiry and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).
ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in shared and independent inquiry and writing projects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can eagerly participate in complex, sophisticated shared and independent inquiry and writing projects. I can thoroughly research multiple sources, meticulously record detailed observations, and skillfully synthesize the information to produce an exceptional, cohesive written piece.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can actively participate in shared and independent inquiry and writing projects. I can read multiple sources on a topic, record relevant observations, and use the information to produce a well-organized report or other written product.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can participate in some basic shared and independent inquiry and writing projects, but my participation is limited. I may have trouble reading multiple sources, organizing information, and producing a cohesive written piece.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to participate in shared or independent inquiry and writing projects. I have difficulty reading multiple sources on a topic, recording observations, and using the information to produce a report or other written product.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can participate in shared writing projects - communicate a message to add information.
I can select a book on a topic related to a shared research project from a collection identified by peers and identify pictures that relate to the topic being researched, share them, and have peers write and read aloud text to accompany them.
I can read and listen with a peer to two electronic books selected by the teacher in a digital reading environment and with a keyboard with alphabet and whole word access type letters, words, or sentences about what they learn (e.g., Katz r mamls. Bab catz r kitns. [Cats are mammals. Baby cats are kittens.]).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, participate in shared writing and research projects.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher, select a book from a choice of two related to the shared research project and identifies pictures that relate to the topic being researched which a peer writes on the collaborative document and reads aloud.
I can when given a premade set-up on an alternative keyboard or onscreen keyboard, select words and pictures to add to a shared research and writing project.
I can type letters as they are dictated by a peer to add content to a shared writing project and then dictate known letters to a peer to type in order to add content to a shared writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select pictures, words, or objects related to a shared research project.
I can when given a multimedia presentation of words and pictures related to a shared research project, use a switch to advance through the pictures looking and/or listening to the words and pictures and select one, which a peer, aide, or teacher will write in the shared research project.
I can use a touchscreen to scroll through pictures related to the topic of a shared research project and select one, which a peer, aide, or teacher will write in the shared research project and read aloud.
I can explore a bin full of objects and artifacts related to a shared research project and select one, which a peer, aide, or teacher will write in the shared research project.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
ee_text: Identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fluently and comprehensively recall detailed information from a wide range of personal experiences, and expertly gather and synthesize information from multiple provided sources to answer complex questions in-depth.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively recall information from my own experiences and gather relevant information from provided sources to answer questions thoroughly and accurately.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can partially recall information from experiences or gather some information from provided sources to answer basic questions, but my responses may be limited in detail or depth.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty recalling information from my own experiences or gathering information from provided sources to answer questions. My responses are often incomplete or inaccurate.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can identify from a list of things that happened on a field trip to answer questions (e.g., The teacher gives small groups of children a list of questions to answer about a field trip, peers read the questions one-at-a-time, make a list of what they remember, ask the student to identify which things he or she remembers, and then use that information to answer the questions.).
I can after the teacher prepares a set-up on an interactive whiteboard for students to use in recoding their experiences from a science project, identify the pictures that reflect what happened and then move them to the correct location to respond to the teacher’s questions.
I can use a picture/label schedule to recall the activities of the day and answer the question, “What did you do today?” for their parents in the home/school journal.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can work with the teacher, select a book purchased at a recent book fair so the teacher can write down the name and then answer the teacher’s question when she asked, “Do you like the book?” Then, place a check in the like column.
I can work with a small group and the teacher, identify supplies from those assembled on the table that were used in completing a group project (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, paper) so the teacher can add them to the list and then respond to the teacher’s question when she asks, “Did you finish?”
I can use a picture/label schedule to identify the next activity of the day by answering what questions (e.g., What is after math? What is next? What is first today?).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and preferences.
I can work with the teacher, identify a picture of a center completed earlier in the day to answer yes or no to the question, “Did you <listen to a story> this morning?” after which, the teacher will write in the home-school journal, “Allison listened to a story this morning.”
I can work with a small group of peers and the teacher, identify objects and artifacts from a personal experience that will then be labeled appropriately by the teacher (e.g., Science things: rocks, leaves, twigs).

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, recall and use facts from literary and informational text to support reflection and inquiry on characters, setting, key details, specified information, and ideas presented in a text.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently and skillfully recall and use a wide range of relevant facts from literary and informational texts to engage in deep, sophisticated reflection and inquiry about complex characters, settings, key details, specified information, and central ideas. I demonstrate a nuanced understanding of the texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, I can effectively recall and use relevant facts from literary and informational texts to thoughtfully reflect on and inquire about characters, settings, key details, specified information, and central ideas presented in the texts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With some guidance and support, I can partially recall and use a few relevant facts from literary and informational texts to reflect on and inquire about basic elements like characters, settings, and key details. However, my responses may be limited in depth and scope.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to recall and use facts from literary and informational texts, even with guidance and support from adults and peers. I have difficulty reflecting on and inquiring about characters, settings, key details, and ideas presented in texts.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can remember and tell important details from a story or informational text.
I can explain key information from a text with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say one important thing I remember from a text with support.
I can recall one detail from a story or informational text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures or words to show something I remember from a text with support.
I can point to something in the book that helps me remember details with guidance.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups. a. Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions and participate by actively listening, taking turns, gaining the floor in respectful ways, and staying on topic.
ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in conversations with adults and peers. a. Engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers with support from an adult.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I consistently and skillfully participate in substantive, collaborative conversations with a wide range of diverse partners. I take a leading role in discussions about complex topics and texts, seamlessly engaging with both small groups and larger audiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can actively participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about a variety of topics and texts, both in small groups and larger settings. I engage thoughtfully with my peers and adults.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With some support, I can participate in basic collaborative conversations about topics and texts, but my participation may be limited or uneven. I can engage with a few diverse partners in small groups, but have more difficulty in larger group settings.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty participating in collaborative conversations, even with guidance and support. I struggle to engage with diverse partners about topics and texts in both small and larger group settings.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers and adults in small groups.
I can after shared reading of a fable in a small group, take turns talking about the fable with the teacher’s involvement.
I can during lunchtime, communicate about the weekend taking multiple turns with peers and adults who are sitting at the table.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with individual peers.
I can while at a literacy center working with letters and words when a peer hands the student a letter and says, “You need this one?,” and the student replies, “No, b!” The peer finds a letter b and says, “This one?” The student replies, “Yeah, b.”
I can when the snack helper asks, “What do you want?” and holds up the white milk and chocolate milk, look directly at the chocolate milk. The peer acknowledges, “Okay, chocolate.” and the student uses sign language to say, “Thank you.” The peer replies, “You’re welcome.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can communicate directly with an adult.
I can select from an array of pictures to indicate a favorite character in a story.
I can look at the carton of chocolate milk when a teacher holds up a carton of white milk and a carton of chocolate milk and asks, “What do you want?”
I can hand a teacher a picture of a desired toy to request an object during center time.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.
ee_text: Build on others’ talk in conversations

descriptors.cc_advanced: I masterfully build on the talk of others in conversations, seamlessly linking my comments to the evolving discussion in a way that advances the dialogue and demonstrates a deep understanding of my conversation partners' remarks.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively build on the talk of others in conversations by thoughtfully connecting my comments to the previous remarks made by my conversation partners.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes build on the talk of others in conversations, but I may have trouble consistently linking my comments to the previous remarks made. My contributions may be limited or lack cohesion.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty building on the comments of others during conversations. I struggle to make connections between my own remarks and the previous statements made by my conversation partners.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can add my own ideas when someone else is talking in a conversation.
I can respond to others and continue a conversation with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can add a comment or ask a question when someone else is talking with some help.
I can share my thoughts after listening to someone else with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to others using gestures or words during a conversation with help.
I can show I am listening and add a simple comment with guidance.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.
ee_text: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I confidently and proactively ask thoughtful, targeted questions to get clarification and deeper explanation about the complex topics and texts under discussion, showing a strong desire to fully comprehend the subject matter.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I appropriately ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts being discussed, in order to deepen my understanding.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I sometimes ask for clarification or further explanation about the topics and texts under discussion, but I may not do so consistently or with enough specificity to get the information I need.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I rarely ask for clarification or further explanation about the topics and texts being discussed, even when I am unsure or need more information.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask questions related to a prescribed topic or text.
I can during shared reading of a fable, ask “What is that?” (pointing to the tortoise).
I can use a multiple message voice output device to ask, “Who?” when the teacher explains that the class will have a special visitor coming to class today.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, ask questions related to a prescribed topic or text.
I can when given a choice of two questions recorded on single message voice output device (e.g., “What happens next?” and “”Why did she do that?”) and support from the teacher who models by saying, “I wonder what will happen next.” or “I wonder why she did that.,” select a question to ask.
I can ask, “How are you today?” during morning group, after several students have asked the question, “How are you today?”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use question words (who, what, when, where, why, or how) to communicate with others.
I can when given a single message voice output device with the single word, why during a shared reading activity with an informational text, hit the switch to say “why?”
I can during morning meeting time when the teacher is explaining the calendar to the group, she exaggerates when asking, “Do you know what we’re going to do then?,” the student hits a single message voice output device to say, “What?”

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.
ee_text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I seamlessly integrate consideration of individual differences into all of my communications. I expertly tailor my style, content, and approach to effectively engage with a wide range of individuals, showing a nuanced understanding of diverse perspectives and communication needs.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I consistently consider individual differences when communicating with others. I demonstrate sensitivity to diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and communication needs, and I adjust my approach accordingly.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can somewhat consider individual differences when communicating, but my awareness and application of this skill is limited. I may occasionally adjust my communication style or content, but not consistently.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty considering individual differences when communicating with others. My interactions may lack sensitivity or awareness of others' perspectives, backgrounds, and communication needs.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can communicate with others while being respectful of their differences.
I can change how I talk to others depending on their needs or feelings.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can think about how others feel when I talk to them with guidance.
I can communicate with others, thinking about their feelings, with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to others using gestures or words while showing care for their feelings with support.
I can show respect when communicating with others with guidance.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
ee_text: Demonstrate an emerging understanding of a familiar text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by answering questions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fluently and comprehensively recount or describe the nuanced, complex key ideas and rich details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media, demonstrating a thorough understanding.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively recount or describe the key ideas and important details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can partially recount or describe some key ideas or details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media, but my recounts may be limited in scope or miss important information.

descriptors.ee_approaching:

descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, answer questions about a text read aloud or information presented through other media.

descriptors.ee_emerging:

I can identify some parts of stories, like the beginning and the end.
I can identify some text features, like pictures and headings.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine the beginning, middle, and end of a story.
I can use picture clues to identify an event that occurred in the beginning, middle, or end of the story.
I can use a story map, fill in the beginning and end of the story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify the beginning or ending of a story.
I can use picture clues to identify the beginning of a story.
I can when given a story map with the beginning and middle completed, identify the ending.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify one event from a story.
I can when given an array of pictures, choose one that matches something that happened in the story.
I can answering yes or no questions to respond, indicate whether an event was in the story.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
text: Discuss how the reader’s point of view or perspective may differ from that of the author, narrator, or characters in a text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify personal point of view about a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author uses different techniques to convey different perspectives within a text.
I can discuss the impact of an author's perspective on the overall meaning of a text.
I can apply my understanding of different perspectives to real-life situations, such as understanding different viewpoints in a news article or recognizing bias in advertising.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can discuss how my own point of view differs from that of the author, narrator, or characters in a text.
I can explain how the author's point of view influences the way a story is told.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can explain how the main character's perspective changes throughout a story.
I can compare and contrast the perspectives of two different characters in a story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify the main character in a story.
I can recognize that different characters in a story can have different opinions.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify a personal point of view about a text.
I can when given three choices, select the choice that best represents their point of view about an assignment.
I can Point to the part or step on an activity sheet that they like best.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify personal point of view about the topic.
I can when given two choices, select the choice that best represents their own point of view about a topic (e.g., “Do you like ____ activity or do you like _____ activity best?”).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, express point of view about a topic.
I can Respond with gestures or facial expressions to topic.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Explain how specific illustrations or text features contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a text (e.g., create mood, emphasize character or setting, or determine where, when, why, and how key events occur). (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify parts of illustrations or tactual information that depict story elements. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how specific illustrations or text features work together to create meaning in a text and explain how they enhance the reader's understanding of the text. I can also use this understanding to create my own texts that effectively use illustrations and text features to convey meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how specific illustrations or text features contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a text, such as creating mood, emphasizing character or setting, or determining where, when, why, and how key events occur.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify specific illustrations or text features in a text and explain how they contribute to the meaning of a few words.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some illustrations or text features in a text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify parts of illustrations that depict a particular mood, setting, or character.
I can Find the part of the illustration that shows that the character is mad (e.g., the face, a fist, red face).
I can Find the part of the illustration that shows that the setting is gloomy (e.g., clouds, gray sky, no color).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use illustrations to describe characters and setting.
I can use an illustration from the text, generate words (character and setting), which are then put into sentences and are repeatedly accessed and used in the classroom (Calhoun’s Picture Word Inductive Model [PWIM]).
I can use an illustration of a character from the text, identify words from a list that describes how the character looks in the illustration.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify character or setting in an illustration from the text.
I can with guidance and support, identify the illustration that shows setting.
I can with guidance and support, identify the character from the text within an illustration.
I can Touch a picture of a character from the story, when given two illustrations, at least one of which is from the story.
I can Touch a picture of the setting of the story, when given two illustrations, at least one of which is from the story.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Explain how claims in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. (RI)
ee_text: Identify two related points the author makes in text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can clearly explain how multiple claims in a text are supported by relevant and strong reasons and evidence.
I can evaluate and compare the strength of evidence used to support claims in different sections of a text, and I can explain why certain reasons are more convincing than others.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can explain how the claims in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence.
I can identify specific pieces of evidence and directly link them to the claims they support.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some claims in a text but need help to fully explain how they are supported by reasons and evidence.
I can find some evidence in a text but need guidance to connect it to the claims being made.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can find a claim in a text with support, but I need help identifying the reasons and evidence that support it.
I need adult assistance to understand the connection between claims and the evidence provided in a text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify two related points the author makes in a text with minimal support.
I can explain how the two points are connected or related to each other.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify one point the author makes in a text, and I need help to find the second point.
I can recognize that the points are related with some guidance, but I need help explaining how they are connected.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify one point the author makes in a text with significant support.
I need help understanding how the points in the text are related or connected to each other.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: ecognize genres and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify similarities between two texts and recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how authors use genre conventions to achieve specific effects.
I can make complex connections between a text and multiple other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations.
I can use my understanding of genre to create my own texts.
I can explain how genre shapes our understanding of the world around us.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can recognize a variety of genres, including fiction and nonfiction.
I can explain how different genres are used for different purposes.
I can make connections between a text and other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations.
I can use evidence from the text to support my connections.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify different genres like biographies, news articles, and fairy tales.
I can explain how different genres use different features, like characters, plot, and setting.
I can make simple connections between a text and my own experiences.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify familiar genres like stories and poems.
I can notice some similarities between different texts I read.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify similarities and differences between two texts.
I can recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture.
I can explain how my own culture is similar to or different from other cultures.
I can use text evidence to support my answers.
I can discuss how cultural differences can enrich our lives.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify most similarities between two texts.
I can recognize how texts reflect different cultures.
I can explain how my own culture is similar to or different from other cultures.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify some similarities between two simple texts.
I can recognize that texts can be about different cultures.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
ee_text: ith guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write complex and sophisticated essays and stories that engage the reader and convey my ideas effectively.
I can use my writing to persuade, inform, and entertain others.
I can use my writing to advocate for myself and others.
I can use my writing to make a difference in the world.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can compose reflective, formal, and creative writing for a variety of purposes, including high-stakes and low-stakes situations.
I can choose the appropriate writing style and format for each purpose.
I can use a variety of persuasive techniques and literary devices in my writing.
I can revise and edit my writing to improve its clarity, organization, and effectiveness.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write longer paragraphs and short essays on a variety of topics.
I can use a variety of sentence structures and vocabulary words.
I can proofread my writing for errors in grammar, punctuation, and spelling.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write simple sentences and short paragraphs on familiar topics.
I can use some basic punctuation and capitalization rules.
I can share my writing with others.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a text and write to state an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from the library, use a computer-based word bank to write It’s the best, and then refer to the book to find an example of what makes it the best and write about it.
I can select a text, write a word to express an opinion about it (e.g., lk [like]) and then, given a written frame with the word “because,” add a reason (e.g., fne [funny]).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a text and write, draw, or dictate an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books and working with a teacher who guides the student to “write those words” and “type the sounds you hear in those words,” use a talking word processor and word prediction software to write good book and add one reason (e.g., lik barz [Like bears.]).
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, state an opinion (e.g., “bad’), attempt to write the word, and then have a teacher show how to use a word wall word (e.g., sad) to spell the word conventionally.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, then the teacher navigates through the student’s multiple message communication device to reveal messages that express an opinion, then selects a message communicating an opinion (e.g., “It’s really good!”) and when the teacher asks, “What makes it good?,” uses the device to answer (e.g., says “boy”) which the teacher interprets to mean the student liked the main character who was a boy and writes in chart form.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, state an opinion about a book.
I can look at, touch, or take a book from a selection of two when the teacher asks, “Show me your favorite.” and then writes <Student’s name> likes <name of book> on the small group chart text.
I can in a small, teacher-led group, select 2-3 snack choices, write them down on a menu, and then select their snack later in the day from the menu.
I can Look at, touch, or take a book from a selection of two when the teacher asks, “Show me your favorite.”

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: write text in a variety of modes. a. Opinion pieces in which the student supports a point of view about a topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, list reasons that support the opinion.
ee_text: with guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion about a topic or text and include at least one reason to support that opinion. b.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write well-developed opinion pieces that persuasively state my viewpoint and provide strong, logical reasons to support it. I can write informative texts that thoroughly explore a topic, incorporating a range of facts, definitions, details, and examples to effectively convey information.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write an opinion piece that states an opinion and provides a list of reasons that support the opinion. I can write informative or explanatory texts that introduce a topic and use facts, definitions, and details to develop points.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write an opinion piece that states my opinion and provides 1-2 reasons to support it. I can write an informative text that introduces a topic and includes some relevant facts, definitions, or details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a simple opinion piece with a basic statement of my opinion, but I struggle to provide reasons that support my view. I can write a basic informative text with a topic, but have difficulty including relevant facts, definitions, or details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a topic and write about it including one fact or detail.
I can select a topic by looking through a class photo album and then writes a label for one of the items in the photo.
I can select a topic from a book used during shared reading and then writes one fact from the book.
I can select a topic from a class chart of recent activities and then writes a remembered detail with an alternative keyboard (e.g., garden, dg dr <dig dirt>).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can write a fact or detail about a given topic.
I can when given an interactive whiteboard with a bank of words on a given topic, select words from the bank that are related to the topic to write a fact or detail about it.
I can select a fact or detail about a given topic from a list of facts and details.
I can when given a repeated line frame, contribute one detail to a group list about the topic (e.g., whales: Whales eat <fish>. Whales eat <krill>. Whales eat <plankton>.).
I can when read a short text by the teacher, suggest one idea to the class’s semantic web of details (e.g., pterodactyl: winged lizard, 40 feet long, flies, eats bugs, has four fingers), which the teacher writes and adds to the class dinosaur blog.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic for use during shared writing.
I can when given a choice of three topics to use during shared writing, eye gaze, point, or touch one to indicate a choice which the group will then write about and read aloud for the student.
I can select the topic for a shared writing activity from two or more choices offered by the teacher, and then select a related picture on the topic to type about, from which the teacher will model a related fact (e.g., Child has a picture of a rock and types “ewfsatrhrgr” and the teacher says, “I like your writing. I could use that r (as she points) and write ‘rock.’ I see a rock.”).

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Informative or explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts, definitions, and details to develop points.
ee_text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they provide at least 2 facts about a predetermined or self chosen topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can introduce a topic clearly and develop it thoroughly using well-organized facts, definitions, and relevant details that enhance understanding.
I can use precise language and transitions to connect ideas, making my writing engaging and informative.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can introduce a topic and use facts, definitions, and details to develop and explain my points clearly.
I can organize my writing in a logical sequence that helps the reader understand my topic.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can introduce a topic and include some facts and definitions, but I need support to organize my details and develop my points fully.
I need help using clear transitions to connect ideas and make my writing flow smoothly.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
With support, I can introduce a topic and include a few basic facts or definitions, but I struggle to develop points clearly.
I need significant guidance to organize my ideas and add enough details to make my writing informative.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can provide at least two facts about a predetermined or self-chosen topic that are accurate and relevant to the topic.
I can present my facts in a way that is understandable and related to the main idea of my writing.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can provide at least one fact about a predetermined or self-chosen topic with support, but I need help to find a second fact or make the connection to the topic clearer.
I need assistance organizing my facts, and my writing may need further development to explain the topic clearly.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with support, provide one fact about a predetermined or self-chosen topic, but I struggle to find a second fact or explain it clearly.
I need ongoing guidance to organize my ideas and ensure my facts are connected to the topic.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Convey events, real or imagined, through narrative or short stories to develop experiences or events using descriptive details and clear event sequences to establish a situation and introduce a narrator or characters. use dialogue and description of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
ee_text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened and tell about the events in the order in which they occurred.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can craft engaging narrative stories that vividly convey experiences and events through the use of descriptive language, well-developed characters, and a clear, logical sequence of events. I can effectively use dialogue, character thoughts and actions to deeply explore how characters respond to different situations, showcasing a nuanced understanding of human nature.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can convey events, real or imagined, through narrative or short stories, using descriptive details and clear event sequences to establish a situation and introduce a narrator or characters. I can also use dialogue and description of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a story that has a clear sequence of events and includes some descriptive details, but my development of characters and their responses to situations is limited.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a simple story with some details, but I have difficulty establishing a sequence of events or developing characters through dialogue and description.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience to write about in shared writing.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Include an introduction that establishes a purpose and provides a concluding statement appropriate to the mode of writing.
ee_text: with guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses words familiar to the student, temporal words to signal event order, and a beginning, middle, and end.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can craft engaging, well-organized writing that hooks the reader with a compelling introduction, artfully uses a variety of transition words and phrases to guide the reader, and selects precise, vivid vocabulary that enhances the overall meaning and flow of my writing. I can effectively adapt my word choice and organizational structure to suit different purposes and audiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create writing that has an introduction that establishes a purpose, uses transitions like "in addition", "for example", and "as a result" to link and build connections between ideas, and uses specific words to convey meaning and connect categories of information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write with an introduction and conclusion, and I try to use some transitions like "first", "then", and "in the end" to sequence my ideas. I use some general words to describe things.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a few sentences with a beginning and an end, but I do not use any transitions or specific word choices to connect my ideas.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
I can choose to write about his own birthday and write, pte [party].
I can choose to write about going to visit grandparents and write, fn [fun].
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
I can choose to write about their own birthday party and with support from the teacher who stretches out the word to isolate the sounds, write prte [party].
I can choose to write about the “fun” they had going to visit grandparents and with support from the teacher, who stretches out the word to isolate the sounds, write fan [fun].
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience to write about in shared writing.
I can choose by looking, pointing, or touching, an event from two choices presented by the teacher which the teacher then writes in the group’s shared text.
I can when given a teacher modeling the use of a multiple message voice output device and talking about the messages on the student’s My News page, select a message on a personal experience to use in shared writing (e.g., I went to my dad’s softball game. They won.), which the teacher will write down, reread aloud while pointing, and save.
I can express a reaction to a personal experience to be shared (e.g., After the teacher reviews free choice selections engaged in that day, she points to and labels each of the visual supports, and asks, “Did you like it?,” and the student responds [e.g., indicates yes by smiling], and the teacher writes, Brian liked art. Brian did not like the sand table. Brian liked his story. in his home-school journal, reading each aloud as she writes it, and the entire text while pointing after she finishes.).

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Transitions: use prompts, words, and phrases to signal event order and to link and build connections between ideas, text, and events.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a variety of transition words and phrases to connect ideas and events smoothly.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use words and phrases to show event order and link ideas, text and events.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use first, next and last to order events with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use and or then to join ideas with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Word Choice (including domain specific): use words familiar to the student for emphasis, addition, contrast, or order to connect categories or information, and to convey meaning.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose exact words to add emphasis, contrast or order and explain my choice.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use familiar words to add emphasis, addition, contrast or order and connect my ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use also, but or then from a word bank to connect ideas.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a few topic words to tell about a picture with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: ith support from adults and peers, produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task and purpose. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)
ee_text: ith guidance and support, produce writing that is appropriate for an explicitly stated task, and expresses more than one idea.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently produce well-developed, culturally-relevant writing that clearly communicates my purpose and engages my audience in a meaningful way.
descriptors.cc_at_target: With support from adults and peers, I can produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to the task and purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With support, I can write in a way that starts to show cultural awareness and a sense of purpose, but my organization and development still need improvement.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write with support, but my writing does not yet reflect cultural awareness or a clear purpose.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing that expresses more than one idea.
I can when working with peers, write one fact about a group project, talk with peers about the fact, and add one more fact with peer support.
I can when working with the teacher and a group of peers, contribute to a shared writing about a shared reading that includes at least two ideas related to a selected topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing that expresses an idea.
I can use a preprogrammed computer set-up with full alphabet access to write one idea.
I can when working with the teacher and a group of peers, contribute a written idea to a shared writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, express an idea.
I can when working with the teacher and a group of peers on a shared writing project, select from an array of choices to express an idea.
I can use a preprogrammed single message voice output device, express an idea to include in a writing project.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: ith guidance and support from adults and peers, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
ee_text: ith guidance and support from adults and peers, including questions or suggestions, revise their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently respond to feedback, plan, revise, and edit my writing to effectively strengthen it, and I can provide constructive feedback to my peers to help them improve their writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and with guidance and support, I can plan, revise, and edit my writing to add details and strengthen it.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write with some guidance and try to respond to feedback, but I have difficulty planning, revising, or editing my work to strengthen it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can try to write with some help, but I have trouble responding to feedback or making changes to improve my writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, revise own writing by adding more information.
I can select writing from own writing folder, share it with peers, and then revise it by adding more information based on the ideas provided by peers.
I can share writing with the teacher using a talking word processor to read it out loud, listen to the teacher talk about the writing, and then add more information based on what the teacher says.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more to own writing.
I can when working with a small group of peers to write a thank you note to a parent who helped the class, write one word and add another when a peer says, “Tell them why you’re thanking them,” or “tell them more about why you liked them helping.”
I can write using a talking word processor, read it back to the group using the software, and then add more when suggestions are offered by peers.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing.
I can when working on a tablet computer with an onscreen keyboard that speaks the letter names, select letters to produce writing.
I can use two-switch partner-assisted scanning, direct an adult to point to/say the next letter of the alphabet and indicate, “write that one down.” when the teacher points to/says a desired letter.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: ith guidance and support from adults and peers, use digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing.
ee_text: ith guidance and support from adults, use digital tools to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others. Learn to produce writing through printing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish high-quality, multi-paragraph writing, collaborating effectively with my peers. I can fluently produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing, and I use these skills to communicate my ideas in real-world situations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use digital tools with guidance and support from adults and peers to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with others. I can also produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use digital tools with some guidance from adults or peers to produce and publish simple, short pieces of writing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use digital tools with a lot of help from adults or peers, but I still struggle to produce and publish any writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use a single switch to scan through choices in an onscreen word bank and peers expand on the word in a collaborative writing project.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use an alternative keyboard while a peer uses a standard keyboard for the pair to work together in producing a collaborative writing project.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use assistive technology to post a comment in response to a text posted on an Internet site (e.g., a children’s reading site, a class science blog, or a children’s author’s homepage).
I can with guidance and support, use assistive technology to engage in instant messaging with another student or volunteer in a digital communication environment (e.g., a cellphone, an online communication site).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce writing.
I can when working with the teacher, use a switch to scan through choices in an onscreen word bank and select words to produce writing.

subject: ELA
cluster: Phonics & Word Recognition
text: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words. a. Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
ee_text: Use letter-sound knowledge to read words. a. Use linguistic context and letter- sound knowledge to identify unfamiliar words. b. Decode and encode, in the way the child is able, single-syllable words with common spelling patterns (consonant-vowel-consonant [CVC] or high-frequency rimes). See L.4.6 for additional spelling/encoding/word analysis guidance.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can confidently decode and understand the meaning of unfamiliar multisyllabic words, even in complex texts, using my knowledge of phonics, syllabication, roots, and affixes. I can also analyze the structure of words to determine their meaning and explain how different parts contribute to the overall meaning.
Ex. Upon encountering the word "unpredictable" in a text, an advanced student can break it down into its morphemes (unpredictable), identify the root word "predict," and use their knowledge of prefixes and suffixes to determine the word's meaning as "not able to be predicted." They can then use context clues to confirm their understanding and infer the word's connotation within the sentence.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can accurately decode unfamiliar multisyllabic words in and out of context by applying my knowledge of phonics, syllabication patterns, and common root words, prefixes, and suffixes.
Ex. When presented with the word "transportation" on a vocabulary list, an at-target student can correctly pronounce the word by breaking it into syllables (trans-por-ta-tion), recognizing the root word "transport," and applying their knowledge of the suffix "-ation." They can then use a dictionary or context clues to determine the word's meaning.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can decode some unfamiliar multisyllabic words by using phonics knowledge and recognizing common syllable patterns. I may still need support decoding words with less common syllable patterns or unfamiliar roots and affixes.
Ex. An approaching student might struggle to read the word "microscope" correctly on the first try. However, after breaking it into syllables (microscope) and sounding out each part, they can decode the word and understand its meaning, especially when supported by a visual aid or context clues.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can decode some single-syllable words with regular spelling patterns. I may still need support blending sounds, recognizing common syllable patterns, or decoding multisyllabic words.
Ex. An emerging student might be able to read the word "play" but struggle to decode the word "replay" even though it shares the same rhyme. They would need additional support and practice to recognize and decode multisyllabic words and words with more complex spelling patterns.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use letter-sound knowledge to read words. I can use linguistic context and letter-sound knowledge to identify unfamiliar words. I can also decode and encode single-syllable words with common spelling patterns (CVC or high-frequency rimes), in the way I am able. 
I can A student sees the word "rain" in a story about a stormy day. They can sound out each letter (/r/ /ai/ /n/) and blend the sounds together to read the word. They also recognize the word "umbrella" because they've seen it before in the context of rain, even though they might not be able to sound it out perfectly. They can confidently read and spell words like "cat," "run," and "make."
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I am starting to use letter-sound knowledge to read words. I can sometimes use context clues to guess unfamiliar words. I am practicing decoding and encoding single-syllable words with common spelling patterns. 
I can A student encounters the word "dog" in a text. They can identify the sounds for /d/ and /g/ but might need a reminder for the sound /o/ makes. They look at the picture next to the word, see a dog, and confirm their guess. They are working on reading and spelling words like "hop," "bed," and "sun."
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I am learning about letter-sounds and how they connect to reading words. I can identify some letters and sounds. I am starting to use picture clues to guess unfamiliar words.
I can A student sees the word "sun" while listening to a story about a sunny day. They can identify the letters "s" and "n" but may need help recognizing the letter "u." They point to the picture of the sun when asked, "Where's the sun?" They are learning to recognize letters like "a," "m," and "t" and their corresponding sounds.

subject: ELA
cluster: Fluency
text: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension. a. Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
ee_text: Read words in text. Read text comprised of familiar words with accuracy and understanding. a. With decreasing support, use features of print to identify or verbalize appropriate expression while reading familiar texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read complex texts fluently and with expression. I can easily understand what I read and can analyze the author's purpose and message. I can use my reading skills to learn new information and complete tasks. I can also discuss what I read with others and share my interpretations. 
Ex. A student effortlessly reads a challenging historical fiction novel set during the American Revolution. They clearly understand the historical context, character motivations, and complex themes presented in the story. They can engage in a thoughtful discussion about the book, comparing it to other historical fiction they've read and drawing connections to real-world events.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level text with accuracy, fluency, and expression. I can understand what I read and use context to confirm or self-correct my understanding. I can reread difficult passages to improve my comprehension.
Ex. A student reads aloud a passage from a grade-level science textbook about the life cycle of a butterfly. They read with appropriate pacing, pausing at commas and using inflection to convey meaning. When they stumble on the word "metamorphosis," they reread the sentence and use context clues to correctly pronounce the word and understand its meaning.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read most simple sentences accurately and fluently. I can usually understand what I read, but I may need to reread some sentences. But I usually can make sense of simple sentences from the context clues. 
Ex. A student reads a short story about a family camping trip. They can read most of the sentences fluently but pause or stumble over some multisyllabic words. They can answer simple comprehension questions about the story, such as "Where did the family go?" but might need help understanding more nuanced details or making inferences.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can read simple texts with familiar words. I understand most of what I read. I can use pictures and other clues to help me figure out new words.I am still developing my reading skills.
Ex. A student reads a simple book about different animals on a farm. They can recognize high-frequency words like "the," "see," and "go" and can sound out some consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words like "cat," "dog," and "pig" with some effort. They rely on the pictures to help them understand the story and can point to the correct animal when asked, "Where is the cow?"
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can read familiar words accurately, understand what I am reading, and use what I know about letters and sounds to figure out new words.
I can The student reads a short story with fluency, can answer comprehension questions about the story, and uses their knowledge of digraphs to read the word "ship" correctly.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can read most familiar words in simple sentences and use letter sounds and pictures to figure out new words.
I can The student can read all but one or two words in the sentence "The dog ran to the park." and uses the picture and the beginning sound to figure out the word "ball" in "The boy kicked the ball."
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can read some words in simple sentences with help.
I can The student can read "The cat sat" in "The cat sat on the mat" with teacher support.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Fluency
text: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

descriptors.cc_approaching:
