I can improve my reading accuracy and expression with practice and guidance (e.g., "I read the text better after practicing and with help to pause at commas").
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can read simple texts aloud with support, improving my speed and expression with practice (e.g., "I practiced reading aloud and got better at reading the sentences with pauses").
I can read aloud more smoothly when someone helps me and I practice multiple times (e.g., "With help, I learned to read the text a little faster and used a happy tone for the characters").
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use letter sounds and context clues to help me read words I don't know.
I can sound out words and use the story to help me understand what I'm reading.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use some letter sounds to figure out words when reading with help.
I can look at the pictures or words around a new word to help me read it with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can listen to the sounds in a word and match them to a picture or word I know with support.

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Locate and refer to relevant details and evidence when explaining what a text says explicitly or implicitly and make logical inferences. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify explicit details in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze details and evidence within a text to make insightful inferences and draw complex conclusions, using these skills to understand real-world situations and form informed opinions.
Ex. A student reads a news article about the pros and cons of school uniforms. They identify the main arguments presented on both sides, evaluate the evidence used to support each claim, and consider the potential implications of implementing uniforms in their own school. They then form a well-reasoned opinion on the topic, drawing connections to their own experiences and values.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use specific details and evidence from the text to explain what is happening, both directly and indirectly, and make logical predictions about what might happen next. 
Ex. During a read-aloud of a mystery, a student listens closely as the detective discovers a muddy footprint near the crime scene. Later, a new character is introduced, described as wearing muddy boots. The student raises their hand to predict that the new character might be involved in the crime, citing the muddy footprint as evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some details in a text to support an answer but may struggle to understand implicit meanings or make logical inferences consistently.
Ex. A student reads a story about a girl who misses her grandmother. When asked why the girl is sad, the student points to the sentence, "Tears rolled down her cheeks." However, they struggle to connect this detail to other clues in the text, like the girl looking at old photos, to fully grasp the reason behind her sadness.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can locate a specific detail within a text when prompted.
Ex. A teacher reads a story about a cat chasing a butterfly. The teacher pauses and asks, "What color was the butterfly?" The student successfully finds and points to the sentence, "The bright yellow butterfly fluttered through the garden."
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify specific details that are directly stated in the text. 
I can after listening to a story about a dog named Spot who goes for a walk in the park, a student can answer the question, "Where did Spot go?" by stating, "Spot went to the park," recalling the specific detail directly from the text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify some explicit details in a text when prompted with questions or visual cues. 
I can A teacher reads a short paragraph about different types of weather. when prompted with the question, "What kind of weather makes the plants grow?", the student, looking back at the text, can identify and point to the sentence that says, "Rain helps the plants grow."
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can select a named detail from a text with visual supports (e.g., pointing to a picture that matches a word). 
I can A student is looking at a page from a book about animals that shows a picture of a cat next to the word "cat." when asked, "Can you find the cat?" the student can point to the picture of the cat.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Summarize texts, from a variety of genres, to determine a theme or central idea and explain how it is supported by key details. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify the theme or main idea from a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze details and evidence within a text to make insightful inferences and draw complex conclusions, using these skills to understand real-world situations and form informed opinions.
Ex. After reading multiple news articles about climate change, an advanced student could synthesize information from each source to identify the most pressing environmental concerns. They could then analyze the different perspectives presented, evaluate the evidence supporting each viewpoint, and develop their own informed opinion on the issue, considering potential solutions and their feasibility.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use specific details and evidence from the text to explain what is happening, both directly and indirectly, and make logical predictions about what might happen next.
Ex. While reading a mystery novel, an at-target student could use clues from the text, such as a character's suspicious behavior or a hidden object, to make inferences about the mystery and predict who the culprit might be. They could explain their reasoning by citing specific details and evidence from the text that support their prediction.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some details in a text to support an answer but may struggle to understand implicit meanings or make logical inferences consistently.
Ex. When asked why a character in a story is feeling angry, an approaching student might point to the sentence, "He slammed his fist on the table." However, they might struggle to connect this detail to other clues in the text, such as the character having just received bad news, to fully explain the reason behind the anger.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can locate a specific detail within a text when prompted.
Ex. When asked, "What color was the car in the story?" an emerging student could successfully locate and point to the sentence stating, "The bright red car sped down the road."
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the main idea or theme of a story, poem, or informational text.
I can after reading "The Giving Tree," the student can explain that the theme is about the selfless love between a tree and a boy.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify the main idea of a story or informational text with help.
I can after reading a nonfiction text about dolphins, the student can, with prompting from the teacher, identify the main idea of each paragraph.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can retell some of the events or key details from a story.
I can after listening to the story "Goldilocks and the Three Bears," the student can use pictures to retell what happened at the beginning, middle, and end of the story.

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Describe a character (traits, motivations, feelings), setting, or event, drawing on specific details in the text. (RL) Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts, including what happened and why, based on specific evidence from the text. (RI)
ee_text: Use details from the text to describe characters in the text. (RL) Identify an explicit detail that is related to an individual event, or idea in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author develops characters, settings, events, ideas, or concepts over the course of a text, using specific details and evidence to support my analysis. I can also compare and contrast these elements across different texts and genres.
Ex. (RL) After reading a fantasy novel, an advanced student could analyze the protagonist's character arc, citing specific details that demonstrate how the character's challenges and choices throughout the story led to their growth and transformation.
Ex. (RI) After reading multiple articles about renewable energy, an advanced student could compare and contrast the different types of energy sources discussed, explaining the benefits and drawbacks of each based on evidence from the texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can thoroughly describe a character, setting, or event in a narrative text, providing relevant details about their traits, motivations, feelings, or significance. I can also clearly explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in informational texts, using evidence from the text to support my explanations.
Ex. (RL) After reading a historical fiction novel, an at-target student could accurately describe the main character's personality, providing details about their actions, thoughts, and relationships with other characters to support their description.
Ex. (RI) After reading a science article about photosynthesis, an at-target student could accurately explain the process, including the steps involved and the role of sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide, using evidence from the text to support their explanation.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some key details about characters, settings, events, ideas, or concepts in a text. I may need support to elaborate on my descriptions or explanations and connect details to a larger understanding of the text.
Ex. (RL) When asked to describe the setting of a story, an approaching student could identify the location and time period but might struggle to provide specific details or explain the setting significance to the story.
Ex. (RI) When asked to explain the main idea of a history article about the American Revolution, an approaching student could identify the key event (the colonies declaring independence) but might struggle to explain the reasons behind the revolution or its lasting impact.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize basic details about characters, settings, events, or topics in a text when prompted with questions or visual cues. I may need significant support to make connections between details or draw inferences from the text.
Ex. (RL) When asked, "Who is the main character in the story?", an emerging student could point to a picture of the character or identify their name in the text.
Ex. (RI) After listening to a teacher read a text about different types of weather, an emerging student could point to a picture of a thunderstorm when asked to identify an example of severe weather.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify and describe a character's traits, actions, and feelings using specific details from a narrative text. In informational texts, I can identify a key detail that directly relates to a specific event, idea, or concept.
I can (RL) after reading a story about a boy and his dog, a student could describe the boy as "kind" because the text says he shares his toys with the dog and "brave" because he saves the dog from a busy street.
I can (RI) after reading a paragraph about the invention of the telephone, a student could identify the year it was invented as a key detail related to that event.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify some details about a character in a story, such as their name, appearance, or a simple action they take. In informational texts, I can pick out a stated detail related to a topic when prompted.
I can (RL) when asked about a character in a story, a student might say, "Her name is Sarah, and she has a cat."
I can (RI) when reading about different types of animals, if asked, "What do birds use to fly?", the student could locate and state, "wings."
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can match a picture to a character or event from a story I have heard or read. In informational texts, I can point to a named detail or picture that relates to the topic.
I can (RL) after listening to a story, the student can choose the correct picture of the main character from a set of options.
I can (RI) when looking at a page about different foods, if asked, "Which picture shows an apple?", the student can point to the image of the apple.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Determine the meaning of words, phrases, figurative language, academic, and content-specific words within a text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Determine the meaning of words in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author's choice of words and phrases, including figurative language, impacts the tone and meaning of a text, and I can apply this understanding to my own writing and communication.
Ex. After reading a poem that uses metaphors to describe nature, a student can discuss how the poet's word choices create vivid imagery and evoke a sense of wonder and awe in the reader. They can then use similar techniques in their own creative writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can determine the meaning of unfamiliar words and phrases, including figurative language, academic terms, and content-specific vocabulary, using context clues and my knowledge of word parts.
Ex. While reading a science article about the solar system, a student encounters the phrase "vast distances." Using context and their knowledge of the word "vast," they understand that the planets are incredibly far apart.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use context clues to figure out the meaning of some unfamiliar words and phrases in a text.
Ex. A student encounters the sentence, "The courageous firefighter rescued the kitten from the tree." Even if they don't know the word "courageous," they can infer it means something positive because the firefighter did something good.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use visual clues or simple definitions to understand the basic meaning of some words in a text.
Ex. When reading a story about a bird building a nest, a student can point to a picture of twigs and leaves when asked, "What is the nest made of?"
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine meaning of words in context.
I can after reading a text, create a picture of the word or character based on descriptions in the text.
I can Identify the words in a text that provide clues that help determine the meaning of an unknown word and use them to determine the meaning.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify two or more words that are related to one another.
I can given a word from the text, identify two or more related words from a list provided by the teacher.
I can Create a graphic organizer showing connections between a new word found in text and other known words.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can after listening to or reading a text, touch or look at a picture, object, or other symbolic representation of the word.
I can after reading or listening to a book and an adult saying or signing a word from the text, find a picture or object that represents the word.
I can after hearing a text about drums, touch a drum, drumstick, and other drum-related objects to demonstrate understanding of the drum-related words.
I can match a word from the text to a picture or object that represents the word.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Identify and analyze structural elements, using terms such as verse, rhythm, meter, characters, settings, dialogue, stage directions. (RL) Identify the overall structure using terms such as sequence, comparison, cause and effect, and problem and solution. (RI)
ee_text: Identify elements that are characteristic of stories (RL) and informational texts (RI).

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author's choice of structural elements enhances the meaning and impact of a text, and I can apply this understanding to create my own writing.
Ex. After reading a play, a student can explain how the playwright uses dialogue to reveal character relationships and build suspense, leading to a climactic resolution. They can then apply this knowledge to write their own short play using similar techniques.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and explain the purpose of different structural elements in both literary and informational texts, using appropriate terminology.Ex. When reading a poem, a student can identify the verses, rhyme scheme, and rhythm. In an informational text about climate change, they can identify the use of cause and effect to explain the relationship between human actions and environmental changes.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some common structural elements in texts, such as characters, setting, and the main events of a story. I can recognize some signal words that indicate text structure in informational texts.
Ex. After reading a short story, a student can name the main characters and describe the setting. In a science article, they can point out words like "because" and "so" that signal a cause-and-effect relationship.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use visual cues and prompts to identify basic structural elements in a text, such as the beginning, middle, and end of a story.
Ex. When looking at a storybook, a student can point to the pictures that represent the beginning, middle, and end of the story.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify and explain the difference between a story and an informational text. I can also identify story elements like characters, setting, and plot in stories and key features like headings and diagrams in informational texts.
I can given a story about a dragon and a nonfiction book about different types of weather, the student can accurately sort them and explain that the dragon book is a story because it has characters and a plot, while the weather book is informational because it has real facts and headings.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify the difference between a story and an informational text with some help. I can identify some story elements in stories and some key features in informational texts.
I can The student can, with prompting from the teacher, identify the characters in a story and the topic of an informational text.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures and some words to describe what a story is about.
I can after listening to a story, the student can point to pictures of the characters and setting.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: In literary text, compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations. (RL)
ee_text: Identify the narrator of a story (RL); compare own experience to that described within the text. In informational text, compare and contrast a primary and secondary source on the same event or topic. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author's choice of point of view shapes the reader's understanding of events and characters, and I can apply this understanding to my own writing.
Ex. After reading two stories about the same historical event, one told from a first-person perspective and the other from a third-person perspective, a student can analyze how each point of view affects the reader's perception of the event and its significance. They can then write their own account of the event from a chosen point of view, explaining their reasoning.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can compare and contrast the point of view in different stories, explaining how the narrator's perspective influences the information revealed to the reader.
Ex. A student reads a story told from the first-person perspective of a young boy and another story told from the third-person perspective of an omniscient narrator. They can explain that the first story only reveals the boy's thoughts and feelings, while the second story provides a broader view of the events and characters.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify whether a story is told from the first-person or third-person point of view, and I can recognize some basic differences between these perspectives.
Ex. When reading a story that uses "I" and "me," a student can identify it as first-person narration. They can also recognize that a third-person narrator might know things that the main character doesn't.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize that stories can be told from different perspectives, and I can identify some clues that indicate who is telling the story.
Ex. When listening to a story, a student can point to the character who is speaking and understand that the story is being told from that character's point of view.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify who is telling a story. I can compare my own experiences to what happens in a story or informational text. I can compare and contrast information from two different texts about the same topic.
I can after reading a story told from the first-person perspective of a child moving to a new town, the student can identify that the child is the narrator and can compare the experience to a time they felt nervous about a new experience. when reading about the American Revolution from a firsthand account and a textbook, the student can identify similarities and differences in how the event is portrayed.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify if a story is told by a character or someone who is not a character in the story. I can find connections between events in a story and my own life.
I can when reading "The Three Little Pigs," the student can identify that the story is not told by one of the pigs or the wolf. after reading about a child who overcomes a fear, the student can share a time they faced a challenge.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can answer simple questions about who and what a story is about.
I can after listening to "Little Red Riding Hood," the student can answer questions like, "Who went to visit Grandma?" and "What happened in the forest?"

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Explain how text features (e.g., charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations, and illustrations) contribute to an understanding of the text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Make connections between the text representation and a visual, tactual, or oral version of the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how different text features can be used to achieve specific purposes, such as emphasizing key information, clarifying complex concepts, or persuading the reader, and I can use this understanding to create my own informative and engaging texts.
Ex. After researching the rainforest ecosystem, a student creates a brochure that includes photographs, maps, and graphs to effectively convey information about the rainforest biodiversity, climate, and the threats it faces. They can explain their reasoning for choosing specific text features to enhance the reader's understanding.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can explain how specific text features, such as charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations, and illustrations, help me better understand the information or ideas presented in a text.
Ex. When reading a science article about the life cycle of a butterfly, a student can explain that the diagram helps them visualize the different stages of metamorphosis and understand the sequence of changes.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify various text features in both literary and informational texts and can describe how those features relate to the main topic or message.
Ex. In a biography about a famous inventor, a student can identify the timeline and explain that it shows the order of important events in the inventor's life.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify common text features, such as pictures, captions, and headings, and I can use these features to gain a basic understanding of the text.
Ex. When looking at a nonfiction book about different animals, a student can point to the captions under the pictures to learn the names of the animals.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can make connections between text and visual or oral presentations.
I can when shown a video of a story that has been read to them, indicate that the two are the same story.
I can after reading or listening to someone read a text-based version of the story, identify one or more ways that the video-based version of the story is the same.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify the text-based version of the story that matches the visual or oral presentation.
I can after watching a video-based presentation of a familiar story, select the matching text from an array of choices.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can communicate a preference for the text-based or visual or oral presentation of a story.
I can after watching a play based on a familiar book, indicate preference for the book or the play version.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Explain how claims in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. (RI)
ee_text: Identify one or more reasons supporting a specific point in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze the strength of an author's argument by evaluating the relevance and credibility of the evidence presented, and I can use this skill to form my own well-supported opinions.
Ex. After reading an opinion piece about the benefits of reducing screen time, a student can identify the author's main claim and supporting reasons. They can then evaluate the credibility of the sources cited and determine if the evidence provided is sufficient and convincing.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the main claim an author is making in a text and explain how the author supports that claim with reasons and evidence.
Ex. While reading an article about the importance of recycling, a student can identify the author's claim that "recycling helps protect the environment." They can then point to specific facts and examples the author uses to support this claim, such as reducing pollution and conserving natural resources.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some reasons and evidence an author uses to support a point, but I may struggle to distinguish between strong and weak support.
Ex. A student reads a text about the benefits of eating fruits and vegetables. They can identify a reason given by the author, such as "Fruits and vegetables are full of vitamins," but may not fully grasp how this supports the overall claim that these foods are good for you.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify a simple claim in a text, and with support, I can locate a related detail or example.
Ex. When reading a text about different types of dogs, a student can identify the claim that "Golden Retrievers are good family pets." With help, they can then find a sentence that provides a reason, such as "Golden Retrievers are known for being gentle and playful with children."
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can find reasons given by the author to support a point in an informational text.
I can after reading a text about why recycling is important, the student can identify several supporting reasons the author provides, such as conserving resources and reducing landfill waste.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can answer “why” questions about a text with support.
I can when asked, "Why do we need to wear sunscreen?" after reading an informational text about sun safety, the student can point to the text that explains sunscreen protects our skin from harmful rays.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can answer simple questions about what I learned from an informational text.
I can after listening to a text about different types of birds, the student can answer, "What do birds use their wings for?"

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Recognize genres and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Identify similarities between two texts and recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how genre influences an author's choices and a reader's expectations, and I can use this understanding to deepen my appreciation for a variety of texts and make insightful connections between them.
Ex. After reading a historical fiction novel set during the American Revolution and comparing it to a nonfiction article about the same time period, a student can discuss how each genre presents information differently and affects their understanding of the historical events and people involved.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the genre of a text and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations.
Ex. After reading a folktale about a clever rabbit, a student can identify it as belonging to the folktale genre and connect it to other folktales they've read from different cultures, noting similarities in themes, characters, or morals.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some common genres, such as realistic fiction, fantasy, and informational texts, and I can make simple connections between texts based on shared topics or themes.
Ex. When presented with a realistic fiction story about a child overcoming a challenge, a student can connect it to a personal experience where they also faced and overcame a difficulty, recognizing similar emotions and problem-solving strategies.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify basic genres, like stories and informational books, and I can connect details in a text to my own life or to things I have seen and heard.
Ex. After listening to a story about a child visiting the zoo, a student can connect it to their own experience visiting a zoo, recalling specific animals they saw or activities they enjoyed.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can find similarities in the topics or events in two different texts. I can identify how a text reflects the culture of the people it describes.
I can after reading "The Tortoise and the Hare" and "The Lion and the Mouse," the student can identify that both stories have a theme of "slow and steady wins the race." after reading a story about a traditional celebration in another country, the student can identify details about the food, clothing, and customs that are part of that culture.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find topics that are the same in two different texts. I can identify characters and settings in stories that are different from my own experience.
I can after reading two different books about animals, the student can identify that both books are about animals. when reading a story set in a different country, the student can point out details about the setting that are unfamiliar to them.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures to identify if two stories have similar characters or events.
I can given two stories with picture supports, one about a child's day at school and one about a child's day at the park, the student can match pictures of similar activities like playing with friends.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically choose from a range of writing styles and genres to effectively communicate my ideas and achieve my purpose for a specific audience, incorporating reflection and creativity to enhance my message.
Ex. A student might write a persuasive letter to the editor of the local newspaper advocating for a new park, using formal language and strong arguments. Later that week, they might write a humorous poem from the perspective of a dog living in their neighborhood, showcasing their creative writing skills and reflecting on their community.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write in different styles for different purposes, including reflective pieces, formal essays, and creative stories. I can develop my ideas with details and use appropriate vocabulary and grammar.
Ex. For a science project, a student writes a formal report about an experiment they conducted, using scientific vocabulary and a structured format. In their journal, they reflect on the challenges and successes they experienced during the experiment, using more informal language and personal anecdotes.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write for different purposes, like telling a story, sharing my opinion, or explaining something I learned. I can use some details in my writing and am starting to try different writing styles.
Ex. A student might write a story about a magical adventure, incorporating fantastical elements and descriptive language. They can also write a paragraph explaining their favorite hobby, providing reasons why they enjoy it.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write short pieces for different purposes, like telling a story or sharing something about myself. I can use words and pictures to express my ideas.
Ex. A student might draw a picture of their family and write a caption for each person, describing their relationship and personality. They might also write a few sentences about their favorite animal, including some simple details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use drawings, dictation, or writing to compose different types of writing for different purposes with help from my teacher.
I can The student participates in a writing workshop where they choose to write a story about a magical creature (low-stakes) and later drafts an informational paragraph about their favorite animal with facts and details (high-stakes). They may use any combination of drawing, dictation, or writing to complete these tasks.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use drawings and dictation to tell a story or share information with help from my teacher.
I can The student draws a picture of their family and dictates a sentence about each family member to the teacher.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use drawings to express my ideas and interests.
I can The student draws a picture of a playground and uses gestures or single words to share details about their drawing.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Opinion pieces in which the student introduces the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose. List reasons that support the opinion.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion about a topic or text and include some reasons to support that opinion.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can skillfully craft different types of writing, using a variety of techniques to engage the reader and achieve my specific purpose. I can seamlessly transition between different modes of writing, adapting my style and structure to best suit the task and audience.
Ex. A student might write a compelling editorial for the school newspaper arguing for a change in the school lunch menu, using persuasive language, strong evidence, and a clear organizational structure. They can then switch gears and write a captivating mystery story with vivid descriptions, suspenseful pacing, and realistic dialogue, demonstrating their versatility as a writer.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write opinion pieces with clear reasons, informative texts with well-organized facts, and narratives with engaging plots and characters. I can use different writing techniques to make my writing interesting and easy to understand.
Ex. For an opinion piece, a student might argue that recess should be longer, providing reasons like increased physical activity and improved focus in class. For an informative text, they might write a report about their state, including headings, maps, and interesting facts. For a narrative, they might write a story about a lost puppy finding its way home, using dialogue and descriptive details to create an emotional connection with the reader.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write in different styles for different purposes, like sharing my opinion, giving information, or telling a story. I can organize my writing and use some details to make it more interesting.
Ex. In an opinion piece, a student might state their preference for cats over dogs, giving a few simple reasons. For an informative text, they might write about their favorite animal, including some basic facts and maybe a picture. For a narrative, they might write a story about a time they went camping, including a few events and some description.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can try different types of writing, like sharing my opinion, telling what I know, or telling a story. I can use words and pictures to express my ideas.
Ex. A student might draw a picture of their favorite playground and write a sentence about why they like it (opinion). They could label parts of a plant and write what each part does (informative). They might draw a series of pictures showing a day at the beach and write a simple caption for each picture (narrative).
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use drawing, dictation, or writing to create opinion pieces, informational texts, and narratives with help from my teacher. I can share my opinions with reasons, teach others about a topic, and tell stories with a beginning, middle, and end.
I can The student dictates an opinion piece about their favorite season, providing reasons why they like it. They draw and label a diagram of a plant for an informational report. They write a short story about a time they went to the zoo, including details about the animals they saw.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use drawing and dictation to share my opinions, give information about a topic, and tell simple stories with help from my teacher.
I can The student draws a picture of their favorite food and dictates a sentence about why they like it. They work with a partner to create a poster with pictures and labels about different types of transportation. They retell a familiar story using pictures and simple sentences.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use drawings and some words to express my opinions, share information, and tell a story.
I can The student draws a picture of themselves playing with a friend and dictates a sentence about what they are doing. They draw a picture of a recent event and label objects in the picture.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Informative texts in which they clearly introduce a topic, group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension. Use facts, definitions, and details to develop points.
ee_text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they introduce a topic and provide some facts, details, and/or multimedia content about a predetermined or self chosen topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write a detailed informative text with sections, headings, and images to clearly explain a topic (e.g., "I used headings and pictures to explain the steps of the water cycle").
I can organize my writing into paragraphs that use facts, definitions, and multimedia to explain a topic.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write an informative text that introduces a topic and organizes facts into sections or paragraphs (e.g., "I wrote about sharks and used paragraphs for their diet and habitat").
I can use illustrations or headings to help explain my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write a simple informative text that introduces a topic with some facts, with help to organize it into paragraphs (e.g., "I wrote about trees and put facts into two paragraphs with help").
I can add a picture or heading with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write a few sentences about a topic and add one fact with help (e.g., "I wrote about dogs and said they have four legs").
I can try to add a picture or heading when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or say facts about a topic and give some details to explain it.
I can use pictures, words, or videos to share information about a topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can write or say one fact about a topic and include a detail with help.
I can use a picture or word to give some information about a topic with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say a word or picture about a topic I know with support.
I can use pictures, words, or objects to show what I know about a topic with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Convey events, real or imagined, through narrative or short stories which orients a reader by establishing a real or imagined situation and introducing a narrator and characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally. Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
ee_text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened and tell about the events in the order in which they occurred.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write a narrative that uses dialogue, description, and pacing to develop events and show how characters react (e.g., "My story included a conversation between the characters and described how one felt nervous").
I can create a well-organized story that unfolds naturally, with clear character development.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write a narrative that introduces the characters and setting, and uses dialogue to show what happens (e.g., "In my story, the characters talked about their plan and went on an adventure").
I can organize my story with a beginning, middle, and end that flows naturally.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write a story with help, introducing characters and describing what happens (e.g., "I wrote about two friends and how they played together").
I can try to use dialogue and description with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write a short story with a simple situation and characters, with help (e.g., "I wrote about a boy and his dog going for a walk").
I can try to describe what happens with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or tell about something that happened, including details and the order of events.
I can share a story, real or made up, and explain what happened in order.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or write about one event and tell what happened with help.
I can share a story with some details about what happened with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures or words to show one event that happened with support.
I can tell or show one part of a story in order with help.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Include an introduction that establishes a purpose and provides a concluding statement related to the body of the composition. Structure of text reflects the purpose.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses familiar words, transitions to link and build connections, temporal words to signal event order, and a beginning, middle, and end.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically structure my writing to enhance clarity and impact. I use a variety of transitional words and phrases to create seamless flow and guide the reader through my ideas. My word choice is precise and engaging, demonstrating a nuanced understanding of language and its effects.
Ex. In a persuasive essay about the importance of libraries, a student begins with a compelling anecdote about discovering a lifelong love of reading at their local library (introduction). They use transition words like "furthermore" and "in contrast" to connect their arguments, and they conclude by urging readers to support library funding (conclusion). Their word choice is sophisticated and persuasive, using terms like "essential resource" and "vital community hub."
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write with a clear beginning, middle, and end. I can use transition words to connect my ideas and make my writing smooth. I choose words carefully to make my writing interesting and to show what I know about a topic.
Ex. In a report about the solar system, a student includes an introductory paragraph that introduces the topic and states their main points. They use transition words like "first," "next," and "finally" to guide the reader through the planets. They use specific vocabulary related to space, such as "orbit," "rotation," and "asteroid belt."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am getting better at organizing my writing and using some transition words to connect my ideas. I am trying to use more interesting and specific words in my writing.
Ex. In a story about a trip to the zoo, a student includes a beginning that sets the scene, a middle that describes the animals they saw, and an ending that shares their feelings about the day. They use some transition words like "then" and "after that" to show the order of events. They use some descriptive words to paint a picture for the reader.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write a beginning, middle, and end for my stories and other writing. I am learning to use words that connect my ideas and make my writing clearer.
Ex. In a personal narrative about a family vacation, a student writes a beginning sentence about where they went, a few sentences about what they did, and an ending sentence about how they felt. They might use simple transition words like "and" and "then." They are beginning to use words that are more descriptive than "good" or "fun."
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use drawing, dictation, or writing to create a story with a beginning, middle, and end. I can use words that tell the order of events and words that connect my ideas.
I can The student writes and illustrates a story about a lost puppy. They use words like "first," "then," and "finally" to show the order of events. They also use connecting words like "and" and "but" to make their writing smoother.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use drawing and dictation to tell a story with a beginning, middle, and end. I can use some words that tell the order of events.
I can The student draws a series of pictures about their trip to the beach. With teacher support, they dictate sentences about each picture, using words like "first" and "then" to show the order of their activities.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use drawings and some words to tell a story. I can put events in order.
I can The student draws three pictures to show what they did during their morning routine. They can point to each picture and use a word or two to describe what happened first, next, and last.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Transitions: Use phrases to signal event order and to link and build connections between ideas, text, and events.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use transition phrases like "after that" or "meanwhile" to smoothly connect events and ideas in my writing (e.g., "I used 'after that' to show what happened next in the story").
I can use complex transitions to link ideas and create a clear flow in my writing (e.g., "I used 'on the other hand' to show a contrast between two ideas").
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use phrases like "first," "next," and "finally" to show the order of events in my writing (e.g., "I used 'first' to show what happened at the beginning of the story").
I can use transition words to connect ideas and make my writing easier to follow.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use simple transition words like "then" and "after" to show event order in my writing with help (e.g., "I wrote 'then' to show what happened next").
I can try to connect my ideas using basic phrases with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use simple words like "and" or "next" to show the order of events with help (e.g., "I used 'next' to show what happened after the first event").
I can try to link ideas together in my writing with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Word Choice (including domain specific): Experiment with words to provide emphasis, addition, contrast, or order to connect themes and ideas.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can experiment with words like "moreover" or "in contrast" to emphasize important ideas and connect themes in my writing (e.g., "I used 'moreover' to add extra information to my point").
I can choose specific words to show differences or similarities between ideas (e.g., "I used 'in contrast' to highlight the differences between two events").
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use words like "also," "but," and "therefore" to add details or show contrast in my writing (e.g., "I used 'also' to add more information to my topic").
I can use words to emphasize key ideas and show connections between themes.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use simple words like "and" or "but" to add information or show contrast with help (e.g., "I used 'and' to add more details to my sentence").
I can try to use words to connect ideas and themes with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use basic words like "and" or "too" to add more information with help (e.g., "I said 'too' to show something extra happened").
I can try to use words to show how ideas are related with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)
ee_text: With guidance and support, produce writing that is appropriate for an explicitly stated task or purpose, and expresses more than one idea.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can adapt my writing style, tone, and content to effectively connect with diverse audiences while staying true to my own voice and experiences. I understand how to use language and storytelling traditions from my own culture to create writing that is both authentic and engaging for a wider audience.
Ex. A student who comes from a family with strong storytelling traditions might write a personal narrative about a family celebration, incorporating vivid imagery, sensory details, and dialogue that reflect their cultural background. They might also write a persuasive letter to the school board advocating for more inclusive curriculum, drawing on their own experiences and perspectives to make a compelling case.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write in a way that is clear, organized, and respectful of different cultures. I can adjust my writing depending on who I am writing for and why I am writing.
Ex. When writing a research report about a different country, a student uses respectful language and avoids stereotypes. They organize their information logically and cite their sources accurately. When writing a letter to a penpal from another country, they use a friendly tone and share information about their own culture and interests.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am learning to write for different audiences and purposes. I am trying to use language that is respectful of different cultures and backgrounds.
Ex. When writing a story about a character from a different culture, a student tries to use accurate details and avoid stereotypes. They might ask a classmate from that culture to review their writing and provide feedback.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about my own experiences and share my ideas with others. I am learning about different cultures and how to be respectful of others.
Ex. A student might write a story about a time they interacted with someone from a different culture, focusing on their observations and feelings. They might also draw a picture of their family and write a caption describing their family traditions.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write for different purposes when my teacher tells me what the purpose is. I can share more than one idea in my writing.
I can when asked to write a letter to a friend about their favorite game, the student includes multiple reasons why they enjoy the game and details about how it is played.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can writ]e for different purposes when my teacher tells me what the purpose is. I can share one or two ideas in my writing.
I can when asked to write a description of a picture, the student writes one or two sentences about what they see.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can write a few words or draw a picture to respond to a prompt.
I can when asked to write about their favorite animal, the student draws a picture of the animal and writes its name.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. Respond to questions and suggestions from peers; and add details to strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, plan before writing and produce writing focused on the planned topic, and revise their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I approach writing as a process of ongoing refinement. I can confidently explain and justify my writing choices, incorporating constructive feedback from peers to enhance the clarity, organization, and impact of my writing. I utilize a variety of revision and editing strategies to strengthen my writing.
Ex. After sharing a draft of their historical fiction story with a writing group, a student thoughtfully considers their peers' suggestions. They decide to add more sensory details to their description of a historical setting and incorporate dialogue to develop the relationship between two characters, ultimately strengthening the story's authenticity and emotional impact.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write for different purposes and audiences, organizing my ideas in a way that makes sense. I can use feedback from my classmates to improve my writing by adding details, making changes to the organization, or fixing mistakes.
Ex. After a peer review session, a student realizes that their informative report about sharks lacks a clear conclusion. They add a paragraph summarizing the main points and emphasizing the importance of shark conservation. They also correct any spelling or grammar errors that their partner identified.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write for different purposes, like telling a story or giving information. I am learning to organize my writing and add details to make it more interesting. I can use some help from my teacher and classmates to make my writing better.
Ex. When writing a story, a student uses a story map to plan out the beginning, middle, and end. They share their writing with a partner and ask for feedback on whether the story makes sense. They use the feedback to add details or make changes to the sequence of events.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about different topics and share my writing with others. I am learning to add details to my writing and make it easier to understand. I can use feedback from my teacher to make my writing better.
Ex. After writing a few sentences about their favorite animal, a student shares their work with the teacher. The teacher helps them add more details about the animal's appearance, habitat, and diet. The student then practices writing a clear ending sentence.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can plan what I am going to write or draw before I start. I can use my plan to help me stay on topic. I can make changes to my writing or drawings to make them better.
I can Before writing a story about a superhero, the student brainstorms ideas with a partner, creates a simple story map, and uses it to guide their writing. after writing, they review their work with a teacher, adding details and fixing errors.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use a planning strategy, like talking to my teacher or looking at pictures, before I write or draw. I can make some changes to my work when my teacher reminds me.
I can Before writing about their favorite animal, the student looks at pictures of animals with the teacher and talks about what they find interesting. after dictation, they listen to the teacher reread their sentences and help fix any mistakes.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can talk about my ideas with my teacher before I draw a picture. I can add more details to my drawings when my teacher helps me.
I can Before drawing a picture about their family, the student tells their teacher who they want to include in the picture. after finishing the drawing, they add details like hair color and clothing with prompting from the teacher.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: With some guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing (with sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting).
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, use digital tools, including the Internet, to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others. Learn to produce writing through printing and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I confidently and independently use a variety of digital tools to enhance my writing process and share my work with a wider audience. I can collaborate effectively with peers on digital writing projects, demonstrating strong communication and problem-solving skills. I can fluidly produce a final written product using printing, cursive, or typing, showcasing legible and developmentally appropriate handwriting or keyboarding skills.
Ex. A student might use a graphic organizer to plan a persuasive essay, then draft and revise the essay using a word processing program. They could collaborate with classmates on a shared online document to co-write a short story, using the comment feature to give each other feedback. They can then choose their preferred method to produce a final polished copy - neatly printing, writing in cursive, or typing at a reasonable speed with minimal errors.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use different digital tools to write and share my work, like typing on a computer, making a slideshow, or using an online dictionary. I can work with my classmates on a shared writing project. I can write neatly and clearly, either by hand or on a keyboard.
Ex. A student uses a word processing program to write a report about their favorite animal, inserting pictures from the internet and using the spell-check feature. They participate in a group project where they create a digital book together, each student contributing a different page. They can type their individual report page at a basic level of proficiency, or neatly hand write their final draft.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am learning to use digital tools to help me write. I can use a computer to type some of my work. I can work with a partner or small group on a writing project. I am working on writing neatly and clearly.
Ex. With help from the teacher, a student uses a drawing program to create illustrations for a story they wrote. They practice typing short sentences and stories on the computer, gradually increasing their speed and accuracy. They participate in a group writing activity where each student contributes a sentence to a shared story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use some digital tools to help me write, like clicking and dragging pictures or typing letters on a keyboard. I can practice writing my letters and words neatly.
Ex. A student uses a digital storytelling app to create a simple story with pictures and text boxes. They practice typing their name and other familiar words on the computer. They participate in a shared writing activity where the teacher writes their dictated sentences on a large chart paper.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use a computer or tablet to write with help from my teacher. I can use the internet to find information for my writing. I can share my writing with others and work together on writing projects.
I can The student uses a graphic organizer on a tablet to plan a report about an animal. They search for pictures and information on a kid-friendly website with teacher guidance. They practice typing sentences for their report and share their writing with a partner for feedback.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use a computer or tablet to write with help from my teacher. I can practice typing or printing my ideas.
I can The student uses a talking word processor to write a sentence about a picture. They practice typing their name and simple words on the keyboard with support.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use a computer or tablet to draw and write letters or my name.
I can The student uses a drawing app to create a picture and explores the keyboard to type letters or their name with assistance.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Conduct short inquiry projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
ee_text: With guidance and support, identify information about two or more aspects of a shared or independent inquiry topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can independently develop a focused research question and pursue a variety of relevant and credible sources to explore different facets of a topic. I can synthesize information from multiple sources to form my own conclusions and present my findings in a clear and engaging way.
Ex. Intrigued by a documentary about endangered animals, a student decides to research the impact of palm oil production on orangutans. They develop a research question, gather information from books, reputable websites, and expert interviews, and synthesize their findings in a multimedia presentation that includes maps, charts, and compelling photographs.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can choose a topic to research, ask good questions about it, and find answers using different sources like books, websites, and interviews. I can share what I learn in an organized way.
Ex. A student wants to learn more about ancient civilizations. They brainstorm a list of questions, such as "What were the major achievements of the Roman Empire?" and "How did ancient Egyptians build the pyramids?" They use books, websites, and museum resources to find answers to their questions and present their findings in a written report with headings and subheadings.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can work with my teacher and classmates to choose a research topic. I can ask questions about the topic and use some resources to find answers. I can share what I learn with others.
Ex. In a small group, students research different biomes around the world. They work together to brainstorm questions, use books and websites to find information, and create a diorama and presentation to share their findings.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can learn about a topic by asking questions and exploring different sources. I can share what I learn with my teacher and classmates.
Ex. A student is curious about different types of sharks. With guidance from the teacher, they explore books and videos about sharks, ask questions about what they are learning, and share interesting facts with the class.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can learn about a topic from different sources with help from my teacher. I can share at least two different things that I learned about the topic.
I can During a class study of weather, the student explores books and websites (with teacher guidance) to learn about different types of clouds and how rain forms. They can share details about both aspects of the topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can learn about a topic from pictures and books with help from my teacher. I can answer questions about what I learned.
I can when learning about the life cycle of a butterfly, the student looks at pictures and listens to a book read aloud. They can answer questions about a butterfly's different stages of development.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can ask questions about a topic I want to learn more about. I can identify a few key details about a topic from pictures.
I can when shown pictures of different ocean animals, the student asks, "What do they eat?" after listening to a simple book about whales, they can point to a picture of a whale and say, "It lives in the ocean."

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources, take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.
ee_text: Recall and sort information from personal experiences or a topic into given categories and write or draw about each one.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically select information from both personal experiences and a variety of sources to effectively support my purpose for writing. I can synthesize information from these sources, taking detailed notes that are accurately categorized and organized. I can create a comprehensive and correctly formatted list of sources.
Ex. A student researching the life cycle of butterflies might recall observations from their own garden, consult books and websites for scientific details, and interview a local entomologist. They take detailed notes, categorizing their findings by life cycle stage, and create a bibliography with accurate citations for each source.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can gather information from different sources, including my own experiences, books, websites, and interviews. I can take notes that help me remember the important information and organize it by topic. I can list the sources I used for my research.
Ex. A student writing a report about their local community might interview family members about its history, gather information from the library's local history section, and explore relevant websites. They take notes using keywords and phrases, organize their notes into categories like "History," "Landmarks," and "Notable Residents," and create a simple list of sources.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use different sources to find information for my writing. I am learning to take notes that help me remember what I learned. I can list some of the sources I used.
Ex. A student researching different types of trees might use books and websites to find basic information. They write down key facts and interesting details, using headings to separate information about different tree species. They create a list of sources, possibly with some assistance in writing complete citations.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can gather information about a topic from different sources. I can write down or draw pictures to remember what I learn.
Ex. A student learning about the planets in our solar system might explore books, watch videos, and look at pictures. They draw pictures of each planet and label them with basic information like size and color. They can identify at least one source they used.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can organize my ideas into different groups and then write or draw about each group.
I can after brainstorming a list of things they do in different seasons, the student sorts their ideas into categories (fall, winter, spring, summer). They then choose one season and write a paragraph describing their favorite activities during that time of year.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can sort pictures or objects into groups and then say a sentence about each group.
I can given a collection of toy animals from different habitats (farm, ocean, jungle), the student sorts them into the correct groups. They can then describe each group by saying a simple sentence, such as, "These animals live on a farm."
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can match objects or pictures to categories.
I can when shown pictures of different foods and given categories like "fruits" and "vegetables," the student can match the pictures to the correct groups.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Recall and use facts from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and inquiry.
ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts to support reflection or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can accurately recall and effectively weave together relevant facts and details from multiple literary and informational texts to support my own analysis, reflection, and inquiry. I can analyze how these facts connect to larger themes and concepts, drawing insightful conclusions and formulating new questions for further exploration.
Ex. A student reading a historical fiction novel about a child escaping a volcanic eruption connects details about volcanic activity to facts they learned from an informational text about Pompeii. They reflect on the devastating impact of natural disasters throughout history and formulate questions about modern-day disaster preparedness.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can remember important facts and details from stories and informational texts. I can use these facts to think critically about what I read, share my thoughts and feelings, and ask new questions.
Ex. After reading a biography about a famous scientist, a student recalls specific details about the scientist's experiments and discoveries. They reflect on the scientist's perseverance in the face of challenges and consider how their own curiosity could lead to new learning experiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can remember some facts and details from what I read. I can use these facts to tell what the text is about and share my ideas.
Ex. After reading a fable about the importance of honesty, a student recalls the main events of the story and can explain how the characters learned a valuable lesson. They can share their own thoughts about the importance of honesty in their own life.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can remember some things I learned from reading a story or informational text. I can use these details to answer questions and talk about what I read.
Ex. After listening to a story about a kind deed, a student can recall who the characters were and what they did. They can identify the kind action in the story and explain why it was important.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can remember important details from a story or informational text. I can use those details to answer questions and share my thinking about the text.
I can after listening to a story about a child who overcomes a fear, the student can recall details about how the character felt and what they did to face their fear. They can use these details to answer questions like, "How did the character change in the story?"
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can remember some details from a story or informational text. I can answer simple questions about the text with help from my teacher.
I can after listening to a nonfiction text about different types of birds, the student can recall one or two details about a specific bird. With prompting from the teacher, they can answer a question like, "What does a woodpecker eat?"
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can answer yes/no or pointing questions about a story or informational text.
I can after listening to a story about a trip to the zoo, the student can point to the animal when asked, "Did they see a lion?"

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher led) with diverse partners on topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing one’s thinking clearly. a. Come to discussions prepared, explicitly draw on topics and texts along with personal knowledge and experiences to explore ideas under discussion.
ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. a. Contribute ideas from prior experiences with a text during discussions about the same text.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I actively listen to and respectfully engage with my peers in a variety of discussion settings. I come prepared to share my own well-developed insights, connecting my thinking to specific details from the text, relevant background knowledge, and personal experiences. I can seamlessly weave my ideas with those of others, respectfully building upon, clarifying, or respectfully disagreeing with their points to deepen our collective understanding.
Ex. During a literature circle discussion about a novel's theme of courage, a student confidently shares their interpretation, citing specific passages from the text and connecting it to a historical figure known for their bravery. They actively listen to their peers' perspectives, asking clarifying questions and offering alternative interpretations that consider different characters' actions and motivations.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can participate in group discussions, sharing my ideas and listening to others. I can refer to the text, my own experiences, and what others say to support my points.
Ex. In a small group discussing the causes of the American Revolution, a student shares their understanding of "taxation without representation," drawing connections to a recent class discussion about fairness and equality. They listen attentively to their peers, nodding in agreement and adding brief comments to build upon their ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can participate in discussions by sharing my ideas and listening to others. I can use the text or my own experiences to explain what I think.
Ex. During a class discussion about a scientific article on animal adaptations, a student shares a personal anecdote about observing camouflage in their own backyard, linking it to the article's explanation of how animals use camouflage for survival. They listen to their peers' contributions and may offer brief comments or ask simple clarifying questions.
b
I can participate in a discussion by sharing my ideas when asked. I can listen to what others have to say.
Ex. In a partner discussion about a story's plot, a student responds to their partner's prompts by sharing their favorite part of the story and explaining why they liked it. They listen attentively as their partner shares their thoughts and may offer nonverbal cues like nodding or smiling to show engagement.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can bring a picture or note to a discussion and share one idea with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can participate in group discussions about a story or topic. I can share my ideas and connect them to what others say. I can listen to others and wait my turn to talk. I can answer questions and figure out the main point of the discussion.
I can During a class discussion about a story with a moral, the student shares a personal experience that relates to the message of the story. They listen attentively to their classmates' ideas and respond by agreeing or respectfully disagreeing, providing reasons for their viewpoint. They can answer questions about specific characters or events and summarize the main points of the discussion.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can participate in group discussions by sharing my ideas and listening to others. I can answer simple questions about what was discussed.
I can During a group discussion about a class field trip, the student shares their favorite part of the trip and listens as others share their experiences. They can answer simple questions about what they learned or observed during the trip.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can participate in a group discussion by answering yes/no questions or pointing to pictures related to the topic.
I can During a circle time discussion about pets, the student points to a picture of a dog when asked if they have a pet dog. They can nod their head "yes" when asked if they like animals.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions (e.g., gaining attention in respectful ways, actively listening, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
ee_text: Listen to others’ ideas before responding and gain attention respectfully.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I consistently and thoughtfully demonstrate respect for the speaker and contribute to a positive and productive discussion environment. I can not only follow established discussion norms but also help to maintain them by respectfully redirecting others when needed.
Ex. A student notices a classmate is not getting a chance to speak during a lively group discussion. They politely interject, "I think Sarah has something to add to this point," ensuring everyone feels heard and respected.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I follow agreed-upon rules for discussions, such as raising my hand to speak, listening attentively to others, and staying on topic. I can participate appropriately in different types of discussions.
Ex. During a teacher-led discussion, a student patiently waits their turn to speak, raises their hand to be recognized, and makes a relevant comment about the text being discussed. They maintain eye contact with the speaker and demonstrate active listening through nonverbal cues.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am learning to follow the rules for discussions. I can raise my hand to speak and try to listen to others. I am getting better at staying on topic.
Ex. In a small group discussion, a student may sometimes interrupt or get off-topic, but they are learning to self-correct with gentle reminders from the teacher or classmates. They are beginning to understand the importance of giving others a chance to speak and listening respectfully.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in discussions by listening to the teacher and my classmates. I am learning to wait my turn to speak.
