Ex. During a whole-class discussion, a student sits quietly on the rug, listening to the teacher and classmates share their ideas. They may need reminders to raise their hand before speaking but are making an effort to follow classroom discussion norms
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can take turns in discussions with others.
I can address comments to peers when taking turns in a structured activity.
I can Wait for a peer to finish speaking before adding own comments through two cycles of turns.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, take turns in structured discussions with others.
I can when the teacher is the partner and deliberately reminds students, “Wait until I am finished,” wait to add comments until after the teacher is finished.
I can when engaged in structured small group interaction with a talking stick being passed from one member to another, listen while others talk and only speak when the talking stick is in their hands.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can participate in discussions.
I can respond to peers’ communications to them by looking in the direction of the speaker and nodding.
I can use a single message voice output device to say, “Who has more to say?” during a group discussion.
I can use a sequenced message device to participate in an interaction about an activity in the classroom using social scripts.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.
ee_text: Answer specific questions related to information in a discussion.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically ask insightful questions to clarify ambiguities, delve deeper into complex ideas, and propel the discussion forward. I can clearly articulate my own ideas in a way that connects to the points made by others, creating a cohesive and enriching discussion.
Ex. During a discussion about a scientific article on climate change, a student asks, "The article mentions rising sea levels. What are some specific impacts this could have on coastal communities?" This question encourages deeper thinking about the real-world implications of the information presented.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can ask questions to better understand what others are saying and make comments that connect to the discussion. I can explain my thinking and respond to questions from my classmates and teacher.
Ex. In a literature circle, a student asks a classmate, "You mentioned that you think the main character made a brave choice. Can you give an example from the text that made you think that?" They then respond to another student's comment by saying, "I agree with you that the setting was important because..."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can ask questions to get more information or help when I don't understand something. I can make comments that relate to what others are saying.
Ex. During a class discussion about a historical event, a student raises their hand to ask, "What does 'rebellion' mean?" After listening to the teacher's explanation, they make a comment connecting it to a character from a book they read who also rebelled against authority.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can ask questions when I need help understanding something. I can make comments related to the topic being discussed.
Ex. In a small group discussing a story, a student asks their partner, "What happened after...?" They may need prompting to elaborate on their thinking but can make simple connections between their ideas and the story.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask and answer questions about information presented by others.
I can respond to teacher’s question about peer’s story, “Are most tomatoes bigger than a basketball?” with “No!” when teacher says, “What do you want to know?,” the student says, “Is that real?”
I can after a peer completes a class presentation about a state hero, ask, “What happened to him?” The peer says, “He won the war. Do you remember the name of the war?,” students answer.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can ask and answer questions about the topic.
I can While looking at a picture of the big tomato a classmate is sharing, ask, “Can you eat it?”
I can While looking at a picture from a peer’s class presentation about a state hero such as a fireman, point to the picture of the hose when asked, “Where is the hero’s tools/equipment?”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, answer questions about the topic.
I can While looking at a picture of the big tomato a classmate is sharing, the teacher asks, “What do you do with a tomato?,” point to eat as a correct answer.
I can While looking at a picture from a peer’s class presentation about a state hero such as a fireman, point to the picture of the hose when asked, “Where is the hero’s tools/equipment?”

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
ee_text: Identify the key ideas in a discussion.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can accurately identify and synthesize the most important ideas presented during a discussion, analyzing areas of agreement and disagreement. I can reflect on how the discussion has shaped or evolved my own understanding, articulating nuanced insights and connections.
Ex. After a debate about the ethics of zoos, a student summarizes the main arguments presented by both sides, acknowledging the validity of opposing viewpoints. They then reflect on their own shifting perspective, explaining how hearing different perspectives prompted them to consider the complexities of animal welfare and conservation efforts.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can summarize the main points of a discussion and explain how my own ideas have changed or developed based on what I heard.
Ex. At the end of a literature circle, a student summarizes the group's discussion about a character's motivations, highlighting key points of agreement and disagreement. They then share how their initial interpretation of the character's actions has evolved after hearing their classmates' perspectives.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some of the main ideas from a discussion and explain how my thinking connects to what others have said.
Ex. After a class discussion about a scientific concept, a student can recall a few key points made by their classmates. They can then explain how the discussion helped them understand the concept better or connected to something they already knew.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in a discussion and share my ideas. I can listen to what others have to say and identify some key points.
Ex. At the end of a small group activity, a student can retell some of the things their classmates shared. They may need prompting to articulate their own takeaways but can demonstrate basic comprehension of the main ideas discussed.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the key ideas of the discussion.
I can Use a voice output system to say, “big, tomato, farm market.”
I can Point to an illustration in a science textbook to identify the topic of a discussion.
I can Say, “the characters” when asked, “What part of the book are we talking about?”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify one idea presented in the discussion.
I can Point to or eye gaze to a picture of the big tomato from an array of pictures of various vegetables.
I can Use multiple message voice output device to select a symbol that represents one idea in a discussion.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify the topic of the discussion.
I can Select from two illustrations showing topics of the discussion (e.g., when the teacher says, “We are talking about Amy’s trip to the farmer’s market. What did she say she saw?” Then, holds up and labels two pictures, the student eye gazes to the picture of the tomato.).
I can During a small group literature circle discussion, point to the appropriate book when a peer holds up two books and asks, “What book are we talking about?”

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats.
ee_text: Ask and answer questions about details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can accurately and succinctly paraphrase complex information from a variety of sources, demonstrating a sophisticated understanding of the main ideas and supporting details. I can flexibly adapt my paraphrasing technique to suit different contexts and purposes.
Ex. After listening to a podcast about the migratory patterns of monarch butterflies, a student accurately summarizes the key factors influencing their migration, using their own words and providing specific examples from the podcast to support their paraphrase.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can retell information I have heard or seen in my own words, using details to support my understanding. I can paraphrase information from different sources, like books, videos, and presentations.
Ex. After watching a documentary about the rainforest, a student can explain the concept of deforestation in their own words, describing the process and its impact on the environment. They can support their paraphrase with details from the documentary, such as the images and statistics presented.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can retell some of the important information from a text or presentation in my own words. I am learning to use more details when I paraphrase.
Ex. After listening to a chapter from a historical novel read aloud, a student can retell the main events in their own words, focusing on the key characters and their actions. They may need some prompting to include specific details or clarify their understanding.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify some of the key details from a text or presentation. I am learning to retell information in my own words.
Ex. After listening to a short story, a student can identify the main characters and setting. With some support, they can retell a few key events in their own words, focusing on the basic plot elements.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the main idea of a text presented through diverse media.
I can after listening to a peer read a text that is projected on an interactive whiteboard, identify the main idea from choices presented at the end of the book.
I can after seeing a video clip of a pumpkin growing in slow motion, state main idea, “pumpkins grow in stages.”
I can after seeing a video clip of a pumpkin growing in slow motion, use a multiple message voice output device to say, “pumpkins grow.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify details from a text presented through diverse media.
I can after seeing a video clip of a pumpkin growing in slow motion, identify details from the video (e.g., seed, stem, leaves, pumpkin).
I can after listening to a peer read a text that is projected on an interactive whiteboard, sort pictures into boxes of those that are details from the story and those that are not.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify the topic of a text presented through diverse media.
I can after watching with focused attention to a video clip of showing a pumpkin growing in slow motion, point to a picture of a pumpkin from an array of choices when asked, “What was that movie about?”
I can after listening to a peer read a text that is projected on an interactive whiteboard, point to a picture from an array that represents the topic of the book.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)
descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can paraphrase longer parts of a text or presentation accurately and explain the key points.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can paraphrase parts of a text read aloud or information presented in different media.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can retell one part of what I heard in my own words using a sentence frame.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can repeat one detail I heard with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can ask and answer questions about details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or in other media.

descriptor_flag_note: EE descriptor describes identifying the main idea, not asking and answering questions about details.

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
ee_text: Identify a point that the speaker makes.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can critically analyze a speaker's message, identifying both explicit and implicit claims and evaluating the relevance, sufficiency, and credibility of the evidence presented. I can differentiate between strong and weak arguments, recognizing potential biases and fallacies in reasoning.
Ex. After listening to a debate about the pros and cons of single-use plastics, a student can identify the main arguments presented by each side, analyzing the evidence used to support their claims. They can point out any logical fallacies or biased information presented and explain why certain arguments are more persuasive than others.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the reasons a speaker gives for their opinion and the evidence they use to support it. I can explain how the evidence relates to the speaker's point.
Ex. During a presentation about the importance of recycling, a student can identify the speaker's main points, such as conserving resources and reducing landfill waste. They can then point to specific evidence the speaker used to support these points, such as statistics on landfill capacity and the environmental impact of resource extraction.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some reasons and evidence a speaker uses to support their ideas. I can tell the difference between a reason and evidence.
Ex. After listening to a classmate's presentation about their favorite animal, a student can identify the main reason why their classmate likes the animal, such as its appearance or behavior. They can also point out a piece of evidence the classmate used to support their reason, such as a fact about the animal's diet or habitat.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify some reasons a speaker gives for their ideas. I am learning to identify evidence that supports a speaker's reasons.
Ex. After listening to a teacher read aloud an opinion piece, a student can identify the author's main point of view. With some prompting, they can point out a detail from the text that the author used to support their opinion.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify a point that the speaker makes.
I can Restate in a word or two a point the speaker makes on the topic (e.g., states a reason Fern used to convince her father to keep Wilbur).
I can after listening to a peer present to the class, identify two things the peer said from a list presented with partner-assisted scanning (e.g., The peer reads each item in the list and the student says, “yes” or “no” to indicate if the item was part of what peer said in presentation).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, repeat one point a speaker makes.
I can Repeat a phrase the speaker has said when asked (e.g., The student points to a picture of one of the messages Charlotte puts on her web, such as “some pig”, when asked, “What did Charlotte say that saved Wilbur?”).
I can Select a pre-stored message from an array of choices to repeat a point the speaker makes.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize speaker.
I can Establish eye gaze with speaker.
I can Face toward the speaker.
I can Nod or otherwise acknowledge the speaker.
I can Point to speaker when asked, “Who is speaking?”

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Presentation of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, read a poem, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace. Communicate clearly and in an engaging manner, considering the audience, purpose, and situation.
ee_text: Clearly retell a story, poem, or personal experience or recount a topic with supporting details.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can confidently and effectively deliver well-structured presentations that engage my audience and clearly convey my message. I can adapt my communication style to suit different purposes, audiences, and contexts, demonstrating a keen awareness of how to make my presentations clear, engaging, and memorable.
Ex. A student delivers a presentation about their science fair project, confidently explaining their hypothesis, methodology, and findings using clear and concise language. They incorporate visuals like graphs and diagrams to enhance understanding and engage their audience with anecdotes and real-world applications of their research. They modulate their voice and make eye contact to keep their classmates attentive.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can plan and deliver organized presentations that present information clearly and logically. I can use facts, details, and examples to support my main points. I can adjust my speaking volume and pace to be easily understood.
Ex. A student shares a personal narrative about a memorable family vacation. They use chronological order to structure their story, incorporating vivid descriptions and sensory details to bring their experience to life. They speak clearly and at an appropriate pace, making eye contact with their audience and using natural intonation to emphasize key moments in their story.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can present information about a topic or text in a somewhat organized way. I can use some facts and details to support my ideas. I am working on speaking clearly and at an appropriate pace.
Ex. A student gives a report on a book they read, summarizing the main events and characters. They may sometimes lose their train of thought or struggle to provide specific details. They may speak too quickly or quietly at times but are making an effort to improve their pacing and volume.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can share information about a topic or experience with others. I am learning to use details to support my ideas. I am working on speaking clearly and being understood.
Ex. A student recounts a recent event they attended, such as a school play or a sporting event. They may rely heavily on visual aids or prompts from the teacher. They may speak in short, simple sentences and need encouragement to speak louder or slower, but they are making an effort to share their thoughts and ideas.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell a story about a personal experience with supporting details.
I can Using a sign, tell about the puppy arriving at home, including details about the first encounter with the puppy (e.g., “We got a puppy at the store. He rode next to me in the car. He jumped on me. We played a lot.”).
I can Before writing, tell the teacher what they are going to write about (e.g., The student says, “I went to the party. Grandma Red Hat party. Aunt Stephanie and I have a party. I got a new dress.”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recount a personal experience including details.
I can use a multiple message voice output device, and select three symbols to show how he or she made the cookies (e.g., mix, cook, oven).
I can use a multiple voice output communication device to report on weekend activities during a morning meeting (e.g., The student says, “Shopping with mom. Shoes, DVD, lunch.”).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify a picture, object, or other artifact from a personal experience.
I can given an array of pictures, point to the appropriate picture when the teacher says, “You got a new puppy? Show me the picture of your new puppy.”
I can given a display of class art projects, identify own project.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Presentation of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Integrate audio and visual content in presentations to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
ee_text: Add audio recordings or visuals to a presentation about a personally relevant topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can thoughtfully select and seamlessly integrate a variety of engaging and informative audio and visual elements into my presentations. I can strategically use these elements to clarify complex information, create emotional impact, and enhance my audience's understanding and retention of key themes.
Ex. For a presentation about endangered species, a student incorporates a variety of multimedia elements: a short video clip showcasing the beauty and diversity of a coral reef, ambient ocean sounds to set the mood, and graphs illustrating the alarming rate of coral bleaching due to climate change. They seamlessly transition between these elements, using them to create an impactful and memorable presentation that inspires action.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use audio and visual elements in my presentations to make them more interesting and engaging. I can choose visuals and sounds that support my main points and help my audience understand the topic.
Ex. A student presenting a report on a historical event creates a slideshow with relevant images, such as maps, portraits of key figures, and photographs of important artifacts. They choose appropriate background music to set the tone and use bullet points to highlight key facts and dates.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can include pictures, diagrams, or other visuals in my presentations. I am learning to choose visuals that relate to my topic and help explain my ideas.
Ex. A student giving a presentation about their favorite hobby, such as playing a musical instrument or collecting stamps, brings in examples to show the class. They may also include a few simple pictures or drawings in their presentation to illustrate their points.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use visuals to communicate my ideas. I am learning to connect pictures and objects to the topic I am presenting.
Ex. A student sharing a story they wrote chooses a few pictures from magazines or online to accompany their storytelling. They may need help from the teacher to explain how the pictures relate to their story and engage the audience.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can add audio recordings or visuals to a presentation about a personally relevant topic.
I can select pictures from a family vacation, label the pictures (e.g., people’s names and places) and sequence them for a presentation.
I can select objects from a collection (e.g., toys, rocks, videos) and select words from a multiple message communication device to go with each object to use in a presentation.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can select pictures, objects, or artifacts or label pictures, objects, or artifacts to contribute to a simple presentation about a personally relevant topic.
I can work with a small group, create a presentation about a class activity (e.g., Creating a presentation about a class trip to a diamond mine, the student selects a sieve, trowel, and diamond chip for the group to include in the presentation.).
I can work with other family members, select pictures of members of the family to show during a presentation about family.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can select a picture, object, or artifact from an array of options to add to a class-created presentation about a personally relevant topic.
I can select favorite picture of the new puppy to add to the presentation Our Pets created by the class.
I can select a favorite food item from an array to add to a class presentation Our Favorite Things created by the class.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Knowledge of Language
text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. a. Compare and contrast the ways in which language is used in familiar and unfamiliar contexts (e.g., at home, outside of their own communities, by diverse authors and speakers).
ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. Use language to express emotion.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can astutely analyze and compare how language use varies across different cultures, contexts, and disciplines. I can explain these variations, recognizing how factors like regional background, cultural norms, and the purpose of communication influence language choices. I can apply this understanding to navigate unfamiliar language situations effectively and appreciate the nuances of diverse communication styles.
Ex. A student notices that a character in a novel uses a regional dialect with unique vocabulary and grammatical structures. They compare this dialect to their own way of speaking, identifying similarities and differences in pronunciation, word choice, and grammar. They research the history and cultural significance of the dialect, recognizing how language reflects the character's identity and background.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify differences in how people speak and write depending on where they are from, who they are talking to, and what they are talking about. I can use this knowledge to understand what I read and hear better.
Ex. A student listens to a speaker use formal language and a serious tone during a presentation at a history museum. They compare this to the more casual language and humorous tone used by a tour guide leading a group of children at the same museum. They understand that the speaker's language is appropriate for the formal setting and audience, while the tour guide's language is more engaging for a younger audience.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can recognize that people use different words and ways of speaking in different situations. I can start to explain why these differences exist.
Ex. A student notices that their grandparents use some old-fashioned expressions that they don't usually hear. They can point out these differences and understand that language changes over time. They might also recognize that people from different parts of the country or world speak the same language with different accents and vocabulary.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can hear and recognize differences in how people speak. I am learning that people use different words and phrases depending on the situation.
Ex. A student notices that their teacher speaks differently when reading a story aloud compared to when giving instructions for an assignment. They can identify that the teacher's voice changes and that they use different words and phrases in each situation.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use words and phrases to clearly tell others how I feel.
I can Instead of simply saying "I'm mad," the student might say, "I feel frustrated because I was playing with that toy and now it's broken." They might also use expressive language like, "I'm over the moon!" to express excitement.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use a few different words to tell others how I feel. I can use my words and my body to show how I feel.
I can The student can use words like "happy," "sad," "mad," or "scared" to label their emotions. They might combine these words with facial expressions or gestures to further communicate their feelings.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use facial expressions or gestures to show how I feel. I am learning to use words to name my feelings.
I can The student might smile when they are happy, frown when they are sad, or cover their eyes when they are scared. They are beginning to connect these expressions with simple emotion words.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Knowledge of Language
text: Determine the language demands of varied writing and speaking situations; respond appropriately (e.g., formal writing and presentations; personal writing and conversations)
ee_text: Notice the differences in language between formal and informal situations.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can confidently analyze the audience, purpose, and context of a writing or speaking task to determine the appropriate level of formality, tone, and language choices. I can seamlessly adapt my language to suit a wide range of situations, demonstrating a sophisticated understanding of how to craft effective and appropriate communication.
Ex. A student writing a persuasive letter to the school principal requesting funding for a new playground understands the need for formal language, a respectful tone, and a well-organized argument supported by evidence. However, when writing a story for their classmates, they use more informal language, vivid imagery, and a conversational tone to engage their peers.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the audience and purpose of my writing and speaking. I can choose appropriate language and tone for different situations, such as writing a report for school or telling a story to a friend.
Ex. A student giving an oral report on a science topic uses clear and factual language, avoiding slang or informal expressions. They understand that the purpose of the report is to inform their classmates and teacher, so they choose language that is appropriate for the academic setting.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can recognize that there are different ways to speak and write depending on who I am talking to and what I am talking about. I am learning to choose more appropriate language for different situations.
Ex. A student writing a thank-you note to their grandmother for a birthday gift understands that they should use polite language and express their gratitude sincerely. They may still need some guidance on using more formal letter-writing conventions, but they are beginning to grasp the concept of audience and purpose in writing.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can adjust my volume and tone of voice depending on the situation. I am learning that there are different ways to talk to different people.
Ex. A student understands that they should use a quieter voice when talking in the library than on the playground. They are also beginning to recognize that they might use different words and phrases when talking to a teacher than when talking to a friend.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify language that is used in different situations. I can tell the difference between language used with friends and language used with adults or in school.
I can identify that using slang or informal language with friends is appropriate, but they would use more polite and complete sentences when talking to the principal or a guest speaker.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify different ways people talk in different places. I know that we sometimes use different voices when we talk.
I can recognize that people might speak more quietly in a library than on a playground. They can identify that they might use a louder, more excited voice when talking to friends than when talking to a teacher.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can change the way I talk when someone tells me to use my "inside voice" or my "listening ears."
I can The student can adjust their volume and tone when reminded to use their "inside voice" in the classroom. They can demonstrate active listening skills when told to use their "listening ears" during a lesson.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Knowledge of Language
text: Identify examples of precise and concise language when reading; choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely when writing and speaking.
ee_text: Communicate effectively with peers and adults.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can discern subtle differences between words with similar meanings and select the most precise and nuanced language to convey my ideas effectively. I can identify and utilize literary devices, figurative language, and technical vocabulary to enhance my writing and speaking, making it clear, engaging, and impactful.
Ex. A student, writing a poem about a bird taking flight, chooses the verb "ascended" instead of "went up" to create a more vivid and powerful image in the reader's mind. They recognize how specific word choices can evoke emotions, create imagery, and convey subtle shades of meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can choose words and phrases carefully to make my writing and speaking clear and interesting. I can identify words that are specific and descriptive when I read.
Ex. A student, describing a character in a story, uses adjectives like "resourceful" and "empathetic" instead of generic terms like "good" or "nice." They understand that these specific words paint a clearer picture of the character's personality for the reader.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use descriptive words in my writing and speaking. I am learning to choose words that are more specific and interesting.
Ex. A student, writing a report about a historical event, uses words like "rebellion" or "treaty" instead of more general terms like "fight" or "agreement." They are beginning to understand that using specific vocabulary can make their writing more accurate and engaging.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use different words to describe things. I am learning to choose words that make my meaning clear.
Ex. A student, recounting an experience, uses words like "gigantic" or "tiny" instead of just "big" or "small." They are starting to experiment with using more descriptive language to make their storytelling more interesting.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can communicate my ideas and needs clearly to my friends and to adults. I can listen to others and respond appropriately in conversations.
I can The student can clearly explain a game idea to a group of friends, taking turns speaking and listening to suggestions. They can also confidently ask a teacher for help with an assignment, using appropriate language and tone.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can talk to my friends and teachers about familiar topics. I can usually understand what others are saying to me and respond appropriately.
I can The student can participate in conversations about shared interests like books, movies, or hobbies. They can follow simple instructions and ask for clarification when needed.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use words, gestures, and pictures to communicate my basic needs and ideas. I can participate in short conversations with familiar adults.
I can The student can tell a teacher when they need to use the restroom or get a drink of water. They can answer simple questions about themselves and their interests.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Knowledge of Language
text: Choose punctuation for effect.
ee_text: Choose appropriate punctuation.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically use a variety of punctuation marks to enhance the rhythm, flow, and clarity of my writing. I can experiment with punctuation to create specific effects, such as building suspense, emphasizing key ideas, or conveying a character's emotions.
Ex. A student writing a suspenseful story uses a series of short, declarative sentences followed by ellipses to build tension and create a sense of anticipation: "The door creaked open slowly... A cold breeze swept through the room... Silence."
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use punctuation correctly to make my writing clear and easy to understand. I can use punctuation like commas, dashes, and parentheses to add information or make my meaning clear.
Ex. A student writing a report on their favorite animal uses parentheses to include additional facts and details: "The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is the fastest land animal, capable of reaching speeds up to 70 miles per hour (112 kilometers per hour)."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use basic punctuation marks, like periods, commas, and question marks, correctly most of the time. I am learning to use other punctuation marks to make my writing more interesting.
Ex. A student writing a friendly letter remembers to use a comma after the greeting ("Dear Grandma,") and closing ("Love, [Name]"). They might also experiment with using an exclamation point to express excitement or strong emotion.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use periods to end my sentences. I am learning to use other punctuation marks to separate ideas and make my writing clear.
Ex. A student writing a simple story uses periods at the end of each sentence. They might occasionally forget to use a capital letter at the beginning of a new sentence, but they are developing an understanding of how punctuation helps to organize their writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use comparative and superlative adjectives to describe people or objects.
I can use a superlative to describe a choice of objects (e.g., “Can I have the biggest one?”).
I can describe a snack and says, “This one is the best.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use adjectives to describe familiar objects.
I can point to the color blue to describe a backpack.
I can Says “big” to describe the ball in physical therapy.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize objects based on simple descriptions.
I can follow instructions from a teacher such as, “Can you give me the red one?”
I can follow instruction when asked to sit in the big chair.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)
descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can choose punctuation such as exclamation marks, commas or ellipses on purpose and explain the effect.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can choose punctuation for effect in my writing.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can choose a period, question mark or exclamation mark for a sentence with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can find the end mark in a sentence with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can choose the right punctuation for a sentence.

descriptor_flag_note: EE descriptor describes comparative and superlative adjectives, not choosing punctuation.

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. a. Use context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. a. Use context as a clue to guide selection of a word that completes a sentence read aloud by an adult.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use context clues effectively to infer the nuanced meanings of unfamiliar words and phrases, even in complex or ambiguous texts. I can identify and analyze different types of context clues, such as definitions, examples, synonyms, antonyms, and logic, to determine the most likely meaning of a word or phrase.
Ex. A student encounters the word "ephemeral" in a poem about the changing seasons. While the word is unfamiliar, they use clues from the surrounding lines, which describe the fleeting beauty of autumn leaves and the transient nature of time, to infer that "ephemeral" means something that is short-lived or temporary.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use clues in the text to figure out the meaning of an unknown word or phrase. I can identify words or sentences around the unknown word that give hints about its meaning.
Ex. A student comes across the word "nocturnal" in a nonfiction book about animals. The text describes nocturnal animals as those that are "active at night and sleep during the day." Using this information, the student correctly infers that "nocturnal" means related to or occurring at night.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can sometimes use clues in the text to figure out what a word means. I am learning to look for words and sentences that might tell me the meaning of an unknown word.
Ex. A student encounters the word "cautious" in a story. The sentence reads, "The cautious rabbit slowly hopped out of its burrow, looking around carefully for any danger." The student might need some prompting to focus on the phrases "slowly hopped" and "looking around carefully" to understand that "cautious" means being careful and avoiding danger.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can sometimes figure out what a word means by looking at the pictures or asking for help. I am learning to look for clues in the text that can help me understand the meaning of a word.
Ex. A student is unsure of the word "gigantic" in a story. The illustration shows a very large monster. With some guidance, the student can connect the picture to the word and understand that "gigantic" means extremely large.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can capitalize the first word in a sentence.
I can answer when the teacher is writing the morning message and stops to ask, “How do I start?” The student responds, “Start with a capital letter.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, indicate that the first word in a sentence must be capitalized.
I can answer when the teacher is writing the morning message and stops to ask, “What do I need to do to that first word in the sentence?” The student responds, “Capital.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, indicate a letter that is capitalized.
I can recognize the first letter in their name when it is capitalized.
I can given two choices, identify (pointing, eye gaze, etc.) the capital letter.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can use several kinds of context clues to work out and check the meaning of new words and phrases.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can use the words around a new word to guess its meaning with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can use a picture to work out a new word with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can use context to choose a word that completes a sentence read aloud by an adult.

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Consult print and digital reference materials for meaning and pronunciation.
ee_text: Use frequently occurring root words (e.g., talk) and the words that result when word endings are added (e.g., talked, talking, talks).

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can skillfully navigate and utilize a variety of print and digital reference materials, such as dictionaries, thesauruses, online encyclopedias, and subject-specific databases, to deepen my understanding of word meanings, pronunciations, and etymologies. I can critically evaluate information from different sources to ensure its accuracy and relevance.
Ex. A student writing a report about ancient Egypt encounters the word "hieroglyphics." They use an online dictionary to find the definition ("a system of writing using picture symbols") and pronunciation (/ˌhaɪərəˈɡlɪfɪks/). They then consult an encyclopedia for more detailed information about the history and use of hieroglyphics in ancient Egyptian culture.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use a dictionary or glossary to find the meaning and pronunciation of an unknown word. I can also use online resources like dictionaries and encyclopedias to find information about words.
Ex. A student is reading a story and comes across the word "exuberant." They use a print dictionary to find the definition ("filled with or characterized by a lively energy and excitement"). They then practice pronouncing the word correctly, paying attention to the syllable stress.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use a dictionary to find the meaning of a word. I am learning to use other reference materials, like a glossary or thesaurus.
Ex. A student is confused about the meaning of the word "habitat" in a science textbook. They use the glossary at the back of the book to find a definition and an example sentence to clarify its meaning.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can ask for help when I don't know how to say or what a word means. I am learning to use a dictionary to find the meaning of a word.
Ex. A student encounters an unfamiliar word in a book. They ask their teacher for help pronouncing the word and understanding its meaning. The teacher then guides them in using a children's dictionary to find the word and its definition.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use different forms of a word correctly when I am speaking and writing. I understand how adding endings to a word can change its meaning.
I can The student can accurately use words like "talked," "talking," and "talks" in sentences, demonstrating their understanding of how the added endings change the tense or form of the base word "talk." They can also apply this understanding to other common root words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use some different forms of a word correctly when I am speaking. I am learning how adding endings to a word can change its meaning.
I can The student may sometimes make mistakes when using different forms of a word in their writing, but they are generally able to use them correctly in their speech. They are beginning to recognize patterns in how endings change the meaning of words.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize the same word when it is used in different ways. I am learning that adding letters to the end of a word can change its meaning.
I can The student can identify that "talk," "talked," and "talking" are all related to the same concept, even though they look and sound slightly different. They are beginning to explore how adding letters to the end of words can change their meaning.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings. a. Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as similes and metaphors.
ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and use. a. Determine the literal meaning of words and phrases in context.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze the author's craft in using figurative language, such as similes, metaphors, personification, and hyperbole, to create imagery, convey emotions, and enhance meaning in both literary and informational texts. I can explain the intended effect of these figurative language choices on the reader.
Ex. A student reads the line "The old house stood on the hill like a watchful sentinel" and recognizes the simile comparing the house to a sentinel. They understand that this comparison suggests the house is solitary, imposing, and possibly a bit ominous, adding to the overall mood of the story.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify similes and metaphors in texts and explain how they create meaning. I can explain how an author uses figurative language to make their writing more interesting or to help the reader visualize something.
Ex. A student reads the sentence "Her heart was a drum pounding in her chest" and identifies it as a metaphor. They can explain that the author is comparing the character's heart to a drum to emphasize her nervousness or excitement.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify similes and metaphors in texts. I am learning to explain what these figures of speech mean and how they relate to the text.
Ex. A student reads the phrase "quiet as a mouse" and recognizes it as a simile. They can explain that it means someone is being very quiet, but they might need some prompting to connect it to the specific context of the story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize some common figures of speech, like similes and metaphors. I am learning to identify the words that signal figurative language.
Ex. A student can identify a simile like "brave as a lion" and understand that it means someone is very brave. They might need help identifying metaphors or explaining the connection between the two things being compared.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use language to express emotion.
I can initiate language to express an emotion related to an activity or experience.
I can use the appropriate words to communicate an emotion (e.g., mad, sad, happy).
I can select a word from my choices to communicate emotion.
I can respond by using an appropriate word that expresses an emotion when asked, “How did that make you feel?”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use words, pictures, or symbols to communicate.
I can when given a choice of two photographs, select one to communicate an emotion.
I can respond by using a word that expresses an emotion when asked, “How did that make you feel?”
I can during a shared reading activity when asked “How does <character’s name> feel about this?” point to an illustration in the book that shows the character’s emotion.
I can when asked a question by the teacher, “How does that make you feel, happy, sad, or scared?,” the student responds with one of the choices by pointing or gazing to a symbol or saying the word.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify words, pictures, or symbols that communicate emotions.
I can respond when others express happiness.
I can identify a picture or symbol that is used to indicate happiness.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)
descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain what similes and metaphors mean and how they help the reader picture an idea.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text, including similes and metaphors.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can explain a simple simile using a picture or example.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a phrase is silly or real with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can determine the literal meaning of words and phrases in context.

descriptor_flag_note: EE descriptor describes expressing emotion, not literal word meaning.

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Explain common idioms and proverbs.
ee_text: Use common idioms (e.g., no way, not a chance, you bet, it’s a deal, we're cool)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can interpret and explain the figurative meanings of idioms and proverbs, recognizing their cultural significance and analyzing how they convey universal truths or insights about human nature. I can use idioms and proverbs effectively in my own speaking and writing to add color, humor, or wisdom.
Ex. A student hears the proverb "Don't judge a book by its cover" and can explain its meaning: We shouldn't make assumptions about people or things based solely on their outward appearance. They can relate this proverb to personal experiences or other stories where judging based on appearances proved to be misleading.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can explain the meaning of common idioms and proverbs. I can understand that these expressions have a figurative meaning that is different from the literal meaning of the words.
Ex. A student encounters the idiom "spill the beans" in a story. They understand that it means to reveal a secret and can use context clues to figure out what secret was revealed in the story.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can recognize some common idioms and proverbs. I am learning to understand that these expressions have a different meaning than what the words literally say.
Ex. A student hears the idiom "raining cats and dogs" and understands that it means it's raining very heavily, even though they might not be able to articulate the origin or figurative meaning of the phrase.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I am learning about idioms and proverbs. I can sometimes understand the meaning of these expressions when I hear them.
Ex. A student hears the proverb "Honesty is the best policy" and, with some explanation, can understand that it means it's important to tell the truth.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can understand and use common idioms correctly in my conversations. I know that these phrases have a different meaning than their individual words.
I can The student can use the idiom "it's a deal" to express agreement or make a bargain with a friend. They understand that this phrase doesn't literally mean there is a business transaction taking place.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can understand some common idioms when I hear them. I am learning to use these phrases in my conversations.
I can The student understands the meaning of idioms like "no way" and "you bet" when they hear them in context, but they might not feel confident using them independently yet.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I am starting to notice that some phrases have a different meaning than the words themselves. I am curious about idioms and what they mean.
I can The student might ask what "spill the beans" means when they hear it for the first time. They are beginning to recognize that language can be playful and have multiple layers of meaning.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Understand words by relating them to synonyms and antonyms.
ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of opposites.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically use my knowledge of synonyms and antonyms to enhance my vocabulary, improve my reading comprehension, and express myself with greater precision and nuance. I can identify subtle differences in meaning between synonyms and choose the most appropriate word to convey my intended meaning.
Ex. A student, writing a story about a courageous character, wants to find a more descriptive synonym for "brave." They consult a thesaurus and consider options like "valiant," "intrepid," and "audacious," ultimately choosing the word that best reflects the specific type of bravery exhibited by the character.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify synonyms and antonyms for common words. I can use synonyms to avoid repetition in my writing and antonyms to show contrast between ideas.
Ex. A student is writing a report about the rainforest and wants to vary their word choice instead of repeating "big" several times. They use a thesaurus to find synonyms like "massive," "enormous," and "gigantic" to make their writing more interesting and precise.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify words that mean the same thing (synonyms) and words that mean the opposite (antonyms). I am learning to use synonyms and antonyms in my writing.
Ex. A student is working on a vocabulary list with the words "happy" and "sad." They can identify "joyful" as a synonym for "happy" and "dejected" as an antonym for "happy."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I am learning about synonyms and antonyms. I can match words that have the same or opposite meanings.
Ex. A student is given a worksheet with pairs of words, such as "hot/cold" and "big/small." They can successfully match the pairs as antonyms.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can communicate effectively with peers and adults.
I can communicate reactions to statements made by others.
I can answer questions from peers and adults about self or joint activities.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can communicate with adults.
I can respond when addressed by an adult.
I can answer questions from adults about self or current activity.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can use words, pictures, symbols, or sign to communicate.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can choose precise synonyms and antonyms to make my writing more exact and interesting.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can understand words by relating them to their synonyms and antonyms.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can match a word to a synonym or antonym using a chart.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can match a word to its opposite picture with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can show I understand opposites, such as hot and cold.

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Make connections between words and how they are used in real life (i.e., help students build or add onto existing schema when encountering new words).
ee_text: Identify words that describe personal emotional states.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can actively connect new words and concepts to my prior knowledge and experiences, creating meaningful associations that deepen my understanding and retention. I can analyze how word choices reflect different perspectives, contexts, and purposes in real-world communication.
Ex. A student learning the word "migration" in a science unit on birds can connect it to their family's annual summer vacation trip, understanding that both involve a temporary movement from one place to another. They can further analyze how "migration" is used differently in social studies to describe human movements.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can relate new words to things I already know. I can use my own experiences and background knowledge to understand the meaning of unfamiliar words.
Ex. A student encounters the word "architect" in a book about famous buildings. They connect it to their uncle, who designs houses, and can now visualize an architect's role in creating structures.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can sometimes make connections between new words and things I have seen or done. I am learning to use my own experiences to understand new words.
Ex. A student learning the word "generous" hears a story about a child sharing their toys. With some prompting, they can connect the character's actions to the word and understand that "generous" means being willing to share.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I am learning to connect words to pictures and objects. I am starting to understand that words have meanings related to the world around me.
Ex. A student learning the word "transportation" is shown pictures of cars, buses, and airplanes. They can start to connect the word to different ways people move from place to place.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify and understand words that describe different feelings. I can use these words to talk about my own emotions and the emotions of others.
I can accurately identify words like "frustrated," "excited," "disappointed," and "proud" as words that describe feelings. They can use these words to talk about their own emotional experiences and to infer the feelings of characters in stories.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify words that describe basic feelings like happy, sad, mad, and scared. I am learning more words that describe different emotions.
I can match facial expressions to basic emotion words. They are beginning to recognize and use a wider range of emotion vocabulary, such as "surprised," "nervous," or "silly."
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can show how I feel with my face and body. I am learning words to name different feelings.
I can express my emotions through facial expressions, body language, and vocal tone. They are beginning to associate these expressions with basic emotion words like "happy," "sad," "mad," and "scared."

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

subject: ELA
cluster: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
text: Demonstrate an ability to collaboratively and independently build vocabulary knowledge when encountering unknown words including cultural, general academic, and discipline-specific terms and phrases; use vocabulary appropriate to the context and situation. a. Identify and use phrases that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).
ee_text: Use words acquired through conversations, being read to, and during shared reading activities a. Identify key domain-specific vocabulary

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can strategically choose and use precise verbs, adverbs, and descriptive phrases to create vivid imagery, convey nuanced emotions, and enhance the clarity and impact of my writing and speaking. I can confidently incorporate domain-specific vocabulary to demonstrate my understanding of a topic and engage my audience effectively.
Ex. In a persuasive essay about protecting endangered species, a student writes, "Poachers ruthlessly hunt elephants for their ivory tusks, decimating populations and pushing these magnificent creatures to the brink of extinction." The student's use of strong verbs like "ruthlessly" and "decimating" and domain-specific terms like "poachers," "ivory tusks," and "endangered species" demonstrates a sophisticated understanding of the topic and creates a powerful emotional appeal.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify and use words and phrases that describe specific actions, feelings, or states of being. I can use vocabulary related to a topic to show my understanding.
Ex. When writing a story about a nervous character, a student might use verbs like "fidget," "tremble," and "stammer" instead of more general words like "move" or "talk." When discussing a science unit on weather, they accurately use terms like "precipitation," "evaporation," and "condensation."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can choose words that describe actions, feelings, or states of being. I am learning to use more specific and interesting words in my writing and speaking.
Ex. Instead of writing "The dog was happy," a student might write "The dog wagged its tail excitedly." They are beginning to use more descriptive verbs to show rather than tell.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use different words to describe how people are feeling or what they are doing. I am learning new words related to different topics we are studying.
Ex. A student can identify "giggled" as a way to show someone is happy and "cried" as a way to show someone is sad. They are starting to build a vocabulary of words related to specific subjects, like using "habitat" and "ecosystem" in a science lesson.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use context as a clue to guide the selection of a word that completes a sentence read aloud by an adult.
I can select from choices a word to complete a sentence (e.g., The teacher reads a sentence aloud skips one word and asks students to select the missing word from an array of choices.).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use context as a clue to guide the selection of a word that completes a familiar sentence read aloud by an adult. 
I can while listening to a familiar text read aloud, select an appropriate word from choices (e.g., The teacher pauses and offers choices of words that will complete the sentence. Student selects the appropriate word.).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can make choices among familiar words to complete familiar sentences.
I can complete the sentence, “I want <missing word> for lunch.”
I can choose a contextually correct picture to represent an answer to a question about a familiar passage.

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can use precise action words and topic words accurately in my speaking and writing.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can learn and use words that show precise actions and feelings and words basic to a topic.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can use topic words from a word wall in my writing with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can point to a picture of a topic word with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can identify key subject-specific words.

subject: ELA
cluster: Conventions of Standardized English
text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: a. relative pronouns and adverbs;
ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. a. Use possessive pronouns.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can easily change how I talk and write depending on who I'm talking to and what I'm writing about. I can explain why different types of writing and speaking require different ways of using language.
Ex. A student gives a presentation to the class about their favorite hobby, using more formal language and avoiding slang. Later, they write a note to a friend about a funny event at recess, using informal language and humor. They can explain that they adjusted their language to fit the audience and purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use the correct grammar and punctuation when I write and speak for different situations. I can choose the right words and phrases to make my meaning clear.
Ex. A student writes a story using correct punctuation, capitalization, and grammar. They use different types of sentences (simple, compound, complex) to make their writing interesting.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am learning to use the right grammar and punctuation when I write and speak. I am getting better at choosing words that fit the situation.
Ex. A student is learning to use commas in a series and to capitalize proper nouns. They are starting to use more descriptive words in their writing, but sometimes they still choose words that don't quite fit.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I am learning about grammar and punctuation. I am starting to understand that we use different kinds of words when we write and speak.
Ex. A student can identify the beginning and end of a sentence. They are learning about different parts of speech, like nouns and verbs.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use many different grammar rules to write clear and interesting sentences.
Example: "My dog, Sparky, is smaller than my neighbor's dog, but Sparky runs faster than any dog I know!"
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can write simple sentences and am learning to use more interesting words to compare things and show how they are related.
Example: "My dog is small. He runs fast!"
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I am learning about how to build sentences and can use some words to talk about who owns things, where things are, and compare things.
Example: "My dog. Run fast!"

source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)
descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can use relative pronouns and adverbs to combine ideas into complex sentences and explain their purpose.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use relative pronouns (who, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why) correctly.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can join two sentences with who or which using a model.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can answer a who question about a picture with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can use possessive pronouns such as my, your, his and her.

subject: ELA
cluster: Conventions of Standardized English
text: Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with prepositional phrases;
ee_text: Combine common nouns with verbs, nouns, or pronouns in communication

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use prepositional phrases like "under the table" or "before the game" in my writing, and explain how they show where or when something happens.
I can create complex sentences using prepositional phrases to add detail.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use prepositional phrases like "on the chair" or "after school" in my writing.
I can explain how prepositional phrases describe where or when something happens.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use simple prepositional phrases like "on the desk" or "at home" with help.
I can explain with support how a prepositional phrase tells where or when.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize and use basic prepositional phrases like "in the room" with help.
I can try to explain what a prepositional phrase shows with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use nouns and verbs together to make sentences, like “The cat runs.”
I can combine nouns with pronouns or other nouns to talk about people, animals, or things.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use a noun and a verb together, like “boy run,” with help.
I can say or point to two words, like a noun and a pronoun, when talking with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can say or point to a noun and verb together, like “boy eat,” with support.
I can use pictures or words to put two things together, like “boy” and “him,” with help.

subject: ELA
cluster: Conventions of Standardized English
text: Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with order of adjective
ee_text: Not applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can correctly use multiple adjectives in the right order, such as "a big red balloon," and explain why they are in that order.
I can vary my use of adjectives to make my writing more descriptive and accurate.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use adjectives in the correct order, such as "a small blue car," in my writing.
I can explain the proper order for adjectives, such as size before color.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use two adjectives like "big" and "yellow" in my writing with help, and I can try to put them in the right order (e.g., "a big yellow ball").
I can explain the order of adjectives with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use simple adjectives like "big" and "small" in my writing with help (e.g., "a small dog").
I can try to put two adjectives together with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable
