I can draw an inference about an informational text (e.g., It is important to know the weather to plan activities for the day.) and select two facts from a weather report that support the inference (e.g., The weather will be sunny in the morning but it will rain in the afternoon.).
I can after reading a narrative on a march with Martin Luther King, select an inference from choices (e.g., The marchers did not want anyone to get hurt.) and choose a related fact stated in the text to support the inference (e.g., The people did not bring guns or clubs.).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can determine which citations demonstrate what the text says explicitly.
I can underline text that tells how a task should be completed.
I can given a statement of what the text says explicitly, find the citation in a teacher-selected portion of the text.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify words from a text.
I can after shared reading of a familiar informational text, respond by nodding or using a switch to identify a statement read aloud as from a familiar informational text.

source: Awsaj G9-10 ELA New Standards 2024 (school sheet)

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: Objectively and accurately summarize texts, from a variety of genres, to determine one or more themes or central ideas and analyze its development, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details. (RI&RL)
ee_text: given the theme or central idea, recount related events and details (including character and setting details for literary texts). (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can objectively and accurately summarize texts from various genres, identifying multiple themes or central ideas and analyzing their development, including how they emerge and are shaped and refined by specific details.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can objectively and accurately summarize texts from a variety of genres to determine one or more themes or central ideas and analyze their development, including how they emerge and are shaped and refined by specific details.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify and summarize the main ideas and details in texts.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recount main events and details from a text and explain how they relate to the theme with some guidance.
I can after reading a story, summarize the main events and discuss how they connect to the theme.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recount related events and details given the theme or central idea (including character and setting details for literary texts).
I can describe the main events and details of a story or article, connecting them to the theme or central idea.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
1I can identify and recount some related events and details with guidance.
I can Identify and summarize key events and details of a text with assistance, relating them to the theme.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance, recount basic related events and details from a text.
I can with help, retell simple events and details from a story or article, and connect them to the theme.

subject: ELA
cluster: Key Ideas & Details
text: In literary texts, analyze how complex and/or dynamic characters develop, interact with other characters, advance the plot, or develop a theme. (RL) In informational texts, analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or argument, including the sequence, the introduction and development of ideas, and the connections that exist. (RI)
ee_text: Determine logical connections between characters, individuals, ideas, or events in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: In literary texts, I can throughly analyze how complex and/or dynamic characters develop, interact with other characters, advance the plot, or develop a theme. In informational texts, I can throughly analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or argument, including the sequence, the introduction and development of ideas, and the connections that exist and provide insightful interpretations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: In literary texts, I can analyze how characters develop, interact with other characters, advance the plot, or develop a theme. In informational texts, I can analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or argument, including the sequence, the introduction and development of ideas, and the connections that exist.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify important dialogue or events in literary texts and explain their basic role, and I can recognize key individuals, events, or ideas in informational texts.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can determine connections between characters, ideas, or events and look for how they affect each other and how they help the story or argument grow.
I can Explain how characters' actions are connected and influence each other with some guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine logical connections between characters, individuals, ideas, or events in a text.
I can Identify and explain how different characters, ideas, or events are connected in a story or informational text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify some connections between characters, ideas, or events with guidance.
I can Recognize and describe basic connections between characters or events with assistance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance, identify simple connections between characters, ideas, or events.
I can with help, point out how two characters or events are related in a story.

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings. Analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood. Examine technical or key terms and how language differs across genres. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in text, including common idioms, analogies, and figures of speech. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can determine the meanings of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings, and analyze their impact on meaning, tone, and mood in a text, examining how language differs across genres.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings, and analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood. I can examine technical or key terms and how language differs across genres.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the meanings of some words and phrases and describe their basic effect on the text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify words or phrases that affect the meaning of a text and attempt to explain how they affect meaning, tone, and mood in the text.
I can Point out a word that has multiple meanings and explain how it affects the sentence.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine meanings of words and phrases in text including figurative language.
I can make idiom books and write the real meaning (e.g., You're driving me up a wall = you are making me crazy.).
I can given more than one meaning of key vocabulary words, select the one that best matches the reading passage.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can determine meanings of words and phrases in text.
I can identify meaning of key words using context clues.
I can use a dictionary to look up the meaning of key words.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize words and phrases used in a text.
I can Name or point out words and phrases in an text
I can given a key word for an ext, point to it in the text.

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: In literary texts, consider how varied aspects of structure create meaning and affect the reader. (RL) In informational texts, consider how the author's intent influences particular sentences, paragraphs, or sections. (RI)
ee_text: Identify where a text deviates from a chronological presentation of events (RL) and locate sentences that support an author’s central idea or claim (RI).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how varied aspects of structure in literary texts create meaning and affect the reader, and how an author's intent influences the structure of informational texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: In literary texts, I can consider how varied aspects of structure create meaning and affect the reader. In informational texts, I can consider how the author's intent influences particular sentences, paragraphs, or sections.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify and describe the basic structures of different texts and their general effect.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify deviations from chronological order and locate supporting sentences for the central idea with minimal support.
I can Point out flashbacks in a story and find sentences that support the main idea in an article with some guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify where a text deviates from a chronological presentation of events and locate sentences that support an author’s central idea or claim.
I can recognize non-chronological sections in a story and find key sentences that support the central claim in an informational text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify some non-chronological events and find some supporting sentences with guidance.
I can notice flashbacks in a story and locate sentences that support the main idea with assistance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance, identify basic deviations from chronological order and find simple supporting sentences.
I can with help, point out non-chronological events in a story and find key sentences that support the central idea.

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Analyze how authors employ point of view, perspective, and purpose to shape explicit and implicit messages (e.g., examine rhetorical strategies, literary elements, and devices). Explain how an author’s geographic location, identity, and culture affect perspective. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Determine author’s point of view and compare with own point of view. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how authors employ point of view, perspective, and purpose to shape explicit and implicit messages, and explain how an author’s geographic location, identity, and culture affect perspective on the text and audience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how authors employ point of view, perspective, and purpose to shape explicit and implicit messages (e.g., examine rhetorical strategies, literary elements, and devices). I can explain how an author’s geographic location, identity, and culture affect perspective.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify basic differences in points of view and explain how the background of the author influences a text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify the author’s purpose, explain how the background of the author influences a text and describe basic differences from my own point of view.

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Delineate and evaluate an argument and specific claims in a text, assessing the validity or fallacy of key statements by examining whether the supporting evidence is relevant and sufficient. (RI)
ee_text: Determine how the specific claims support the argument made in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can delineate and evaluate arguments and specific claims in texts, assessing the validity or fallacy of key statements by examining whether the supporting evidence is relevant and sufficient.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate specific claims in a text by checking the validity of key statements and by looking at the supporting evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the main argument and supporting evidence in a text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use evidence and statements to support an argument.
I can ask and answer questions about whether key details support the central idea or claim of an author in the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can delineate statements that support an argument.
I can given two statements related to an argument, select the one that supports the argument (e.g., select from “there is no red and green light” and “the street sign is a rectangle” to support “crossing the street in the middle of the block is dangerous”).
I can after reading text about the president in which all of the statements are about the president except for one statement, identify the statement that is not about the president.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify a fact from a text.
I can after two statements are read by the student or teacher, identify which is a fact versus which is an opinion using key words such as I think, I believe, I feel, (e.g., “The body needs food to live.” versus “Some people think sugar is bad for you.”).
I can as statements are read by the teacher from a historical passage, identify which is a fact versus opinion using key words such as I think, I believe, I feel, (e.g., “Lincoln was president of the United States.” versus “Many believe he was a great man.”).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize that an event occurred.
I can after the teacher reads a brief account of something that happened and discusses it, use a switch to indicate whether an event occurred in the passage (e.g., “Did this happen?”).

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: write text in a variety of modes. a. write arguments and literary analysis to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning, literary theory, and relevant and sufficient evidence that introduce precise claim(s); distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims; and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence. Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
ee_text: with guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: a. write an argument or literary analysis with a clearly stated claim and valid reasons to support the claim. Organize reasons logically and develop the claim fairly. b. Write informative texts which introduce a topic and provide well chosen facts, details, and/or multimedia content to develop the topic and convey information clearly and accurately. Provide a concluding statement.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write compelling arguments and literary analysis with clear reasoning, literary theory, and relevant evidence, effectively introducing and acknowledging alternate or opposing claims using credible sources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write arguments and literary analysis using valid reasoning, literary theory, and sufficient evidence,introducing claims, reasons,evidence, and develop claims and counterclaims by providing evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write arguments with clear reasoning and evidence, and organize my writing logically.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write to convey ideas and information clearly, grouping ideas into categories including facts, details, and other information as well as graphics and multimedia as needed.
I can write about a hobby stating what the hobby is (e.g., I like cooking.), writing a paragraph about favorite foods to cook with a reason (e.g., I like make gril ches [grilled cheese], mac n chees [macaroni and cheese]. I like melt ches [melted cheese].) and favorite desserts (e.g., I like make [making] hot fuj sunda [fudge sundaes] with ice crem sprinkls [cream sprinkles]. Ice crem [cream] is cold and swet [sweet]
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write to convey ideas and information using clear organization and including facts, details, and other information as well as graphics and multimedia as needed.
I can write to give directions to a place in the school including a step-by-step organization with illustrations as needed to support understanding.
I can write to describe a school assembly first describing what the topic was (e.g., DARE), who was involved (all the kids), then the activity (listen to polis [police]) and details (No beer. No drugs.).
descriptors.ee_advanced:
I can write to convey ideas and information clearly, grouping ideas into categories including facts, details, and other information as well as graphics and multimedia as needed.
I can write about a hobby stating what the hobby is (e.g., I like cooking.), writing a paragraph about favorite foods to cook with a reason (e.g., I like make gril ches [grilled cheese], mac n chees [macaroni and cheese]. I like melt ches [melted cheese].) and favorite desserts (e.g., I like make [making] hot fuj sunda [fudge sundaes] with ice crem sprinkls [cream sprinkles]. Ice crem [cream] is cold and swet [sweet].).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can write to convey ideas and information using clear organization as well as graphics and multimedia.
I can write to give directions to a place in the school including most of the steps with illustrations as needed to support understanding.
I can write to describe a school assembly about DARE saying who was involved (all the kids) and what happened (listen to polis [police]).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, write to convey ideas.
I can use a preprogrammed alternate keyboard to write about the school assembly (like it).
I can Work with a teacher using two-switch step scanning to scan through the letters of the alphabet directing the teacher to “go to the next one,” and “write that one down,” in order to select letters to use in writing about school.
I can Using word prediction software and with a teacher’s support and guidance, write about a favorite activity in class (like going to a movie).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write detailed informative texts that examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information through well-organized content, using a variety of formats and multimedia to enhance comprehension.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write informative texts that examine and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content by introducing a topic; organizing complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; including formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia to aid comprehension.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write informative texts with some relevant information and organization.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write two or three facts about a topic using a sentence frame and word bank with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate an informative text that introduces a topic, gives well-chosen facts and details and has a conclusion.

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: write narratives that develop real or imagined experiences or events using relevant descriptive details and well- structured event sequences that organize an event sequence logically. ee_text: Write narratives to convey events and experiences, real or imagined. Include dialogue, relevant details, character descriptions, and tell about the events and in a logical sequence.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write engaging narratives with well-structured event sequences, using advanced techniques such as dialogue, pacing, and reflection to develop characters and events.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write narratives that develop real or imagined experiences or events using details and structured event sequences, engaging and orienting the reader by establishing a context and point of view.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write narratives with basic descriptive details and event sequences.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell or draw what happened first, next and last in a story with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can write or dictate a narrative with dialogue, details and character descriptions that tells events in a logical order.

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.
ee_text: Produce writing that is appropriate for the task, purpose, and audience.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently and collaboratively produce writing that is clear, coherent, culturally-sustaining, and rhetorically authentic, tailored to the task, purpose, and audience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can produce writing with clarity and coherence, with attention to task, purpose, and audience.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can produce writing that is complete and appropriate to a particular task, purpose, and audience.
I can write directions in sequence to do a particular task.
I can make a list of things to assemble that will be needed for a class project.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can produce writing that is appropriate to a particular task, purpose, or audience.
I can make a list of things to pack for a trip using a talking word processor with word prediction software.
I can make a list of three or four steps needed to complete a task by responding to questions in graphic organizer software (e.g., List all the things you did. What did you do first? What did you do next? What was the last thing you did?), which is then converted to text outline and imported into talking word processor, where students expands on the notes and checks accuracy.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing that is appropriate to the task, purpose, or audience.
I can use a word/picture bank projected on an interactive whiteboard combined with spelling to make a list of things to pack for a trip.
I can use a set of guidelines, word prediction software, and a talking word processor to write a letter with of application with an introduction, body, and a closing.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, write.
I can use a keyboard to type letters interactively with a peer who provides a model by writing conventionally but simply.
I can use a multiple message voice output device interfaced with a computer and help from an adult who navigates to the desired page to make a list of free choice activities and then types letter-by-letter about each activity.

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: Develop and strengthen writing (collaboratively and individually) as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
ee_text: with guidance and support from adults and peers as needed, plan before writing, produce writing for a specific purpose and focused on a planned topic, and revise and edit their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently revise and edit my writing, incorporating feedback to enhance clarity and coherence, with a strong focus on purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and strengthen my writing (collaboratively and individually) as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can revise and edit my writing with guidance to improve clarity and address purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can strengthen writing by planning and revising own writing and adding more information.
I can given a topic and a sample brainstorming bubble, generate ideas and write them down, then reread what is written and add one more detail.
I can Develop outline before beginning the writing process (topic, three details, conclusion) and use it to write, seek peer feedback, and then add to the outline based on feedback provided.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can develop writing by planning and revising own writing by adding more information.
I can given a topic and a sample brainstorming bubble, generate ideas and write them down, then reread what is written and add one more detail.
I can Using a question framework (e.g., 5 W’s and an H) in graphic organizer software, take turns entering information into the organizer, seek another peer partner group’s feedback, and then add to the outline.
I can after reading a science text, work with a classmate to take notes in graphic organizer software, convert the graphic representation into an outline, and use word prediction software with a specific topic dictionary to complete the L column of a KWL chart, share it with another pair of classmates, and revise based on their feedback.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, develop writing by planning and revising own writing by adding more information.
I can after sharing writing with peers, work with peers to brainstorm ideas to add. Peers write all of the ideas in a list and give it to the student to use in revising and adding more information to improve the overall quality of the writing.
I can Work with peers to plan a written report of their research project. Each takes turns reading what they have to one another and then the group works together to add ideas to a graphic organizer provided by the teacher. Finally, the student adds ideas from the graphic organizer to own writing to strengthen it.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more to writing to clarify message.
I can When asked by an adult or peer to add more, select additional letters or words to add to the overall message.
I can with teacher guidance and support and using word prediction software (e.g., The teacher asks, “What sound do you hear at the beginning of cat?”), and a talking word processor (e.g., The teacher says, “It said car. I thought you were trying to write cat. What can we change to make it say cat?”), label familiar pictures from a favorite text.

subject: ELA
cluster: Production & Distribution of Writing
text: make informed and intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, multilingual, multimodal, mobile, or other interactive formats) to engage in authentic rhetorical tasks for specific purposes and audiences. Such decisions include assessing particular technologies’ affordances for: a. connecting writers and readers, b. producing accessible experiences for specific audiences, and c. dynamically and flexibly matching modes with ideas to communicate with readers.
ee_text: make intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, and/or other interactive formats) to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products. Proficiently produce writing through printing, cursive, and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can make informed and intentional decisions about technology use to engage in authentic rhetorical tasks, assessing particular technologies’ affordances for connecting writers and readers, producing accessible experiences, and dynamically matching modes with ideas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make informed and intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, multilingual, multimodal, mobile, or other interactive formats) to engage in authentic rhetorical tasks for specific purposes and audiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use technology to produce and share my writing, with basic linking and citation of sources.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use technology, including the Internet,to produce, publish, and update individual writing products.
I can use technology to update, edit, and revise a piece of own writing.
I can use a talking word processor to listen to first draft and decide what information to add, spell check and grammar check to edit, and then export digital draft to class wiki.
I can Having published a draft in a digital writing environment (e.g., website, wiki, blog), review comments of classmates about the draft, download it to a talking word processor with word prediction software, revise it based on the feedback, and upload back to the digital writing environment.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products.
I can use technology to add a sentence in an electronic shared writing product.
I can add words to sentences in an electronic shared writing product.
I can use online communication software to text message with an e-buddy in another classroom or school.
I can record daily activities on a blog that is shared with parents instead of a traditional home-school notebook.
I can navigate the Internet using screen reader software, identify information about the selected topic, use the information to write using a talking word processor with an alternative keyboard, and share what was learned with classmates.
I can use a teacher-created or teacher-identified website to learn about a topic with a peer, take notes with the peer in graphic organizer software, convert the graphic organizer to an outline, and co-author a summary.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update shared writing products.
I can after reviewing and discussing a shared writing product, add words to sentences in the electronic shared writing product.
I can having sent an e-mail to an adult, read their response seeking additional information or clarification, and write a new e-mail to address the request.
I can use an alternative keyboard programmed with the day’s activities and some comments to write an entry on a blog that is shared with parents instead of a home-school notebook.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use technology to write.
I can use a keyboard to type letters and words interactively with a peer or an adult who types simple, conventionally spelled messages.
I can use a keyboard programmed for only alphabet letters and a space bar, word prediction software, and a talking word processor with a peer model to take turns typing text messages to one another.

cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital, academic, and popular sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.
ee_text: write answers to research questions by selecting relevant information from multiple resources.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can gather information from a multiple sources, evaluate the usefulness of each source to answer the research question, and integrate information into the text, using paraphrasing to avoid plagiarism, and indicate source of information with in-text citation.

descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can select information, including quotes, from multiple sources and use the information to write answers to research questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, select information about the topic and use the information to answer questions using direct quotes from the websites.
I can given a problem and bookmarked websites, use at least two sources to show a solution to the problem.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select information from multiple sources and use the information to write answers to research questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, use a screen reader to read the sites and select information about the topic. Then, use the information to answer questions.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select information from multiple sources and use the information to write answers to research questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, navigate to each site and copy/paste information to answer the questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, navigate to each site, listen and read the information with a screen reader, and use word prediction software with a talking word processor to write their answers.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use information from one source to answer a question.
I can given a guiding question, use a single message voice output communication device to say, “That’s it” when the teacher reads something from a teacher-selected text that answers the question.
I can with teacher guidance and support as needed with any of the steps: given a topic, a single bookmarked website, a what or where question, use a screen reader to listen to and read the information at the site, and use word prediction software with a talking word processor and adapted keyboard presenting only alphabet letters, space bar, and a period, write an answer.

cluster: Inquiry to Build & Present Knowledge
text: draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research. (Apply grades 9-10 Reading standards)
ee_text: with guidance and support from adults, draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support reflection, analysis or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can draw relevant evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

I can find some evidence in texts to support my thoughts with guidance.

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on topics, texts, and issues, listening actively, and building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly. a. Come to discussions prepared, explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic, text, or issue. Support analysis by making connections, paraphrasing, clarifying, or explaining the evidence.
ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. a. Prepare evidence for discussions by collecting information on the topic and be able to explain it.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can come to discussions thoroughly prepared, using a wide range of evidence to support my analysis and enhance the discussion through detailed connections, paraphrasing, and explanations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can come to discussions prepared,using evidence to support my ideas by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic, text, or issue. I can support my analysis and make the discussion better by making connections, paraphrasing, clarifying, or explaining the evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can come to discussions with some preparation and use evidence on the topic, text, or issue to support my analysis. I can support my analysis by making connections, explaining, and using my own words.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can prepare for discussions by collecting information on the topic and referring to it in the discussion.
I can In preparation for a discussion, read or listen to a text or other multiple media source to create a list of facts about an assigned topic, and then refer to that list during a discussion on the topic.
I can In preparation for a discussion, read or listen to a text on a topic and highlight important information, and then refer to that highlighted information during a discussion on the topic.
I can In preparation for a discussion, preprogram information about a topic on a multiple message voice output device and then use the preprogrammed messages during a discussion.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can prepare for discussions by collecting information on the topic.
I can In preparation for a discussion, read or listen to a text or other multiple media source to create a list of facts about an assigned topic.
I can In preparation for a discussion, read or listen to a text on a topic and highlight important information.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can prepare for discussions by collecting information on the topic with a group.
I can In preparation for a discussion, work with a peer or group of peers reading and/or listening to text or other multiple media sources to create a list of facts about an assigned topic.
I can In preparation for a discussion, work with a peer or group of peers to read with text displayed on an interactive whiteboard and highlight the important information.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, prepare for a discussion by previewing pre-stored messages and then share those messages during the discussion.
I can In preparation for a discussion, practice selecting four different messages from a multiple message voice output device programmed by the teacher, and then share the messages during a discussion.
I can In preparation for a discussion, preview a message on a single message voice output device programmed by a peer by activating the message and attending to the peer’s explanation, and then activate the message during the ensuing group discussion.

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Work with peers to set norms for collegial discussions,decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views) and clear goals as needed. Reflect on progress as an individual and as a group.
ee_text: Work with adults and peers to set norms for discussions, and reflect on the conversation.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently set norms for collegial discussions and decision-making, reflecting on progress as an individual and as a group.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can work with peers to set norms for collegial discussions, decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views) and clear goals as needed. I can reflect on progress as an individual and as a group.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow established norms for discussions with some guidance and reflect on progress with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can work with peers to set rules for discussions and follow those rules during the discussion.
I can Contribute own ideas (e.g., take turns) during a discussion of group rules, agree upon the rules the group decides, and then follow the rules during the ensuing discussion.
I can Work with peers to select rules they will follow from a list of possibilities, and then follow those rules during the discussion.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can work with peers to set rules for discussions.
I can contribute own ideas (e.g., take turns) during a discussion of group rules, agree upon the rules the group decides.
I can work with peers to select rules they will follow from a list of possibilities.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can follow rules for discussions.
I can given that the group decided they would take turns, take turns during the discussion.
I can given that the group decided they would stick to the topic, remain on the topic of the discussion.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can follow the discussion.
I can Demonstrate attention to the discussion by nodding, gesturing, or vocalizing appropriately in response to peers and the teacher.
I can Indicate agreement to include a group rule by activating a single message voice output device (e.g., “That’s a good idea.”).

subject: ELA
cluster: Comprehension & Collaboration
text: Propel conversations by posing and engaging with questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions. Promote multiple and divergent perspectives.
ee_text: Relate the topic of discussion to broader themes or ideas and acknowledge other perspectives.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can propel conversations by posing and engaging with insightful questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions. I can promote multiple and divergent perspectives.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can propel conversations by asking questions that connect what we are talking about to bigger ideas. I can get others involved in the discussion and help clarify or question ideas and conclusions. I can share and respect different viewpoints. "
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can pose questions and respond to others' comments with some relevant observations and ideas.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can relate the topic of discussion to broader themes or ideas and consider other perspectives with some support.
I can discuss how a specific event relates to a larger theme and mention other viewpoints with guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can relate the topic of discussion to broader themes or ideas and acknowledge other perspectives.
I can During a discussion, explain how the topic connects to larger ideas and recognize different viewpoints.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can connect the topic of discussion to broader themes or ideas with guidance.
I can Identify how a specific topic is part of a larger theme and acknowledge another perspective with assistance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance, relate a topic to a broader idea and recognize different perspectives.
I can with help, explain how a topic connects to a bigger theme and mention another viewpoint.

ee_text: Indicate agreement or disagreement with others during discussions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoughtfully engage with diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, qualify or justify my own views, and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can engage with diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and explain my own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence presented.

descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can clarify own views during discussions.

I can indicate agreement or disagreement with others during discussions.

I can state own views during a discussion.

text: Analyze and synthesize multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats to determine credibility and accuracy of each source.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critically analyze and synthesize multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats to determine credibility and accuracy of each source.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats to determine if each source is credible and accurate.

ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. Notice that standardized English is only one dialect of many and has a specific history that is implicated in power relationships.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain the history and power relationships of standardized English and recognize its use as one dialect among many.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize that standardized English is only one dialect of many and has a specific history that is implicated in power relationships.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify standardized English as one type of language use.

I can recognize standardized English and understand it as one of many dialects, including its role in power relationships, with some support.
I can discuss how different people might use different types of English in various situations with guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can notice that standardized English is only one dialect of many and has a specific history that is implicated in power relationships.
I can Identify standardized English and explain its role and history in different contexts.
I can notice the language demands of a writing/speaking situation (i.e., formal, informal) and respond in an appropriate way.
I can use formal language in an essay and informal language in a conversation with friends.
I can continue to develop metacognitive awareness as a writer and speaker by explaining the reasons for language choices.
I can Reflect on and explain the language choices I made in a speech or essay.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize standardized English as one type of language use with guidance.
I can Identify standardized English in texts and discuss its significance with assistance.
I can recognize some language demands of different situations with guidance.
I can Identify when to use formal and informal language in various contexts with assistance.
I can identify some reasons for my language choices with guidance.
I can discuss why I used certain words or phrases in a paragraph with assistance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance, identify standardized English.
I can Recognize standardized English in a passage and discuss its basic role with help.
b. Notice the language demands of a writing/speaking situation (i.e., formal, informal) and respond in an appropriate way.
I can with guidance, respond to basic language demands.
I can Choose formal or informal language for specific situations with help.
c. Continue to develop metacognitive awareness as writers and speakers by explaining the reasons for language choices.
I can with guidance, explain basic language choices.
I can with help, explain why I used specific words in a sentence.
d. Not applicable

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a character or event and tell one thing that happens to it with help.

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings. Analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood, including words with multiple meanings. Analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of technical or key term(s) over the course of a text. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Determine how words or phrases in a text, including words with multiple meanings and figurative language, impact the meaning. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how an author develops and refines a key term over a text and how word choices create layered tone and mood.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine figurative, connotative and technical meanings and analyze how word choice and the refining of key terms affect meaning, tone and mood.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain the meaning of a key term in context and how it affects tone using a vocabulary chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match key words in a text to their meanings with pictures or a word bank with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell how words or phrases, including multiple-meaning words and figurative language, affect meaning.

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: In literary texts, analyze how varied aspects of structure create meaning and affect the reader. (RL) In informational texts, analyze the impact and evaluate the effect structure has on exposition or argument in terms of clarity, persuasive or rhetorical technique, and audience appeal. (RI)
ee_text: Use a text’s ending (e.g., story (RL)) or structure (e.g, informational (RI) and determine its impact on meaning of the text as a whole.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how an author's structural choices create meaning and judge their effect on clarity, persuasion and audience appeal.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how structure creates meaning in literary texts and evaluate how structure affects clarity, persuasion and appeal in informational texts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the structure of a text and explain one way it helps the reader using a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what happens at the beginning and end of a text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use a text's ending or structure to tell how it affects the meaning of the whole text.

subject: ELA
cluster: Craft & Structure
text: Analyze how authors employ point of view, perspective, and purpose to shape explicit and implicit messages (e.g., persuasiveness, aesthetic quality, satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement). Explain how an author’s geographic location, identity, and culture affect perspective. (RI&RL)
ee_text: Determine author’s point of view and compare and contrast it with own point of view. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how authors use irony, satire or understatement to shape messages and how their identity and culture influence perspective.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how authors use point of view, perspective and purpose to shape explicit and implicit messages and how background affects perspective.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the author's purpose and point of view and one technique used to show it with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what the author thinks about a topic with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can determine an author's point of view and compare and contrast it with my own.

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: In literary texts, analyze multiple adaptations of a source text as presented in different formats (e.g., works of art, graphic novels, music, film, etc.), specifically evaluating how each version interprets the source. (RL) In informational texts, integrate and evaluate sources on the same topic or argument in order to address a question or solve a problem. (RI)
ee_text: Compare two or more interpretations (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry) of a story, drama, or poem. (RL) Analyze information presented in different media on related topics to answer questions or solve problems. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how different adaptations reinterpret a source text and synthesize multiple sources to solve a complex problem.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze and evaluate how adaptations in different formats interpret a source text and integrate sources to address a question or solve a problem.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare two versions of a story or two sources on a topic using a chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to the same event in a text and in a video with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can compare two interpretations of a story, drama or poem and use information from different media to answer questions.

subject: ELA
cluster: Integration of Knowledge & Ideas
text: Delineate and evaluate an argument in applicable texts, applying a lens (e.g., constitutional principles, logical fallacy, legal reasoning, belief systems, codes of ethics, philosophies, etc.) to assess the validity or fallacy of key arguments, determining whether the supporting evidence is relevant and sufficient. (RI)
ee_text: Determine whether the claims and reasoning enhance the author’s argument in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply a chosen lens to judge an argument's validity and explain how specific fallacies or insufficient evidence weaken it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can delineate and evaluate an argument through a lens such as logical fallacy or legal reasoning, judging whether evidence is relevant and sufficient.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the claim and evidence in an argument and tell whether the evidence is enough using a checklist.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what the author wants me to believe and one reason with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell whether the claims and reasoning make an author's argument stronger.

ee_text: Evaluate the quality of texts; make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, and personal events or situations. (RI&RL)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
ee_text: With guidance and support as needed, use dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can combine reflective, formal and creative writing in sophisticated ways for real audiences and justify my choices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write reflective, formal and creative pieces for both high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a short piece for a given purpose using a model and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can dictate or write a few words to share an idea with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support as needed, dictate or write to share my ideas for different purposes.

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Write arguments and literary analysis to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts. Establish the significance of the claim(s) using valid reasoning, literary theory, and relevant and sufficient evidence that introduce precise claim(s); distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims; and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence. Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: a. Write an argument or literary analysis with a clearly stated claim and valid and sufficient reasons to support the claim. Organize reasons logically and develop the claim fairly.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a sophisticated argument or literary analysis that weighs claims and counterclaims fairly and anticipates my audience's concerns.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write arguments that introduce precise claims, distinguish counterclaims, and develop both fairly with evidence, organized to show clear relationships.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a claim, a counterclaim and evidence for each using an argument organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say or write my opinion and one reason with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate an argument with a clear claim and valid reasons organized logically.

source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Write text in a variety of modes. b. Write informative texts that examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content by introducing a topic; organizing complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; including formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension; thoroughly developing the topic by selecting the most significant and relevant well-chosen facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, and other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: b. Write informative texts which introduce a topic and provide well chosen facts, details, quotes, and/or multimedia content to develop the topic and convey information clearly and accurately. Provide a concluding statement.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an informative text that synthesizes the most significant evidence and uses formatting and multimedia to make complex ideas clear.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write informative texts that organize complex ideas clearly and develop the topic with the most significant facts, definitions, details and quotations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write an informative text with headings, facts and quotes using a planning frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share facts about a topic using words, pictures or dictation with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate an informative text with well-chosen facts and quotes and a conclusion.

source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Write text in a variety of modes. c. Write narratives that develop real or imagined experiences or events using relevant descriptive details and well-structured event sequences that organize an event sequence logically. Engages and orients the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator or characters using techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.
ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: c. Write narratives to convey events and experiences, real or imagined. Include dialogue, relevant details, characterization, and tell about the events and in a logical sequence.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a narrative that uses pacing, reflection and multiple plot lines to develop a complex experience or theme.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write narratives that engage the reader with context and point of view, using dialogue, pacing, description, reflection and a logical event sequence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a narrative with dialogue and a clear sequence using a story map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell or draw what happened first, next and last with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate a narrative with dialogue, details and characterization that tells events in order.

source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, analysis, information, and claims, so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole. Establish and maintain a structure and conventions consistent with the mode of writing. Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the topic, themes, and experiences presented in the text.
ee_text: Use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a unified text where each part extends the last and end with a conclusion that adds insight beyond the text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can organize complex ideas so each new element builds on the last to create a unified whole, and write a conclusion that follows from the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can organize my ideas into an introduction, body and conclusion that connect using a planning frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can put my ideas in order (first, then, last) with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, create a text with an introduction, body and conclusion.

subject: ELA
cluster: Text Types & Purposes
text: Create writing that utilizes: b. Transitions: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.
ee_text: Use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use varied transitions and sentence structures to create seamless cohesion across complex arguments.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use appropriate, varied transitions and syntax to link major sections, create cohesion and clarify relationships among complex ideas.

text: Create writing that utilizes: c. Word Choice (including domain specific): Use culturally-sustaining language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic. Use techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

cluster: Knowledge of Language

Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice. a. Recognize that conventions (i.e., aspects of punctuation, layout, and formatting within a particular genre) are the result of agreed upon usage.
ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. a. Use conventions of standard English when needed.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how conventions in different genres developed through agreed usage and apply them flexibly.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize that conventions of punctuation, layout and formatting in a genre are the result of agreed-upon usage.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one convention of a genre, such as a letter or report, using examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to a title or heading in a text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use conventions of standard English when needed.

source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

subject: ELA
cluster: Conventions of Standardized English
text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions. a. Use sophisticated punctuation and capitalization techniques as appropriate to situation and genre (e.g., brackets and italics in research; capitalization expressing extended meaning in poetry).
ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English. a. Demonstrate conventions of standard English including capitalization, ending punctuation, and spelling when writing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use sophisticated punctuation such as brackets, italics and expressive capitalization to create precise effects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use sophisticated punctuation and capitalization techniques that fit the situation and genre.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use brackets or italics correctly in a research sentence using a model.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find capital letters and end marks in a sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use capitals, end punctuation and spelling conventions when writing.

source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)
