subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion, PS2.B Types of Interactions)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and carry out an investigation to compare how different strengths of pushes and pulls affect the motion of various objects. Example: I can push a light ball and a heavy ball, explaining which one rolls farther and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct a simple investigation to see how different pushes affect the motion of an object. Example: I can test how far a car rolls with a soft push compared to a hard push.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how pushing or pulling changes where an object goes. Example: I can say that pulling my toy closer makes it stop moving away.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that some objects move when I push or pull them. Example: I can point to a toy and say it rolls when I push it.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions (PS2.A Forces and Motion)
text: Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or a pull.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an experiment to show how balanced and unbalanced forces work in real life, explaining my observations. Example: I can demonstrate using a seesaw to explain how weight affects balance and movement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct an investigation to explore how balanced and unbalanced forces affect the motion of an object. Example: I can push two toy cars at the same time and see one move while the other stays still.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe when an object moves and when it doesn’t based on how I push or pull it. Example: I can explain that my toy car moves when I push it hard but not when I just touch it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: can see that some objects do not move when I push or pull them. Example: I can say that a heavy box stays in place when I try to push it.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test a ramp or other tool, use my results to explain how it changes an object's speed or direction, and make it work better.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can look at test results to tell if my design, like a ramp, changes the speed or direction of an object as I wanted.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test a ramp with a ball and say if the ball went faster or changed direction, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can push a ball and show that it can go fast, slow, or turn.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth’s surface.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a simple project to demonstrate energy transfer in action and explain what happens. Example: I can create a simple circuit with a battery and a light bulb and describe how the energy makes the bulb light up.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe and explain how energy can be transferred from one object to another. Example: I can show how rubbing my hands together creates heat.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how energy is used in everyday objects. Example: I can explain that a toy car needs batteries to move.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that some things can make light or sound. Example: I can say that a flashlight makes light when I turn it on.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare how warm different surfaces get in the sun, such as sand, water, and grass, and explain why.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make observations to tell how sunlight changes Earth's surface, such as making sand or water warmer.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can touch things in the sun and in the shade and say which is warmer, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun makes things feel warm.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS3 Energy (PS3.B Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer)
text: Use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and build a sunshade and explain how it works in real life to keep things cool. Example: I create a sunshade and share my ideas about how it could help people or animals stay safe from the sun.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use tools and materials to design and build a sunshade that keeps things cool in the sun. Example: I create a sunshade with a clear structure and explain how it helps reduce heat.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can choose some materials and start to build my sunshade with help. Example: I use cardboard and tape to make a simple shape but need support to finish it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what I want to make but need help with my ideas. Example: I can tell someone I want to build a shade but don’t know how.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.C Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in)
text: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and explain how different environments meet the needs of various plants and animals. Example: I can compare how a cactus and a tree get water and explain why they need different amounts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and explain the basic needs of plants and animals, including food, water, and shelter. Example: I can list that plants need sunlight, water, and soil to grow.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what plants and animals need to live and grow. Example: I can explain that animals need food and water.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize that living things need certain things to grow. Example: I can say that plants need water.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.D Weather and Climate)
text: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and explain how different weather patterns impact the environment and living things.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe and report on daily weather conditions and how they affect my surroundings. Example: I can tell what the weather is like today and how it affects my playtime outside.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe different types of weather and how they feel. Example: I can explain that a windy day feels cold and makes leaves move.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that the weather changes. Example: I can say that it is sunny or rainy today.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.E Biogeology)
text: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals (including humans) can change the environment to meet their needs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and explain how seasonal changes influence the behavior of living things and the environment. Example: I can describe how animals prepare for winter and how plants change throughout the seasons.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can observe and explain how different seasons affect weather patterns and the environment. Example: I can list what happens to trees and plants in spring, summer, fall, and winter.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how weather changes with the seasons. Example: I can explain that it rains more in spring and snows in winter.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that seasons change and the weather is different. Example: I can say that it is colder in winter than in summer.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can give several examples of how plants, animals, and people change their surroundings and explain my evidence.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use evidence to tell how plants and animals, including people, change the environment to meet their needs, like a bird building a nest.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can give one example of an animal or person changing a place, using pictures and sentence frames.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can point to pictures of animal homes, like nests and holes.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.A Natural Resources)
text: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants or animals (including humans) and the places they live.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a detailed model to explain how various plants and animals meet their needs in their environments. Example: I build a model of a forest and describe how animals like deer and plants work together to survive.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show how different plants and animals, including humans, depend on their homes. Example: I create a model of a pond and explain that frogs need water and plants to live there.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a simple model to show how some plants and animals need certain things to live. Example: I draw a picture of a tree and say it needs sun and water.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say what plants and animals need but need help with where they live. Example: I can name a plant but don’t know where it grows.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.B Natural Hazards)
text: Ask questions to obtain information about the purpose of weather forecasting to prepare for, and respond to, severe weather.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask detailed questions about weather forecasting and explain how it helps people stay safe during different weather events. Example: I ask, "What tools do meteorologists use to predict storms, and how does that keep us safe?"
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to learn about weather forecasting and why it helps us prepare for serious weather. Example: I ask, "How does a weather report help us stay safe during storms?"
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask questions about the weather and start to understand why forecasting is useful. Example: I ask, "Why do we need to know if it will rain?" and can explain that it helps us plan.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask simple questions about the weather but need help. Example: I might ask, "What is rain?" but don't know why it's important.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS3 Earth and Human Activity (ESS3.C Human Impacts on Earth Systems)
text: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air, and/or other living things in the local environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and suggest solutions to help reduce human impact on the environment. Example: I can discuss how turning off lights when not in use saves energy and why that is important.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and explain ways to reduce waste and protect the environment. Example: I can list ways to reuse items, like using a water bottle instead of buying new ones.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe simple actions people can take to help the environment. Example: I can explain that recycling helps keep our planet clean.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that we can use less of some things. Example: I can say that we should not waste water.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.A Wave Properties)
text: Plan and conduct investigations to provide evidence that vibrating materials can make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can relate my understanding of living things to how we care for them in our community. Example: I can explain how taking care of a pet helps it stay healthy and happy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how living things grow and change, and what they need to survive. Example: I can say that animals need food, water, and shelter to live.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic needs of living things with guidance. Example: I can say that plants need water, but I might not explain why.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some living things in my environment but don’t know much about them. Example: I can say there are birds outside, but I can’t tell you what they do.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can design my own test to show that vibrating things make sound and that sound can make things vibrate, and explain my results.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can plan and do investigations to show that vibrating materials make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can feel or see a vibration when I pluck a string or tap a drum, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can make sounds with objects, like tapping a drum.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.B Electromagnetic Radiation)
text: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that objects can be seen only when illuminated.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect what I learn about plants and animals to real-life situations in my community. Example: I can explain how planting flowers in my garden helps attract bees, which are important for food.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how plants and animals depend on each other and their environment. Example: I can say that bees help flowers grow by spreading pollen.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some simple features of plants and animals but need help explaining them. Example: I can say that a flower is colorful and grows in the ground, but I don’t know why.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some things I see in nature but don’t understand how they work. Example: I can point to a tree and say it's a tree.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence why we cannot see in a dark room and how light lets us see, using a test I did.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make observations to show that objects can be seen only when there is light.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can look in a dark box and say I can see the object only when light shines in, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that I need light to see.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.B Electromagnetic Radiation)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect weather changes to how plants and animals adapt in different seasons. Example: I can explain how trees lose leaves in fall and why some animals hibernate in winter.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how weather affects the environment and our daily activities. Example: I can say that when it snows, we wear warm clothes and play in the snow.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic weather patterns with help. Example: I can say it rains sometimes and that we need umbrellas.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice some changes in the weather but don’t understand them. Example: I can say it is sunny today, but I don’t know what makes it sunny.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can predict and test how clear, see-through, solid, and mirror materials change a light beam and explain the results.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can investigate what happens when different materials are put in the path of a beam of light.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort materials into ones that let light through and ones that block it, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can shine a flashlight on objects and say what I see.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS4 Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer (PS4.C Information Technologies and)
text: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect the use of natural materials to our everyday lives and the environment. Example: I can explain how recycling paper helps save trees and keeps our planet clean.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how different materials come from nature and how we use them. Example: I can say that paper comes from trees and we use it to write on.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some materials and their basic properties with help. Example: I can say that wood is hard and used for building things.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some natural materials but don’t know their uses. Example: I can say that rocks are found outside but can't explain what we do with them.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can build and improve a device that uses light or sound to send a message far away and explain how it works.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to communicate over a distance.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can build a simple device, like a cup phone or flashlight signal, by following steps with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can show a way to send a message, like waving or clapping.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.A Structure and Function, LS1.D Information Processing)
text: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants and/or animals use their external parts to help them survive, grow, and meet their needs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can relate how the parts of plants and animals interact with each other and their environment. Example: I can explain how a flower attracts bees to help it grow and produce seeds.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how different parts of plants and animals help them survive. Example: I can say that a bird’s wings help it fly and find food.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic functions of plant and animal parts with help. Example: I can say that a root helps a plant stay in the ground.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize some parts of plants and animals but don’t know what they do. Example: I can point to a leaf but can’t explain its purpose.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes (LS1.B Growth and Development of Organisms)
text: Read texts and use media to determine patterns in behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect my understanding of plant and animal characteristics to their roles in the ecosystem. Example: I can explain how different types of birds have beaks that help them eat specific foods.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how plants and animals are classified based on their features. Example: I can say that trees are tall and have trunks, while bushes are shorter and bushy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some characteristics of plants and animals with guidance. Example: I can say that some plants need sunlight while others grow in the shade.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice some ways that plants and animals are alike and different but don’t understand them. Example: I can say that some animals have fur and some have feathers.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare parent and baby behaviors from several animals in books or videos and explain how each helps the baby survive.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can read texts and use media to find patterns in how parents and offspring behave to help the offspring survive.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name one way an animal parent helps its baby, like feeding it, using a book with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can match baby animals to their parents in pictures.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits (LS3.A Inheritance of Traits, LS3.B Variation of Traits)
text: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect my understanding of how traits are passed from parents to offspring to real-life examples. Example: I can explain how my hair color is similar to my parents' hair color.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how offspring resemble their parents and how they change as they grow. Example: I can say that kittens grow into cats and look like their parents.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some similarities and differences between parents and their offspring with help. Example: I can say that baby birds look like their parents but are smaller.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize that living things have parents but don’t understand how they are similar. Example: I can say that a puppy has a mom and dad.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.A The Universe and its Stars)
text: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect my understanding of Earth and sky features to what I see in my daily life. Example: I can explain how sunlight helps flowers grow and how rain can create puddles.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how different features of the Earth and sky change over time. Example: I can say that the moon looks different each night and that we have seasons.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic features of the Earth and sky with help. Example: I can say that the sun helps us see during the day.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice some things in the sky but don’t understand what they are. Example: I can see clouds but can’t explain why they are there.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.B Earth and the Solar System)
text: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect my understanding of weather patterns to how they impact the environment and activities. Example: I can explain how different types of weather help plants grow and influence what we wear each season.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how weather conditions change and how they affect our daily lives. Example: I can say that when it rains, we need umbrellas and that sunny days are good for playing outside.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe basic weather conditions with assistance. Example: I can say that it is sunny or rainy but don’t know what causes these changes.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice some changes in the weather but don’t understand them. Example: I can say it is windy today but can’t explain why.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare daylight at different times of year and explain the pattern using my observations.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can say whether it gets dark earlier or later in summer or winter, using a chart with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say when it is daytime and nighttime.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use my understanding of nature to solve real-life problems and explain how we can protect the environment. Example: I can suggest ways to help bees and plants thrive in our community, like planting a garden.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how different parts of nature work together and give specific examples. Example: I can say that bees help flowers grow by spreading pollen, and I can explain how this helps both.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some parts of nature and how they help each other, but my explanations are basic. Example: I can say that plants need sunlight, but I can't explain why.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a few things in nature, but I struggle to explain how they work together. Example: I can point out plants and animals but don’t know why they need each other.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can create my own groups for materials and explain the properties I used to sort them.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can investigate and classify different materials by their properties, like color, texture, hardness, and flexibility.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort materials as hard or soft, rough or smooth, with a word bank.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name what an object is made of, like wood or plastic.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my knowledge of objects to create new solutions or improve how we use them in everyday life. Example: I can design a special pencil holder that keeps pencils organized and easy to find
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the uses of different objects and give specific examples of how they help us. Example: I can say a pencil is used for writing and drawing, and it helps us share ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe what some objects are used for, but my explanations are not detailed. Example: I can say a pencil is for writing, but I can’t explain how it helps us.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some objects around me, but I have trouble explaining their uses. Example: I can point to a chair but don’t know why we use it.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test several materials and use the data to choose and justify the best one for a job.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can analyze test data to decide which materials have the best properties for a purpose.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test two materials and say which is better for a job, like keeping water out, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say which material is good for a job, like a cup made of plastic.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.A Structure and Properties of Matter)
text: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use my understanding of changes in objects to predict outcomes or explore new ideas in real-life situations. Example: I can predict what happens to ice cream on a hot day and suggest ways to keep it from melting quickly.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how and why objects change in specific ways, using examples from my observations. Example: I can explain that ice melts into water when it gets warm because of heat.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some changes in objects, but my explanations are simple. Example: I can say that ice turns to water, but I don’t explain why it happens.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize some changes in objects, but I struggle to describe them. Example: I can see that ice melts, but I can’t explain what happens.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can take apart an object made of pieces, build a new object, and explain how the same pieces made something different.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use observations to explain how an object made of small pieces can be taken apart and made into a new object.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can take apart a block tower and build something new, and say what I did, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can put blocks together and take them apart.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: PS1 Matter and Its Interactions (PS1.B Chemical Reactions)
text: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of living things' needs to help care for them in real-life situations. Example: I can create a care plan for a pet that includes feeding, exercise, and grooming.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the basic needs of different living things and give specific examples. Example: I can say that dogs need food, water, and exercise to stay healthy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic needs of living things, but my explanations are not detailed. Example: I can say that plants need water, but I can’t explain why.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some living things, but I struggle to describe their needs. Example: I can name a dog, but I don’t know what it needs to live.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can predict which heating or cooling changes can be reversed, test them, and argue with evidence.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use evidence to argue that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort changes, like melting ice and cooking an egg, into can or cannot change back, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that ice melts when it gets warm.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.A Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems)
text: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use my knowledge of animal habitats to make connections about their survival and suggest ways to protect their environments. Example: I can explain how pollution affects fish habitats and suggest ways to keep water clean.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how different animals are adapted to their habitats and give specific examples. Example: I can explain that fish live in water because they have gills to breathe underwater.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe where some animals live, but my explanations are basic. Example: I can say that birds live in trees, but I can’t explain why they choose trees.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize some animals, but I struggle to describe where they live. Example: I can name a fish, but I don’t know what kind of water it needs.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can design a fair test with plants and explain what my results show about light and water.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can plan and do an investigation to find out if plants need sunlight and water to grow.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can grow plants with and without water or light and say which grew better, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need water and sunlight.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics (LS2.A Interdependent Relationships in Ecosystems)
text: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of plant and animal characteristics to solve problems or improve their environments. Example: I can design a garden that includes plants suited for water conservation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the characteristics of various plants and animals and give specific examples of how they help them survive. Example: I can explain that cacti have thick skin to store water in the desert.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some characteristics of plants and animals, but my explanations are not detailed. Example: I can say that a dog has fur, but I can’t explain how fur helps it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some plants and animals, but I struggle to describe their basic characteristics. Example: I can name a tree, but I don’t know what makes it different from other plants.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can build a model of how an animal spreads seeds or pollen and explain how it helps the plant.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make a simple model that works like an animal spreading seeds or pollinating plants.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can show with a model how a bee carries pollen or seeds stick to fur, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that bees visit flowers.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity (LS4.D Biodiversity and Humans)
text: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use my knowledge of plant and animal parts to explore real-world applications, such as conservation. Example: I can suggest ways to protect plant roots to prevent soil erosion in my community.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the functions of various parts of plants and animals and give specific examples. Example: I can explain that leaves help plants make food through sunlight.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some functions of plant and animal parts, but my explanations are basic. Example: I can say that roots help plants, but I can’t explain how they do it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some parts of plants and animals, but I struggle to explain their functions. Example: I can name leaves, but I don’t know what they do for the plant.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare the variety of plants and animals in two habitats and explain why they are different.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can list plants and animals I see in one habitat, like the desert or the sea, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name some animals that live on land and in water.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe (ESS1.C The History of Planet Earth)
text: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of people's needs to suggest improvements in my community. Example: I can propose a community garden to help provide fresh food for everyone.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the basic needs of people and how these needs are met in specific ways. Example: I can explain that people need food and they get it from farms and stores.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some needs of people and mention where they can be met, but my explanations are simple. Example: I can say people need water, and I know they get it from taps, but I can’t explain how it gets there.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some basic needs of people, but I struggle to explain how they are met. Example: I can say people need food, but I don’t know where it comes from.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare fast and slow Earth events from several sources and explain how long each takes to change the land.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use information from several sources to show that Earth events can happen quickly or slowly.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort events, like an earthquake and erosion, into fast or slow, using pictures with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name an event that changes the land, like a flood.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.A Earth Materials and Systems)
text: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use my understanding of community helpers to suggest ways we can support them in their work. Example: I can propose a thank-you event for community helpers to show our appreciation for their hard work.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the roles of various community helpers and give specific examples of how they support the community. Example: I can explain that doctors help keep people healthy by treating illnesses.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the jobs of some community helpers, but my explanations are basic. Example: I can say that a teacher helps kids learn, but I can’t explain how.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize some community helpers, but I struggle to explain what they do. Example: I can name a firefighter, but I don’t know how they help people.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test and compare designs that stop wind or water from moving sand and explain which works best.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can compare different solutions that slow or stop wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test one way to stop water from washing sand away and say if it worked, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can show that water and wind can move sand.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.B Plate Tectonics and Large-Scale System)
text: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of local places to suggest improvements or new ideas for community development. Example: I can propose adding more parks in the neighborhood for kids to play and families to
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the functions of various local places and give specific examples of how they benefit the community. Example: I can explain that a grocery store provides food and that it helps families get their meals.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some local places and mention their purposes, but my explanations are simple. Example: I can say a library is for reading, but I can’t explain what else people do there.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some local places, but I struggle to explain their purposes. Example: I can name a park, but I don’t know what activities happen there.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can make a detailed model or map of land and water in an area and explain what it shows.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make a model to show the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can label land and water features, like hills and the sea, on a model with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can point to land and water on a map or picture.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
cluster: ESS2 Earth's Systems (ESS2.C The Roles of Water in Earth’s Surface)
text: Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of family roles to suggest ways to strengthen family relationships. Example: I can propose having regular family game nights to help us bond and have fun together.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the roles of various family members and give specific examples of how they contribute to the family. Example: I can explain that parents provide care and guidance, helping us learn and grow.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some family roles and mention their responsibilities, but my explanations are basic. Example: I can say that a sibling plays with me, but I can’t explain how we support each other.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some family roles, but I struggle to explain what they do. Example: I can say that a parent is in my family, but I don’t know how they help us.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can find where water is on Earth in different forms and explain which places have solid or liquid water.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can get information to tell where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name places with water, like oceans and ice, using pictures with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be ice or liquid.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.A Defining Engineering Problems)
text: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can investigate and create a simple design to solve a problem, and explain how it works. Example: I can build a model of a windmill and explain how it can help generate energy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify a problem, plan a solution, and explain my design. Example: I can say that we need a way to keep drinks cold and describe how I would design a cooler.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a problem and suggest ways to solve it using design. Example: I can explain that we need a way to keep toys organized and suggest making a box.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize that people design things to solve problems. Example: I can say that a bridge helps cars cross a river.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.B Developing Possible Solutions)
text: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate a design after testing, make changes, and explain why the changes will improve it. Example: I can redesign my boat to make it float better and explain how the shape helps.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can test a design, identify what works, and suggest improvements. Example: I can test my car and say it needs bigger wheels to roll better.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe ways to make a design better after testing it. Example: I can explain that my bridge needs to be stronger.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice when a design works or doesn’t work. Example: I can say that a tower fell down.

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can draw or build a model, label its parts, and explain how changing its shape would make it work better.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can make a simple sketch, drawing, or model to show how the shape of an object helps it do its job.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can draw an object and say what one part of its shape does, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can draw or build a simple object, with teacher support.

subject: Science
strand: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science
cluster: ETS1 Engineering Design (ETS1.C Optimizing the Design Solution)
text: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify a problem, ask detailed questions, and suggest ways to create or improve an object or tool to solve it. Example: I see that my bike is hard to ride and propose making a new seat that is more comfortable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions and gather information to define a simple problem that needs a new or better tool. Example: I observe that a toy is hard to play with and say, "We need a new way to hold it."
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask questions and make observations about a problem that needs fixing. Example: I notice that my backpack is heavy and ask, "How can I make it easier to carry?"
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask basic questions about a problem but need help understanding it. Example: I might ask, "Why is it hard to carry things?" but don't know how to solve it.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test two designs, record results in a chart, and explain which is stronger and why.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can look at test results from two objects made to solve the same problem and compare what each does well and not well.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test two designs and say which one worked better, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can watch two designs being tested and point to the one that worked.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)

text: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify a problem, ask detailed questions, and suggest ways to create or improve an object or tool to solve it. Example: I see that my bike is hard to ride and propose making a new seat that is more comfortable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions and gather information to define a simple problem that needs a new or better tool. Example: I observe that a toy is hard to play with and say, "We need a new way to hold it."
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask questions and make observations about a problem that needs fixing. Example: I notice that my backpack is heavy and ask, "How can I make it easier to carry?"
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask basic questions about a problem but need help understanding it. Example: I might ask, "Why is it hard to carry things?" but don't know how to solve it.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can test two designs, record results in a chart, and explain which is stronger and why.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can look at test results from two objects made to solve the same problem and compare what each does well and not well.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can test two designs and say which one worked better, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can watch two designs being tested and point to the one that worked.

source: NGSS DCI Arrangements (Achieve 2013, nextgenscience.org AllDCI.pdf)
