subject: Social Studies
text: Identify stories about past events, people, places or situations

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how cultural differences and similarities help people understand and respect each other in real life. Example: I can say that even though people in Qatar speak Arabic and people in India speak Hindi, we can be friends and learn from each other.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can tell how my culture is similar to and different from others in ways like clothes, food, or holidays. Example: I can say that in Qatar we celebrate National Day, and in other countries they have different special days.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can notice that people in Qatar and other places do things differently, but I’m not sure how they are the same or different. Example: I know some people wear abayas and others don’t, but I can’t say why or how it’s different.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name something about my own life, like food I eat or clothes I wear, but I don’t compare it to other people’s lives. Example: I say I eat machboos at home but do not talk about what others eat.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can retell a story about the past and explain what it teaches us about people or places.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can identify stories about past events, people, places, or situations.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can point to a picture in a story about the past and say who or what it shows, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can listen to a story about long ago and name one person in it.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Give examples of conflict and cooperation among individuals and groups.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how my actions and others’ actions can make a real difference in solving conflicts or helping with cooperation. Example: I say “If I share my toy, my friend feels happy and we both get to play together,” or “When I say sorry after conflict, we can be friends again.”
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how conflict or cooperation affects people. Example: I say “fighting makes people sad,” or “sharing makes people happy because everyone gets a turn.”
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say what conflict or cooperation looks like, but I can’t explain how it affects people. Example: I say “sharing is cooperation” or “fighting is conflict,” but I don’t say how it helps or hurts others.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name something people do, but I don’t know if it’s conflict or cooperation. Example: I say “kids play together” or “kids fight” but I can’t explain which is cooperation or conflict.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify regional folk heroes, stories, or songs that have contributed to the development of a history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify and analyze various folk heroes and stories from Qatar, connecting them to contemporary issues and understanding their broader significance. Example: I can discuss how the tales of Qatar's pearl divers highlight themes of resilience and community, relating them to current efforts in preserving cultural heritage.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple folk heroes and stories from Qatar, understanding their significance in shaping national identity. Example: I can explain the story of Sheikh Mohammed bin Jassim and how it reflects the values of leadership and bravery in Qatari culture.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some regional folk heroes and stories from Qatar and explain their importance, though my understanding may be limited. Example: I can mention the story of Al-Ghufran and say it is important, but I need help with details about its cultural significance.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify a few folk stories or heroes from Qatar, but I struggle to explain their significance. Example: I can name a few Qatari folk tales but cannot describe what they mean to the culture.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify connections between who they are as a person and their place in the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on various aspects of my identity and how they relate to my role in Qatari society and the global community. Example: I can explore how my experiences in Qatar’s education system influence my perspectives on global issues, such as sustainability and cultural exchange.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple traits about myself and explain how they connect to my identity as a Qatari citizen. Example: I can discuss my interest in Qatari history and how it shapes my understanding of community and belonging.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some personal traits and explain how they relate to my identity in Qatar, though my connections may be limited. Example: I can mention that I enjoy traditional Qatari food, which connects me to my culture, but I need to elaborate on why it matters.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify a few personal traits but struggle to connect them to my identity in relation to Qatar. Example: I can say I am Qatari, but I need help explaining what that means to me.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Distinguish themselves as individuals from others.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on my individuality in the context of Qatari society, understanding how my unique traits contribute to the cultural tapestry of my community. Example: I can explore how my experiences as a Qatari citizen influence my views on cultural diversity and how I engage with others in a global context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple traits that distinguish me as an individual and explain how these traits relate to my experiences in Qatar. Example: I can discuss my family's traditions and how they shape my identity differently from my friends’ traditions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some personal traits that make me unique and explain how they differ from others in Qatar, though my explanations may be limited. Example: I can mention that I speak Arabic and English, which makes my experience different from others who may only speak one language.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize that I am different from others, but I struggle to express what makes me unique. Example: I can say I live in Qatar, but I need help explaining how I differ from my classmates.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Recognize that individual people are part of a group.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on my roles in various groups and how they shape my identity and connections to Qatari society. Example: I can explore how being part of a local sports team influences my understanding of collaboration and community spirit in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple groups I belong to and explain my role and contributions within those groups. Example: I can discuss how I participate in my family, school, and community events in Qatar, helping to foster teamwork.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize some groups I belong to and explain my role, though my understanding may be limited. Example: I can say I am part of my school and that I have friends, but I need help explaining how we support each other.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify that I am part of a group, but I struggle to explain what that means. Example: I know I am in a family, but I can't describe how we work together.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify rights and responsibilities of the individual in relation to his or her social group, including the characteristics of good citizens.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on the roles of various individuals in my community and their impact on cultural and social development in Qatar. Example: I can discuss how community activists influence social change and the importance of their work in promoting cultural heritage and unity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple individuals in my community and explain their roles and contributions. Example: I can explain how local leaders and teachers contribute to the development of education in Qatar and support students.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some individuals in my community and describe their roles, though my explanations may be limited. Example: I can talk about my school principal and say they help lead the school, but I need more details about their responsibilities.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a few individuals in my community, but I struggle to explain their roles. Example: I can mention a neighbor but cannot describe what they do in our community.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain how my rights and responsibilities help my class work well together.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can identify my rights and responsibilities in my class or family and the qualities of a good citizen.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name one right and one responsibility I have in class, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can follow one class rule.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify sources and purposes of authority in various settings (e.g., mayor, chief, ruler, principal, and teacher).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on the unique roles of individuals in my community, understanding how these roles interact and contribute to the broader social fabric of Qatar. Example: I can discuss how the work of various community leaders and activists fosters collaboration and cultural awareness among diverse groups in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple unique roles within my community and explain how each contributes to our society. Example: I can explain how a heritage preservationist helps maintain Qatar's cultural sites, highlighting the importance of history in our identity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize some unique roles individuals play in my community and explain their importance, though my understanding may be limited. Example: I can mention that a local artist shares Qatari culture through their work, but I need help detailing their impact.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify that people have different roles in my community, but I struggle to explain what makes each role unique. Example: I know there are teachers and doctors, but I can't say how their roles differ.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain why we need people in authority and what makes their authority fair.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can identify people with authority, such as a teacher, principal, or the Emir, and say why they have it.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can match a person in authority to the place they lead, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name a person who is in charge at school.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Distinguish between needs and wants.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on the complex relationships between various communities and cultures, understanding their impact on social cohesion and cultural diversity in Qatar. Example: I can discuss how the global presence of expatriates enriches Qatari culture, fostering dialogue and collaboration across different cultural backgrounds.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple connections between communities and cultures, understanding their significance in Qatar. Example: I can explain how the blending of Bedouin traditions and modern influences shapes Qatari identity and community life.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some connections between communities and cultures, though my explanations may be limited. Example: I can mention that Qatari culture includes influences from neighboring countries, but I need more detail about how these connections exist.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a few communities or cultures, but I struggle to explain how they are connected. Example: I can list different cultures in Qatar, but I can't describe their relationships.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain why I chose something as a need or a want and what happens if a need is not met.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can distinguish between needs and wants.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort pictures into needs and wants, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can point to something I need, such as food or water.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Distinguish between "tool" and "technique."

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and reflect on the role of technology in society, understanding its influence on cultural, economic, and social aspects in Qatar. Example: I can discuss how advancements in energy technology are transforming Qatar's economy and addressing sustainability challenges in the region.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and describe multiple technologies and explain their roles and contributions to Qatari society. Example: I can explain how technology in education, like digital learning platforms, enhances learning opportunities for students in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some technologies and describe their roles in society, though my explanations may be limited. Example: I can talk about social media and say it connects people in Qatar, but I need more detail on its impact.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a few technologies used in Qatar, but I struggle to explain their roles in society. Example: I can mention smartphones but can't describe how they affect daily life in Qatar.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can give an example of a tool and the technique used with it, and explain the difference.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can distinguish between a tool (an object) and a technique (a way of doing something).
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort pictures into tools and ways of doing things, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name a tool I use.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Differentiate between people, places, and events in the past, present and future.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how people, places, and events change over time and predict how they might be different in the future. Example: I can describe how Doha has changed over time and share ideas about what it might look like in the future.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain if people, places, or events happened in the past, are happening now, or will happen in the future. Example: I can say that Qatar’s National Day happened in the past, that my school is a place in the present, and that the FIFA World Cup in Qatar was planned for the future.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe people, places, or events with help and start to say if they are from the past, present, or future. Example: I can say that the museum is a place from the past, but I need help explaining why.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some people, places, or events, but I don’t yet understand when they happened. Example: I can say “my grandfather” or “Doha” but can’t say if it’s past, present, or future.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify and describe factors that contribute to cooperation and factors that may cause conflict.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how cooperation and conflict affect communities and suggest ways to solve conflicts peacefully. Example: I can explain how families in Qatar solve problems by talking and listening, and I can suggest ways to help friends cooperate better.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify and explain reasons why people cooperate or have conflicts in Qatar. Example: I can explain how working together helps a team win a game, and how not listening to others can cause disagreements.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some reasons for cooperation or conflict with help. Example: I can say that sharing helps friends get along, and not sharing can cause problems, but I need help explaining more.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some reasons why people work together or disagree, but I don’t fully understand them yet. Example: I can say “friends share” or “people fight,” but I can’t explain why.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe ways in which people depend on the physical environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how people in Qatar change the way they live because of the desert, the sea, or the weather.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe ways people depend on the physical environment for food, water, and shelter.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one thing people get from the land or sea, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to pictures of land, water, and sky and say what people use them for.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain the concept of location.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why location is important and use maps or directions to describe places clearly. Example: I can explain how knowing the location of the airport helps people travel easily in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the concept of location by describing where places are in Qatar using words like “near,” “far,” “north,” or “south.” Example: I can explain that the Museum of Islamic Art is near the Corniche in Doha.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe where some places are with help using simple words. Example: I can say that my school is near the park, but I need help explaining more details about its location.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize places but don’t yet understand what location means. Example: I can point to my school or home but cannot explain where they are.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe how people in different types of institutions and organizations (e.g. families, schools, local religious communities, clubs, etc.) interact with each other.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why positive interactions are important in families and schools and suggest ways people can work together better. Example: I can explain how families and schools can communicate to help students succeed and share ideas to make these relationships stronger.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how people in families and schools in Qatar interact and support each other. Example: I can describe how parents teach children at home and teachers help students learn at school.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how some people in families or schools interact with help. Example: I can say that parents care for children and teachers help students, but I need help explaining how they communicate.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some people in families or schools but don’t yet understand how they interact. Example: I can say “mom” or “teacher,” but I don’t know how they work or talk with each other.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe how people from different cultures interact with the environment, such as the use of resources, shelter and transportation.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how two cultures use resources, shelter, and transportation and explain why they are different.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how people from different cultures interact with the environment, such as using resources, shelter, and transportation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of how a culture uses the land or sea, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match pictures of homes or transport to the place where people use them.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Distinguish themselves as individuals from others.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why understanding differences and group behavior is important and suggest ways to work well with others. Example: I can explain how respecting differences helps my group work better and share ideas to make group activities fair and fun.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how I am different from others and how people behave when they are in groups. Example: I can say that in my class, some students like to work alone while others like working in groups.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some ways I am like and different from others with help. Example: I can say that I like playing soccer and my friend likes basketball, but I need help explaining why people act differently in groups.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can talk about myself but don’t yet understand how I am different from others. Example: I can say “I like apples” but don’t know how others might be different.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Recognize culturally and contextually appropriate and inappropriate social behavior and the impact of making choices about behavior.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a behavior that is fine in one place may not be fine in another, and choose well.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize appropriate and inappropriate social behavior in different places and explain the impact of my choices.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort behaviors into good and not good choices, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can show one good behavior for the classroom.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain why people live in social groups (e.g. families, communities, and nation).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how living in groups such as family, community, and nation helps people meet needs.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain why people live in social groups, such as families, communities, and nations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name groups I belong to and say one reason people live together, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the people in my family.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify sources and purposes of authority in various settings (e.g., mayor, chief, ruler, principal, and teacher).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how different types of authority work in real life and share ideas about using authority fairly and respectfully. Example: I can compare how a majlis leader and a school principal both listen to others and make decisions for their communities.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify different sources of authority in Qatar and explain how they help keep order in schools, communities, and the country. Example: I can explain that school principals make decisions for the school, and that Qatar’s leaders make laws to help people live safely together.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some sources of authority with help and begin to explain where they have power. Example: I can say that a teacher makes rules in the classroom, but I need help explaining how that helps everyone learn.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some people who are in charge, but I am still learning what they do. Example: I can say “teacher” or “police officer,” but I don’t yet understand how they help make rules or decisions.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe rights and responsibilities of the individual in relation to his or her social group, including the characteristics of good citizens.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how my rights and responsibilities in a group are connected.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe my rights and responsibilities in my social group and the qualities of a good citizen.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one right and one responsibility I have in class, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one class rule.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify qualities that leaders need in order to meet their responsibilities.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain which leadership qualities matter most in a situation and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify qualities that leaders need to meet their responsibilities.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one quality of a good leader, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a leader at school or at home.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe the impact of families and schools on their lives.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how my family and school work together to help me grow.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe the impact of my family and school on my life.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one way my family or school helps me, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name people in my family and my school.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe roles resources play in our daily lives.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how jobs and resources support the community and share ideas about how they can be used better in Qatar. Example: I can suggest that using more local farms for food can support farmers and reduce how much food we import.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how different jobs and resources help meet people’s needs in Qatar. Example: I can describe how people working in Qatar’s gas industry provide energy that helps the country grow.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some jobs and resources with help and begin to say how they are useful in daily life. Example: I can say that doctors help sick people and oil is important, but I need help explaining why they are important for Qatar.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some resources or jobs, but I am still learning how they help people. Example: I can say “water” or “teacher” but I can’t yet explain how they help people in Qatar.

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe how we depend upon people with specialized jobs.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain what would happen in my community if one specialized job disappeared.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how we depend on people with specialized jobs.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match a job to how it helps people, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a job such as doctor or teacher.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Distinguish between goods and services.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish between goods and services.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort pictures into goods and services, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name something I can buy.

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe examples in which tools and techniques have changed the lives of people.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how tools or techniques make life better in Qatar and share new ideas to help people. Example: I can suggest that more solar-powered lights could help save energy and protect the environment in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how tools or techniques help people live, work, or solve problems in Qatar. Example: I can describe how mobile apps like Karwa make it easier to travel around Doha.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe simple tools or techniques with help and start to say how they are useful in Qatar. Example: I can say that air conditioners help keep us cool, but I need help explaining how they improve life in hot weather.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some tools or techniques, but I am still learning how they help people in daily life. Example: I can say “mobile phone” or “air conditioner” but cannot explain how they help people in Qatar.

subject: Social Studies
text: Relate stories about past events, people, places, or situations to help our understanding of the past and present.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some local places and mention their purposes, but my explanations are simple. Example: I can say a library is for reading, but I can’t explain what else people do there.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some local places, but I struggle to explain their purposes. Example: I can name a park, but I don’t know what activities happen there.

descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can say one way life in a story from the past is different from today, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can listen to a story about the past and say what happened.

text: Identify that some ways of dealing with disagreements work better than others.

text: Describe how families influence the individual.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the benefits of living in social groups and provide examples of how these groups impact individuals and communities. Example: I can discuss how living in social groups in Qatar fosters a sense of belonging and helps people cooperate during cultural events.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain why people live in social groups, including safety, support, and shared interests. Example: I can explain that people in Qatar live in groups to help each other and celebrate traditions together.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some reasons why people might live in social groups but struggle to explain them clearly. Example: I can say that people like to be together, but I can’t explain why that’s important.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can’t explain why people form social groups. Example: I don’t know why friends hang out together.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain how my family's traditions and values influence the choices I make.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can describe how families influence the individual.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name one thing I learned from my family, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name the people in my family.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify how sociological circumstances (race, ethnicity, gender, class, etc.) influence an individual's perceptions of and reactions to the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a person's background can shape how they see an event and why others may see it differently.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify how circumstances such as ethnicity, gender, and family background influence how a person sees and reacts to the world.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of how a person's background affects what they think, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people can feel differently about the same thing.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Compare and contrast how groups and cultures are similar and different in meeting needs and concerns of their members.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why groups and cultures meet their members' needs in different ways.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare and contrast how groups and cultures meet the needs and concerns of their members.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one way a group helps its members, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a group I belong to and one thing it does for me.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe the various forms of institutions (e.g., school, church, clubs, etc.) and how they influence the individual.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how two institutions influence people and explain which affects me most and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe different institutions, such as schools, mosques, and clubs, and how they influence a person.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name an institution and one thing it does, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name my school and one thing I learn there.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify issues involving rights, roles and responsibilities of individuals in relation to broader society.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how effective leadership and community service impact individuals and society, providing specific examples. Example: I can discuss how leaders in Qatar inspire others through service projects and how this fosters community spirit and cooperation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the importance of leadership and service in helping others and making communities better. Example: I can explain that leaders in Qatar help organize events and that service helps support those in need.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some leaders and service roles but struggle to explain their importance clearly. Example: I can say that teachers lead us, but I can’t explain why that matters.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can’t explain what leadership and service mean. Example: I don’t know what a leader does or why helping is important.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain an issue about rights and responsibilities in my community and suggest a fair solution.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can identify issues involving rights, roles, and responsibilities of individuals in society.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name one right and one responsibility people have in society, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name one rule in my community.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe how political institutions meet needs and wants of individuals and society.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a political institution in Qatar meets needs and suggest an improvement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how political institutions meet the needs and wants of people and society.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one institution and one need it meets, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a government service such as hospitals or schools.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify community leaders, local and national government officials, and world leaders.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain the job of a community leader, a national official, and a world leader and how they connect.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify community leaders, local and national government officials, and world leaders.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one community leader and one national leader, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a leader at my school.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe characteristics, locations, uses, and management of renewable and non-renewable resources.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the implications of using renewable and non-renewable resources on the environment and society, providing real-life examples. Example: I can discuss how using wind energy in Qatar helps reduce pollution compared to relying on oil.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe renewable resources, like solar energy, and non-renewable resources, like oil, including examples from my community. Example: I can explain that solar panels use sunlight, which is renewable, while oil is limited and will run out.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some resources but struggle to categorize them as renewable or non-renewable. Example: I can say water is important, but I can’t explain if it’s renewable or not.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can’t explain what renewable and non-renewable resources are. Example: I don’t know the difference between types of resources.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Distinguish among human, natural, and capital resources.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how human, natural, and capital resources combine to make a product.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish among human, natural, and capital resources.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort examples into human, natural, or capital resources, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a natural resource such as water or oil.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain the difference between science and technology.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how science and technology work together to improve our lives and provide specific examples from everyday life. Example: I can discuss how scientific research leads to new medical technologies that help people stay healthy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that science is the study of the natural world, while technology is the application of that knowledge to solve problems. Example: I can explain that scientists study plants, and technology helps us grow them better.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify examples of science and technology but struggle to explain how they are different. Example: I can say that computers are technology, but I can’t explain how it relates to science.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe some basic ideas about science and technology but need help explaining them. Example: I don’t understand what scientists do or what technology means.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Examine ways in which tools and techniques make certain tasks easier.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how a task is done with and without a tool and measure the difference.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can examine ways tools and techniques make certain tasks easier.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of a tool that makes a job easier, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a simple tool in class.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe ways that tools and techniques can have both positive and negative effects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can weigh the positive and negative effects of a technology and suggest how to reduce the negatives.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe ways tools and techniques can have both positive and negative effects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one good effect and one bad effect of a tool, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say if a tool is helpful.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe changes in society (e.g., political, social, cultural).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare different societies and explain how their beliefs, values, and technology influenced their worldviews, using real-world examples. Example: I can explain how ancient Egyptians believed in many gods based on nature, and how today's beliefs are shaped by science and global communication.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how people from different times and places saw the world differently because of their culture, beliefs, or available technology, and describe how societies change over time. Example: I can explain that people in the past believed the Earth was flat because they didn’t have the tools to see space like we do now.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some ways people lived differently in the past or in other places, but I need help explaining why they thought or acted that way. Example: I can say people used candles instead of lights, but I don’t explain why they did that.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recognize that people in the past were different from people today, but I need help explaining how or why. Example: I know people long ago didn’t have phones, but I’m not sure how that changed their lives.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify cause and effect relationships in history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can connect cause and effect in history and explain how one event led to another. Example: I can explain that when explorers came to Qatar, it led to trade and changes in how people lived.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe a historical event and explain what caused it and what happened because of it. Example: I can explain that a fire in a village caused people to build stronger homes afterward.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes identify what happened and why, but I need help to explain the connection. Example: I know that people moved to a new place after a storm, but I need help saying the storm caused it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can listen to a story from history but don’t yet understand why things happened. Example: I know something changed after a big event, but I don’t know what caused it.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain varied causes and effects of conflict and cooperation among individuals, groups, societies and nations in the following categories: politics, economics, geography, ethnicity/race/gender, and culture.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how personal and group choices about wants and needs can lead to long-term effects on society and the planet. Example: I can explain how buying local food supports farmers and reduces pollution from transportation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how people’s wants and needs can affect others and the environment around them. Example: I can explain that using too much electricity can lead to pollution that affects everyone.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes explain how my wants and needs might affect others, but I need help to understand the bigger impact. Example: I know using too much water might mean less for others, but I don’t explain how.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name my own wants and needs but don’t yet understand how they affect others. Example: I want lots of toys but don’t realize that making them uses up resources.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare causes and effects of conflict and cooperation in politics, economics, and culture, with examples.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can explain causes and effects of conflict and cooperation among individuals, groups, societies, and nations.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name one cause and one effect of cooperation or conflict, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can give an example of people working together.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Apply concepts such as location, distance, direction, scale, movement and region.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can consistently and accurately apply geographic concepts to analyze complex spatial information and solve problems. Example: I can analyze how Qatar's regions are connected through transportation routes and explain population movements toward urban areas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can accurately apply geographic concepts to interpret maps and describe spatial relationships. Example: I can use a map scale to estimate the distance between Doha and Al Wakrah and explain the direction from one to the other.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify and define geographic concepts with some accuracy; application is inconsistent. Example: I can locate Doha and Al Khor on a map and describe their positions using cardinal directions.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify basic geographic terms like "map" and "globe" but struggle to apply them accurately. Example: I can point to Qatar on a map but cannot explain its location relative to neighboring countries.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe ways physical and human-made features have changed over time.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze and explain the causes and effects of changes in physical and humanmade features over time. Example: I can discuss how land reclamation projects like Lusail have transformed the coastline and the reasons behind these changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe specific changes in physical and humanmade features over time with appropriate examples. Example: I can explain how the Corniche area in Doha changed from a fishing port to a modern cityscape.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize some changes in physical and humanmade features with limited explanation. Example: I can identify that The Pearl-Qatar is a new development but cannot explain its transformation over time.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify physical and humanmade features but do not recognize changes over time. Example: I can name the desert and buildings in Qatar but cannot describe how they have changed.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe how cultural contributions from various groups have formed a national identity.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the significance of diverse cultural contributions and their impact on national identity. Example: I can analyze how diverse cultures contributed to events like the FIFA World Cup 2022, blending global and Qatari identities.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how various cultural contributions have collectively shaped national identity. Example: I can explain how Qatari traditions like pearl diving and dhow building, along with international influences, shape national celebrations like Qatar National Day.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize some cultural contributions with limited connection to national identity. Example: I can identify that various nationalities have influenced food or clothing styles in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify cultural groups but lack understanding of their contributions to national identity. Example: I know that people from different countries live in Qatar but don't understand how they influence Qatari culture.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify and describe ways that ethnicity and cultures influence people's daily lives.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the interplay between cultural influences and daily life, providing detailed examples. Example: I can compare daily routines during Ramadan and Eid in Qatar to other cultural celebrations in different communities.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe specific ways in which ethnicity and culture influence daily practices and traditions. Example: I can explain how practices like Ramadan fasting and Majlis gatherings reflect cultural values.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some cultural influences on daily life with limited detail. Example: I can describe simple traditions like eating dates and Arabic coffee during gatherings.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I recognize that different cultures exist but cannot describe their influence on daily life. Example: I know that people wear different clothes but don't understand why.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify the elements of major political systems (e.g., monarchy, democracy, constitutional monarchy, dictatorship).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare and contrast the elements of various political systems with detailed analysis. Example: I can explain the benefits and challenges of different political systems using Qatar and another country as examples.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can accurately identify and describe the key elements of major political systems. Example: I can describe Qatar’s monarchy and compare it with democratic systems elsewhere.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify major political systems with basic descriptions of their elements. Example: I recognize Qatar as a monarchy ruled by an Emir.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name some political systems but cannot describe their elements. Example: I know that Qatar is ruled by a leader but cannot identify the system.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe the organization and major responsibilities of the various levels of governments.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the interrelationship between various levels of government and evaluate their responsibilities. Example: I can explain how different ministries collaborate, such as during national events or public health campaigns.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe the organization and major responsibilities of local, state, and national governments. Example: I can describe the role of ministries such as the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Interior.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify levels of government with limited understanding of their organization and responsibilities. Example: I know that the Emir makes important decisions and mention ministries.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I recognize different levels of government but cannot describe their organization or responsibilities. Example: I know that the government exists in Qatar but don't know what it does.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain what citizenship is.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the roles and responsibilities of citizenship and its impact on communities. Example: I can discuss how active citizenship, like volunteering, contributes to the well-being of society.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can clearly explain the concept of citizenship and its significance in society. Example: I can explain that citizenship includes rights and responsibilities, such as obeying laws and participating in the community.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can provide a basic explanation of citizenship with some examples. Example: I know that citizens have rights like voting but can't explain responsibilities.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have a limited understanding of the concept of citizenship. Example: I think a citizen is just someone who lives in a country.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify and describe means by which citizens can monitor, evaluate and influence actions of their government.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the effectiveness of different methods citizens use to engage with and influence government. Example: I can compare how petitions and social media campaigns can lead to policy changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe various means by which citizens monitor, evaluate, and influence government actions. Example: I can explain that citizens can write to officials, participate in public forums, or join community groups to influence decisions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some methods citizens use to influence government with limited detail. Example: I know that people can vote or attend meetings but can't explain their impact.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I recognize that citizens can interact with government but cannot describe how. Example: I know people can talk to the government but don't know the ways.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe the roles of laws, courts of law, and judges.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the impact of laws, courts, and judges on society and individual rights. Example: I can discuss how fair trials protect individual rights and maintain public trust in the legal system.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the roles and importance of laws, courts, and judges in maintaining order and justice. Example: I can explain that laws set rules, courts interpret them, and judges ensure fair application.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the basic functions of laws, courts, and judges with limited detail. Example: I can say that laws keep order and judges make decisions in court.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify laws, courts, and judges but lack understanding of their roles. Example: I know that judges work in courts but don't know what they do.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe how changes in transportation and communication have affected trade and economic activities.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the broader economic impacts of changes in transportation and communication over time. Example: I can discuss how digital communication has enabled Qatar to participate in global markets and attract international investment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how advancements in transportation and communication have influenced trade and economic activities. Example: I can explain that improved shipping and internet services have expanded Qatar's trade opportunities.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some changes in transportation and communication with limited connection to economic activities. Example: I can say that faster transport helps businesses but can't explain how.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I recognize transportation and communication methods but cannot relate them to trade or economy. Example: I know about cars and phones but don't see how they affect business.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain and compare ways in which people satisfy their basic needs and wants through the production of goods and services.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate different economic systems and their effectiveness in meeting people's needs and wants. Example: I can analyze how Qatar's mixed economy combines government planning and private enterprise to provide services.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain and compare various ways people produce goods and services to meet their needs and wants. Example: I can compare how local markets and supermarkets provide food, discussing differences in production and distribution.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some methods of satisfying needs and wants with limited comparison. Example: I can say that farmers grow food and factories make products but can't compare them.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify basic needs and wants but cannot explain how they are met. Example: I know people need food and shelter but don't know how they get them.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Describe changes in scientific knowledge and technology that have affected your host country.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the implications of scientific and technological advancements on various aspects of the host country's development. Example: I can discuss how Qatar’s investment in solar energy and smart city technologies supports sustainability and improves living standards.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe specific changes in scientific knowledge and technology and their effects on the host country. Example: I can explain how advances in desalination technology help provide fresh water for people in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some changes in science and technology with limited explanation of their impact. Example: I can say that Qatar has high-speed internet and modern hospitals, but I can't explain what difference they make.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I recognize that scientific and technological changes occur but cannot describe their effects. Example: I know that Qatar has new buildings and machines, but I don’t know how they changed things.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify cause and effect relationships in history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze a Qatari historical event using different sources and explain how cause and effect shaped the present. Example: I can compare an old newspaper and a current report to show how oil affected modern Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain both the causes and effects of a Qatari historical event using both primary and secondary sources. Example: I can use photos and articles to explain how oil discovery changed Qatari society.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a cause or effect of a Qatari historical event using one type of source. Example: I can explain that oil discovery led to economic growth using a textbook.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a historical event in Qatar but cannot explain why it happened or what it caused. Example: I can say the discovery of oil was important, but not why or how.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Identify and use primary and secondary sources to examine the past and present.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare a primary and a secondary source about the same event and explain which is more useful and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify primary and secondary sources and use them to find out about the past and present.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort sources into primary or secondary with help and find one fact in a source.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can look at an old photo or object and say one thing it shows about the past.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf')

subject: Social Studies
text: Explain the major ways groups, societies, and nations interact with one another (e.g., trade, cultural exchanges, and international organizations).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how Qatar’s cooperation or conflict influenced relationships with other countries. Example: I can explain how Qatar’s peace efforts improved its global partnerships.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain why Qatar had a conflict or cooperated and what happened as a result. Example: I can explain how Qatar acted as a mediator and helped solve a regional disagreement.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a cause or an effect of a conflict or cooperative event involving Qatar. Example: I can say Qatar cooperated with the UN to help refugees.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a time Qatar had a conflict or helped another country, but I don’t know why it happened. Example: I know Qatar helped during a conflict but not why or how.

descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can compare how trade, cultural exchange, and international organizations connect Qatar with other nations.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can explain the major ways groups, societies, and nations interact, such as trade, cultural exchange, and international organizations.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name one way Qatar interacts with another country, with help.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can name a country that Qatar is friends with.

source: AERO Social Studies Curriculum Framework: K-5 Learning Progression (school copy, 'Social Studies Standards K-5 Aero .pdf'); placement and descriptors: Awsaj 'Social Studies Standards.xlsx' (K-5 report-card sheet)

subject: Social Studies
text: Apply concepts such as location, distance, direction, scale, movement and region.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare different regions in Qatar and explain how natural resources shape land use. Example: I can describe how oil fields in Dukhan led to industrial land use.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use geography terms to explain where and why people live and work in Qatar. Example: I can explain how Qatar’s coast led to fishing villages like Al Wakrah.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe Qatar’s location and give one reason for its settlement pattern. Example: I can say people live in Doha because it's near the sea.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name cities in Qatar but struggle to explain where they are or why people live there. Example: I know Doha is a city but not why it’s important.

subject: Social Studies

cluster: SS.Inq2: Wisconsin students will gather and evaluate sources. | Inq2.b: Evaluate sources

ee_text: Wisconsin students will develop claims to answer an inquiry question.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq3: Wisconsin students will develop claims using evidence to support reasoning. | Inq3.c: Elaborate how evidence supports a claim
text: Assess how evidence supports a claim.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will develop claims to answer an inquiry question.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can assess how well evidence supports a claim.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say if evidence supports a claim, with help.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq4: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions. | Inq4.a: Communicate conclusions
text: Communicate conclusions from a variety of teacher-provided presentation options.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions of a claim.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can communicate conclusions using one of the presentation options my teacher gives.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq4: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions. | Inq4.b: Critique conclusions
text: Evaluate the strength of a claim, evidence, and communication using criteria established by both teacher and student.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions of a claim.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can give helpful feedback on a claim and use feedback to improve my own.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq5: Wisconsin students will be civically engaged. | Inq5.a: Civic engagement

ee_text: Wisconsin students will be civically engaged.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can plan a civic action with others and explain how it helps the community or the world.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explore opportunities to take civic action alone or with others in my community, school, country, or world.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way people can help their community, with help.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can take part in civic action on an issue that matters to me.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH2: Wisconsin students will investigate and interpret interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology). | BH2.a: Relationship of people and groups
text: Compare how people from different cultures solve common problems, such as distribution of food, shelter, and social interactions.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will investigate interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why two cultures solve the same problem in different ways.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare how people from different cultures solve common problems, such as food, shelter, and getting along.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH3: Wisconsin students will assess the role that human behavior and cultures play in the development of social endeavors (Anthropology). | BH3.a: Social interactions
text: Investigate how interpretations of similarities and differences between and among cultures may lead to understandings or misunderstandings.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine how human behavior and cultures can influence people, events, and other cultures (Anthropology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a misunderstanding between cultures could be fixed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can investigate how similarities and differences between cultures can lead to understanding or misunderstanding.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH4: Wisconsin students will examine the progression of specific forms of technology and their influence within various societies. | BH4.a: Progression of technology
text: Classify technologies based on intended use, access, and design, and how they might change people’s lives (for better or worse).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the progression of specific forms of technology and their influence within various societies or cultures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a technology changed people's lives for better and for worse.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can classify technologies by use, access, and design and explain how they might change people's lives.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort technologies by what they are used for, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name two technologies.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how a technology has changed over time and how it influences societies or cultures.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ2: Wisconsin students will analyze how decisions are made and interactions occur among individuals, households, and firms or businesses (Microeconomics). | Econ2.b: Supply, demand, and competition
text: Assess the roles of consumers (demand), producers (supply), prices, non-price factors (e.g., drought or a fad item), and competition in the product market.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will understand how decisions are made and interactions occur among consumers (i.e., individuals and households) and producers (firms/businesses) (Microeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict how a change, such as a drought or a fad, will affect prices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can assess the roles of consumers (demand), producers (supply), prices, and competition in a market.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain what happens to price when many people want a product, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that people buy and sell at a market.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can understand how consumers and producers make decisions and interact.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ3: Wisconsin students will analyze how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics). | Econ3.b: Money
text: Describe the role of money, banking, and savings in everyday life, including why people borrow money and the role of interest.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how interest affects saving and borrowing, using a simple example.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe the role of money, banking, and saving in everyday life, including why people borrow and the role of interest.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say why people put money in a bank, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a bank or a place to keep money.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify how an economy works as a whole, such as prices, jobs, and saving.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.b: Institutions

ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how banks or the government help society and compare private and public property.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify government decisions and how they affect people, businesses, markets, and resources.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.c: Role of government

ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.d: Impact of government interventions

subject: Social Studies

text: Use evidence to draw conclusions about probable effects of historical events, issues, and problems.

cluster: SS.Hist2: Wisconsin students will analyze, recognize, and evaluate patterns of continuity and change over time and contextualization of historical events. | Hist2.b: Patterns change over a period of time
