subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH1: Wisconsin students will examine individual cognition, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology). | BH1.a: Individual cognition, perception, and behavior
text: Identify patterns such as culture, prior knowledge, family, peers, school, communities, and personal interests that influence a person’s cognition, perception, and behavior.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine individual learning, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how several factors combine to shape a person's thinking and behavior in a case study.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify patterns such as culture, prior knowledge, family, peers, and school that influence a person's thinking and behavior.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name two influences on a person's behavior with examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one thing that influences how I act.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people learn, see things, behave, and form identity.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH1: Wisconsin students will examine individual cognition, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology). | BH1.b: Personal identity and empathy
text: Analyze how culture, ethnicity, race, age, religion, gender, and social class affect a person's self-image and identity and interactions with others.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine individual learning, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how identity factors affect interactions between people and suggest ways to build empathy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how culture, ethnicity, age, religion, gender, and social class affect a person's self-image, identity, and interactions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how one identity factor affects self-image.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name parts of my own identity.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people learn, see things, behave, and form identity.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH2: Wisconsin students will investigate and interpret interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology). | BH2.a: Relationship of people and groups
text: Summarize the role culture plays in personal and group behavior. Categorize factors that contribute to cooperation and conflict among peoples of a country and/or the world (i.e., culture, language, religion, political beliefs).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will investigate interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare causes of cooperation and conflict between two peoples and suggest ways to build cooperation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can summarize the role culture plays in behavior and categorize factors that lead to cooperation and conflict among peoples.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort factors into causes of cooperation or conflict, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can give one example of cooperation and one of conflict.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can investigate how people and groups interact with each other.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH2: Wisconsin students will investigate and interpret interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology). | BH2.b: Cultural patterns
text: Model how individuals learn the elements of their culture through interactions with others, and how individuals learn of other cultures through communication, travel, and study.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will investigate interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can model how I learned parts of my culture and how I learn about other cultures.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can model how people learn their culture through interaction and learn other cultures through communication, travel, and study.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way people learn about another culture.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one tradition I learned from my family.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can investigate how people and groups interact with each other.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH3: Wisconsin students will assess the role that human behavior and cultures play in the development of social endeavors (Anthropology). | BH3.a: Social interactions
text: Analyze how a person’s local actions can have global consequences and how global patterns and processes can affect seemingly unrelated local actions.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine how human behavior and cultures can influence people, events, and other cultures (Anthropology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can trace how a local action in Qatar has global consequences and the reverse.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how local actions can have global consequences and how global patterns affect local actions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of a local action with a global effect.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a global issue that affects Qatar.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how behavior and culture can influence people, events, and other cultures.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH4: Wisconsin students will examine the progression of specific forms of technology and their influence within various societies. | BH4.a: Progression of technology
text: Differentiate between intended and unintended consequences of various forms of technology and how they may affect societies and cultures.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the progression of specific forms of technology and their influence within various societies or cultures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate intended and unintended consequences of a technology for two societies.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can differentiate between intended and unintended consequences of technologies and how they affect societies and cultures.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one intended and one unintended effect of a technology.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a technology and what it is for.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how a technology has changed over time and how it influences societies or cultures.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ1: Wisconsin students use economic reasoning to understand issues. | Econ1.a: Choices and decision making
text: Predict the opportunity costs of various decisions and explain why the opportunity cost might differ from person to person or in different situations. Assess how limited resources (e.g., money, land, natural resources, workers, time) impact the choices of individuals, households, communities, businesses, and countries.
ee_text: Wisconsin students use economic reasoning to understand issues.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why opportunity cost differs between two people and how scarcity shapes national choices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can predict opportunity costs of decisions and assess how limited resources affect the choices of people, businesses, and countries.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the opportunity cost of a simple decision.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can explain that resources are limited.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use economic reasoning, such as costs and benefits, to understand an issue.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ1: Wisconsin students use economic reasoning to understand issues. | Econ1.b: Incentives
text: Evaluate how incentives impact individual and/or household decision making.
ee_text: Wisconsin students use economic reasoning to understand issues.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate whether an incentive will change household decisions and predict side effects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate how incentives affect individual and household decision making.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain how one incentive changes a decision.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name an incentive, such as a discount.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use economic reasoning, such as costs and benefits, to understand an issue.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ2: Wisconsin students will analyze how decisions are made and interactions occur among individuals, households, and firms or businesses (Microeconomics). | Econ2.a: Consumers, producers, and markets
text: Analyze the role of consumers and producers in product markets. Provide examples of how individuals and households are both consumers and producers.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will understand how decisions are made and interactions occur among consumers (i.e., individuals and households) and producers (firms/businesses) (Microeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how households act as both consumers and producers in different markets.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze the role of consumers and producers in product markets with examples.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way consumers and producers interact.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell the difference between a consumer and a producer.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can understand how consumers and producers make decisions and interact.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ2: Wisconsin students will analyze how decisions are made and interactions occur among individuals, households, and firms or businesses (Microeconomics). | Econ2.b: Supply, demand, and competition
text: Investigate the relationship between supply and demand. Evaluate the extent to which competition exists in product markets, and its relationship to price and quality of goods and services.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will understand how decisions are made and interactions occur among consumers (i.e., individuals and households) and producers (firms/businesses) (Microeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a simple supply and demand graph to predict price changes and explain competition effects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can investigate the relationship between supply and demand and evaluate how competition affects price and quality.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain what happens to price when demand rises.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define supply and demand.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can understand how consumers and producers make decisions and interact.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ2: Wisconsin students will analyze how decisions are made and interactions occur among individuals, households, and firms or businesses (Microeconomics). | Econ2.c: Firm/business behavior and costs of production
text: Categorize factors of production and how they are combined to make goods and deliver services. Evaluate how profits influence sellers in markets.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will understand how decisions are made and interactions occur among consumers (i.e., individuals and households) and producers (firms/businesses) (Microeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a business could change its mix of production factors to raise profit.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can categorize factors of production and evaluate how profits influence sellers.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort examples into land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name what is needed to make a product.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can understand how consumers and producers make decisions and interact.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ3: Wisconsin students will analyze how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics). | Econ3.a: Economic indicators
text: Analyze how inflation, deflation, and unemployment affect different groups.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how inflation and unemployment affect two different groups and explain why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how inflation, deflation, and unemployment affect different groups.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain what inflation means using a price example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that prices can go up over time.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify how an economy works as a whole, such as prices, jobs, and saving.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ3: Wisconsin students will analyze how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics). | Econ3.b: Money
text: Differentiate between the functions of money (i.e., medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account). Assess how interest rates influence borrowing and investing.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a change in interest rates would affect a saver and a borrower.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can differentiate between the functions of money and assess how interest rates influence borrowing and investing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the three functions of money with examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say why people use money.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify how an economy works as a whole, such as prices, jobs, and saving.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ3: Wisconsin students will analyze how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics). | Econ3.c: Economic fluctuations and business cycles
text: Define Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and compare the GDP of different nations.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify how an economy functions as a whole (Macroeconomics).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain what GDP comparisons show and do not show about life in two countries.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can define Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and compare the GDP of different nations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read GDP figures for two countries from a chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that GDP measures what a country produces.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify how an economy works as a whole, such as prices, jobs, and saving.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.a: Economic systems and allocation of resources
text: Compare and contrast how different economic systems (traditional, command, market, mixed) choose to allocate the production, distribution, and consumption of resources (what, how, for whom is it produced).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate which economic system best answers what, how, and for whom to produce in a case.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare and contrast how traditional, command, market, and mixed economies allocate resources.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match an economic system to its description.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one type of economic system.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify government decisions and how they affect people, businesses, markets, and resources.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.b: Institutions
text: Compare and contrast the role of different economic institutions such as banks, labor unions, non-profits, and businesses in an economy. Analyze rules and laws that protect and support both consumers (e.g., private property, zoning, contracts, agreements, and product safety) and workers (e.g., labor unions, regulations, minimum wage).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how a rule or law protects both consumers and workers in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare economic institutions such as banks and businesses and analyze rules that protect consumers and workers.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the role of one economic institution.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a bank or a business.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify government decisions and how they affect people, businesses, markets, and resources.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.c: Role of government
text: Analyze the impact of different government policies (e.g., taxation and government spending) on the economy.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the effect of a government spending decision on different groups.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze the impact of government policies such as taxes and spending on the economy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way government spending affects people.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name something the government spends money on.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify government decisions and how they affect people, businesses, markets, and resources.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.d: Impact of government interventions
text: Analyze potential unintended costs and benefits (i.e., externalities) for a local or state law or policy.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict externalities of a proposed local law and suggest changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze possible unintended costs and benefits (externalities) of a local or national law or policy.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify one externality of a policy with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one effect of a rule.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify government decisions and how they affect people, businesses, markets, and resources.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Econ4: Wisconsin students will evaluate government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government). | Econ4.e: Specialization, trade, and interdependence
text: Summarize the role of specialization on trade and cost of goods/services. Identify examples of U.S. exports and imports.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify government decisions and their impact on individuals, businesses, markets, and resources (Role of Government).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how specialization and trade affect prices of Qatar's imports and exports.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can summarize the role of specialization in trade and cost and identify examples of exports and imports.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort products into imports and exports for Qatar.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name one thing Qatar exports.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify government decisions and how they affect people, businesses, markets, and resources.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog1: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to analyze the world. | Geog1.a: Tools of geography
text: Use paper and digital maps to ask and answer geographic questions (e.g., Where are there patterns? Why there? So what?). Analyze how various map projections distort shape, area, distance, and direction (e.g., Mercator, Robinson, Peters).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to explore the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare map projections and explain which is best for a given question.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use paper and digital maps to answer geographic questions and analyze how map projections distort shape and size.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a map to answer a where question.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a country on a world map.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use geographic tools, such as maps, to explore the world.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog1: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to analyze the world. | Geog1.b: Spatial thinking (map interpretation)
text: Interpret patterns in a variety of maps, charts, and graphs to display geographic information (contour, cartogram, population, natural resource, historical maps) and explain relationships among them.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to explore the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can interpret patterns across several thematic maps and explain how they are related.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret patterns in maps, charts, and graphs and explain relationships among them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one pattern on a thematic map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read the title and key of a map.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use geographic tools, such as maps, to explore the world.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog1: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to analyze the world. | Geog1.c: Mental mapping and maps from memory
text: Construct a mental map of regions and locate the major regions of the world and their physical and cultural features including continents, cities, countries, bodies of water, landforms, mountain ranges, and climate zones. Compare mental maps shaped by individual perceptions of people, places, regions, and environments.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to explore the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can draw a world mental map from memory and compare it with an accurate map.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct a mental map of world regions with physical and cultural features and compare mental maps.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can label continents, oceans, and major regions on a blank map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the continents.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use geographic tools, such as maps, to explore the world.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.a: Population and place
text: Analyze why populations increase or decrease in various regions throughout the world. Analyze the distribution of population patterns at various scales (i.e., local, state, country, region).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why population is rising in one region and falling in another, using data.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze why populations increase or decrease in world regions and analyze population patterns at different scales.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a population pattern on a map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say which places have many people.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.b: Reasons people move
text: Analyze patterns of migration of various types (e.g., age, sex, ethnicity, race) in the community, state, country, and world.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare migration patterns of two groups and explain the reasons.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze patterns of migration of different groups in the community, country, and world.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one migration pattern using a map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a reason people migrate.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.c: Impact of movement
text: Use regions in the world to analyze the role of population shifts in why places change over time. Evaluate the impact of migration on the place of origin and the place of settlement.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how migration changed both the place of origin and the place of settlement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use world regions to analyze how population shifts change places and evaluate the impact of migration.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way migration changes a place.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say that migration changes places.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.d: Urbanization
text: Investigate the impact of rural decline and the growth of cities on a place. Analyze patterns of urbanization around the world.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare urbanization in Qatar with another region and predict future changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can investigate the impact of rural decline and city growth and analyze patterns of urbanization worldwide.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one effect of a city growing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell the difference between rural and urban.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog3: Wisconsin students will examine the impacts of global interconnections and relationships. | Geog3.a: Distribution of resources
text: Analyze the relationship between the distribution of resources and patterns of human settlement within states, countries, and regions of the world now and in the past.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify the effects of global distribution of resources and geographic networks.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how the location of resources shaped settlement in the Gulf now and in the past.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the effects of where resources are found and how places are connected.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog3: Wisconsin students will examine the impacts of global interconnections and relationships. | Geog3.b: Networks
text: Analyze spatial patterns of social and economic development in a variety of regions in the world. Identify how people, products, and ideas move between places (e.g., internet commerce, outsourcing).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify the effects of global distribution of resources and geographic networks.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how the movement of people, products, and ideas links Qatar to world regions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze spatial patterns of development and identify how people, products, and ideas move between places.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of how products or ideas move between countries.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a way products travel.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the effects of where resources are found and how places are connected.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog4: Wisconsin students will evaluate the relationship between identity and place. | Geog4.a: Characteristics of place

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how a place and people's identity are connected.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog5: Wisconsin students will evaluate the relationship between humans and the environment. | Geog5.a: Human environment interaction
text: Analyze how technology interacts with the environment and how increased use of technology affects the burden and use of natural resources.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the relationships between humans and the environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how a technology both helps and burdens natural resources in Qatar.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how technology interacts with the environment and affects the use of natural resources.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can give one example of a technology that affects the environment.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a natural resource.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people and the environment affect each other.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog5: Wisconsin students will evaluate the relationship between humans and the environment. | Geog5.b: Interdependence

cluster: SS.PS1: Wisconsin students will identify and analyze democratic principles and ideals. | PS1.b: Origins and foundation of the government of the United States

ee_text: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions of a claim.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq4: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions. | Inq4.b: Critique conclusions
text: Examine a claim’s strengths and weaknesses, including an evaluation of supporting evidence, taking into consideration cultural, social, economic, political, geographic, and historic influences that inform these perspectives.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions of a claim.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq5: Wisconsin students will be civically engaged. | Inq5.a: Civic engagement
text: Explore opportunities, informed by the knowledge and methods of the social sciences, for personal or collaborative civic engagement with community, school, state, tribal, national, and/or global implications.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will be civically engaged.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and lead a civic action informed by social science research and evaluate its results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explore civic engagement opportunities informed by the knowledge and methods of the social sciences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can plan one civic action on a local issue.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can take part in civic action on an issue that matters to me.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog1: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to analyze the world. | Geog1.a: Tools of geography
text: Use printed and digital maps to ask and answer geographic questions (e.g., Where are there patterns? Why there? So what?) and evaluate the appropriateness of geographic data and representations to understand real-world problems. Explain how current geospatial technologies (e.g., Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), satellite images, remote sensing) are used for personal, business, and government purposes.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to explore the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use GIS or digital maps to analyze a real-world problem and evaluate the data used.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use printed and digital maps to answer geographic questions and explain how geospatial technologies are used.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a digital map to answer a geographic question.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a geospatial tool such as GPS.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use geographic tools, such as maps, to explore the world.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog1: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to analyze the world. | Geog1.b: Spatial thinking (map interpretation)
text: Interpret maps and images (e.g., political, physical, relief, thematic, virtual or electronic) to analyze geographic problems and changes over time.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to explore the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can interpret several map types to explain how a geographic problem changed over time.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret maps and images to analyze geographic problems and changes over time.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe a change shown on two maps from different years.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify the type of a map.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use geographic tools, such as maps, to explore the world.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog1: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to analyze the world. | Geog1.c: Mental mapping and maps from memory
text: Compare and contrast a mental map before and after an event to see if perception reshaped their perspectives. Explain how using a virtual or electronic mapping application can aid in the development of a more complete and accurate mental map of places and region.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use geographic tools and ways of thinking to explore the world.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare my mental map before and after an event and explain how digital tools improved it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare mental maps before and after an event and explain how digital mapping improves mental maps.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw a mental map of a region and compare it to a real map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw a simple map from memory.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use geographic tools, such as maps, to explore the world.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.a: Population and place
text: Evaluate population policies by analyzing how governments affect population change. Analyze population compositions (e.g., age, gender, ethnicity) and the different implications each has on countries or regions throughout the world.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate a population policy using composition data and predict its effects.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate population policies and analyze population compositions and their implications.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a population pyramid and describe its shape.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define population composition.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.b: Reasons people move
text: Evaluate the impact of major international migrations, both past and present, on physical and human systems.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the impact of major international migrations on physical and human systems.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.c: Impact of movement
text: Analyze the social impact of movement of people to different locations in a variety of time periods and locations throughout the world.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze the social impact of the movement of people across time periods and places.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog2: Wisconsin students will analyze human movement and population patterns. | Geog2.d: Urbanization
text: Evaluate the impact of spatial inequality as a result of urbanization and develop various solutions to address these inequalities. Analyze the impact of rural decline and urbanization on a place.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify reasons for human movement and explore population patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can propose solutions to spatial inequality caused by urbanization in a real city.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate spatial inequality from urbanization and analyze the impact of rural decline and urbanization.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one effect of urbanization on a place.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define urbanization.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify reasons people move and explore population patterns.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog3: Wisconsin students will examine the impacts of global interconnections and relationships. | Geog3.a: Distribution of resources
text: Evaluate, in both current and historical context, how the prospect of gaining access to resources in contested zones creates competition among countries. Assess how and why consumption of resources (e.g., petroleum, coal, electricity, steel, water, food) differs between developed and developing countries now and in the past.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify the effects of global distribution of resources and geographic networks.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate competition for resources in a contested zone and how consumption differs by country.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate how access to resources creates competition and assess why resource use differs between countries.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare resource use in a developed and a developing country.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a resource countries compete for.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the effects of where resources are found and how places are connected.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog3: Wisconsin students will examine the impacts of global interconnections and relationships. | Geog3.b: Networks
text: Analyze the evolution of the global economy to its present state and the role it plays in the economic development of world regions. Analyze the role of supranational organizations (e.g., NAFTA, NATO, UN).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify the effects of global distribution of resources and geographic networks.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how the global economy and supranational organizations shape a region's development.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze the evolution of the global economy and the role of supranational organizations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the role of one supranational organization such as the UN or GCC.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name an international organization.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the effects of where resources are found and how places are connected.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog4: Wisconsin students will evaluate the relationship between identity and place. | Geog4.a: Characteristics of place
text: Evaluate the effect of culture on a place over time. Analyze how physical and human characteristics interact to give a place meaning and significance (e.g., Panama Canal, Chunnel) and shape culture. Explain how and why place-based identities can shape events at various scales (e.g., neighborhood, regional identity). Explain how and why people view places and regions differently as a function of their ideology, race, ethnicity, language, gender, age, religion, politics, social class, and economic status.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the relationship between identity and place.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how ideology, culture, and identity shape how people see places and events.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate how culture and characteristics give a place meaning and how place-based identities shape events.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how physical and human features give a place meaning.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a place with special meaning.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how a place and people's identity are connected.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog5: Wisconsin students will evaluate the relationship between humans and the environment. | Geog5.a: Human environment interaction
text: Analyze the intentional and unintentional spatial consequences of human actions on the environment at the local, state, tribal, regional, country, and world levels.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the relationships between humans and the environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the spatial consequences of a human action at several scales and propose solutions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze intended and unintended spatial consequences of human actions on the environment at different levels.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one consequence of a human action on the environment.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a human action that changes the environment.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people and the environment affect each other.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Geog5: Wisconsin students will evaluate the relationship between humans and the environment. | Geog5.b: Interdependence
text: Hypothesize how changes in human behavior (e.g., organic agriculture, Genetically Modified Organisms, ecotourism) can result in changes that have effects on a global scale.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the relationships between humans and the environment.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can hypothesize the global effects of a change in human behavior and support it with evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can hypothesize how changes in human behavior can cause effects on a global scale.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one way a change in behavior affects the environment.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people and the environment affect each other.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq1: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions that initiate an inquiry. | Inq1.a: Develop questions based on a topic
text: Frame researchable, complex, and open-ended questions, integrating multiple social studies strands that call for investigation.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions related to a social studies topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can frame a complex research question that links three strands and justify why it needs investigation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can frame researchable, complex, open-ended questions that integrate several social studies strands.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can construct meaningful questions about a social studies topic.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq1: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions that initiate an inquiry. | Inq1.b: Plan an inquiry
text: Construct questions that support the research and identify the sources that will be used in the student-developed research proposal.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions related to a social studies topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a full research proposal with supporting questions and evaluated sources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct supporting questions and identify the sources I will use in my research proposal.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq2: Wisconsin students will gather and evaluate sources. | Inq2.a: Gather diverse sources (electronic, digital, print, and other mass media) applicable to the inquiry
text: Explore evidence discovered through personal research through a variety of disciplinary lenses (e.g., economics, history, political science) and multiple perspectives (e.g., race, gender, ethnicity, language, ability, sexual orientation, family background, and/or family income) with a variety of sources including primary and secondary sources and media resources.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will gather and select reliable sources related to a social studies topic or issue.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can gather and choose reliable sources about a social studies topic or issue.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq2: Wisconsin students will gather and evaluate sources. | Inq2.b: Evaluate sources

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim to answer an inquiry question.

cluster: SS.Inq1: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions that initiate an inquiry. | Inq1.a: Develop questions based on a topic
text: Frame researchable, complex, and open-ended questions, integrating multiple social studies strands that call for investigation.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions related to a social studies topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can frame a complex research question that links three strands and justify why it needs investigation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can frame researchable, complex, open-ended questions that integrate several social studies strands.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask an open question about a topic.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can construct meaningful questions about a social studies topic.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq1: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions that initiate an inquiry. | Inq1.b: Plan an inquiry
text: Construct questions that support the research and identify the sources that will be used in the student-developed research proposal.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will construct meaningful questions related to a social studies topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a full research proposal with supporting questions and evaluated sources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can construct supporting questions and identify the sources I will use in my research proposal.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list supporting questions and two sources for a research plan, with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can list what I want to find out.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can construct meaningful questions about a social studies topic.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq2: Wisconsin students will gather and evaluate sources. | Inq2.a: Gather diverse sources (electronic, digital, print, and other mass media) applicable to the inquiry
text: Explore evidence discovered through personal research through a variety of disciplinary lenses (e.g., economics, history, political science) and multiple perspectives (e.g., race, gender, ethnicity, language, ability, sexual orientation, family background, and/or family income) with a variety of sources including primary and secondary sources and media resources.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will gather and select reliable sources related to a social studies topic or issue.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can gather evidence through several disciplinary lenses and perspectives and explain gaps in the evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explore evidence from my own research through different disciplines and perspectives, using primary, secondary, and media sources.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can gather primary and secondary sources on my topic from a given list.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find one source on my topic.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can gather and choose reliable sources about a social studies topic or issue.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq2: Wisconsin students will gather and evaluate sources. | Inq2.b: Evaluate sources
text: Analyze and weigh relevance of a source through a disciplinary lens to determine how the author, context, audience, and purpose affect the reliability, limitations, and usefulness of a source.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will gather and select reliable sources related to a social studies topic or issue.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can weigh several sources and explain how author, context, audience, and purpose change their reliability.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how the author, context, audience, and purpose affect a source's reliability, limits, and usefulness.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the author, audience, and purpose of a source.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say whether a source is primary or secondary.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can gather and choose reliable sources about a social studies topic or issue.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq3: Wisconsin students will develop claims using evidence to support reasoning. | Inq3.a: Develop claims to answer an inquiry question
text: Develop a defensible claim to provide focus for an inquiry that is based upon the analysis of sources.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim to answer an inquiry question.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq3: Wisconsin students will develop claims using evidence to support reasoning. | Inq3.b: Cite evidence from multiple sources to support a claim
text: Support a claim with evidence using sources from multiple perspectives and media (electronic, digital, print, and other mass media).

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq3: Wisconsin students will develop claims using evidence to support reasoning. | Inq3.c: Elaborate how evidence supports a claim
text: Analyze the extent to which evidence supports or does not support a claim, and if it does not, modify the claim appropriately.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will develop claims to answer an inquiry question.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how far evidence supports a claim and modify the claim if needed.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can make a claim to answer an inquiry question.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq4: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions. | Inq4.a: Communicate conclusions
text: Communicate conclusions while taking into consideration that audiences from diverse backgrounds (e.g., gender, class, proximity to the event or issue) may interpret the information in different ways).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions of a claim.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can adapt my conclusions for audiences with different backgrounds and explain my choices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can communicate conclusions while considering how diverse audiences may interpret them.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can state my conclusion.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can share and critique the conclusions of a claim.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq4: Wisconsin students will communicate and critique conclusions. | Inq4.b: Critique conclusions
text: Examine a claim’s strengths and weaknesses, including an evaluation of supporting evidence, taking into consideration cultural, social, economic, political, geographic, and historic influences that inform these perspectives.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can examine a claim's strengths and weaknesses, including its evidence and the influences behind its perspective.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can share and critique the conclusions of a claim.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.Inq5: Wisconsin students will be civically engaged. | Inq5.a: Civic engagement
text: Explore opportunities, informed by the knowledge and methods of the social sciences, for personal or collaborative civic engagement with community, school, state, tribal, national, and/or global implications.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will be civically engaged.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and lead a civic action informed by social science research and evaluate its results.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explore civic engagement opportunities informed by the knowledge and methods of the social sciences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can plan one civic action on a local issue.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify an issue that matters to my community.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can take part in civic action on an issue that matters to me.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH1: Wisconsin students will examine individual cognition, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology). | BH1.a: Individual cognition, perception, and behavior
text: Analyze biological and environmental factors that influence a person’s cognition, perception, and behavior. Explain the interaction of biology and experience (i.e., nature and nurture) and its influence on behavior. Using scientific practices, conduct research related to a problem or issue affecting individuals and/or society.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine individual learning, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design and conduct a small research study on a behavior and explain nature and nurture influences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze biological and environmental factors that influence behavior and explain the role of nature and nurture.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one biological and one environmental influence on behavior.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define nature and nurture.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people learn, see things, behave, and form identity.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH1: Wisconsin students will examine individual cognition, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology). | BH1.b: Personal identity and empathy
text: Examine the effects of discrimination on identity. Explore developmental theories (e.g., Piaget, Erikson, Maslow) as they relate to cultural bias.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine individual learning, perception, behavior, and identity (Psychology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how discrimination affects identity using a developmental theory and evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can examine the effects of discrimination on identity and explore developmental theories in relation to cultural bias.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one developmental theory and how it relates to identity.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define discrimination.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how people learn, see things, behave, and form identity.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH2: Wisconsin students will investigate and interpret interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology). | BH2.a: Relationship of people and groups
text: Investigate how language and culture can unify a group of people. Evaluate the factors that contribute to cooperation and conflict among peoples of a country and the world (e.g., language, religion, culture, race, ethnicity, gender, social or financial inequity, political beliefs, access to resources, economics, environment).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will investigate interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate factors behind cooperation and conflict in a real case and propose ways to build unity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can investigate how language and culture unify groups and evaluate factors that cause cooperation and conflict.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how language or culture unifies a group.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can give an example of a group united by language.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can investigate how people and groups interact with each other.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH2: Wisconsin students will investigate and interpret interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology). | BH2.b: Cultural patterns
text: Critique interpretations of how different cultures interact with their environment.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will investigate interactions between individuals and groups (Sociology).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critique two interpretations of how a culture interacts with its environment.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can critique interpretations of how different cultures interact with their environment.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can summarize one interpretation of a culture's relationship with its environment.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe how one culture uses its environment.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can investigate how people and groups interact with each other.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH3: Wisconsin students will assess the role that human behavior and cultures play in the development of social endeavors (Anthropology). | BH3.a: Social interactions
text: Analyze the means by and extent to which groups and institutions can influence people, events, and cultures in both historical and contemporary settings. Become critically aware of ethnocentrism, its manifestations, and consequences in a world that is increasingly interconnected.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine how human behavior and cultures can influence people, events, and other cultures (Anthropology).

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how groups and institutions influence people, events, and cultures and recognize ethnocentrism.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can examine how behavior and culture can influence people, events, and other cultures.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.BH4: Wisconsin students will examine the progression of specific forms of technology and their influence within various societies. | BH4.a: Progression of technology
text: Evaluate the purpose for which a technology is created and analyze the consequences (intended and unintended) to different cultures.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine the progression of specific forms of technology and their influence within various societies or cultures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate a technology's purpose and its intended and unintended effects on two cultures.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the purpose of a technology and analyze its intended and unintended consequences for cultures.

subject: Social Studies

text: Evaluate multiple events from different perspectives using primary and secondary sources and analyze intended and unintended causes from both long- and short-term perspectives. Evaluate how different groups and individuals contributed to the event or cause.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use historical evidence for determining cause and effect.

cluster: SS.Hist1: Wisconsin students will use historical evidence for determining cause and effect. | Hist1.b: Effect
text: Evaluate multiple events from different perspectives using primary and secondary sources and analyze intended and unintended effects from both long- and short-term perspectives. Evaluate how different groups and individuals contributed to the effect.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will use historical evidence for determining cause and effect.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate long- and short-term effects from several perspectives and judge which mattered most.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate events from different perspectives using sources and analyze intended and unintended, long- and short-term effects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify a long-term and a short-term effect of an event.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use historical evidence to find causes and effects.

cluster: SS.Hist2: Wisconsin students will analyze, recognize, and evaluate patterns of continuity and change over time and contextualization of historical events. | Hist2.b: Patterns change over a period of time
text: Evaluate a variety of primary and secondary sources to apply knowledge of major eras, enduring themes, turning points, and historical influences to analyze the patterns of change in the community, the state, the United States and the world.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will recognize patterns of continuity and change over time, and contextualization of historical events.

descriptors.ee_at_target: I can recognize what changed and what stayed the same over time and the context of a historical event.

cluster: SS.Hist2: Wisconsin students will analyze, recognize, and evaluate patterns of continuity and change over time and contextualization of historical events. | Hist2.c: Contextualization

ee_text: Wisconsin students will recognize patterns of continuity and change over time, and contextualization of historical events.

cluster: SS.Hist4: Wisconsin students will evaluate a variety of primary and secondary sources to interpret the historical context, intended audience, purpose, or author’s point of view (Historical Methodology). | Hist4.c: Purpose

ee_text: Wisconsin students will examine a variety of primary and secondary sources to identify the historical context, intended audience, purpose, and/or author's point of view (Historical Methodology).

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.PS2: Wisconsin students will examine and interpret rights, privileges, and responsibilities in society. | PS2.a: Civil rights and civil liberties
text: Critique the struggle for suffrage and citizenship since the founding period. Analyze the constitutional tension between protecting individual rights and promoting the general welfare and security of the country, as well as between majority rule and minority rights. Assess the impact of individuals, groups, and movements on the development of civil rights for different groups.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify differences between a right, a responsibility, and a privilege.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critique the struggle for rights and evaluate the tension between individual rights and security.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can critique the struggle for suffrage and citizenship and analyze tensions between rights and the general welfare.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one movement that expanded rights.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define civil rights.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the differences between a right, a responsibility, and a privilege.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.PS2: Wisconsin students will examine and interpret rights, privileges, and responsibilities in society. | PS2.b: Fundamentals of citizenship
text: Assess the difference in constitutional and legal protections for citizens vs. noncitizens. Demonstrate the skills necessary to participate in the election process (i.e., registering to vote, identifying and evaluating candidates and issues, and casting a ballot).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify differences between a right, a responsibility, and a privilege.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare legal protections for citizens and noncitizens and model the election process.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can assess differences in protections for citizens and noncitizens and show skills needed to participate in elections.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe one difference between citizens and noncitizens.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can define citizen.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the differences between a right, a responsibility, and a privilege.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.PS2: Wisconsin students will examine and interpret rights, privileges, and responsibilities in society. | PS2.c: Asserting and reaffirming of human rights
text: Analyze how the U.S. Supreme Court has allowed the restriction and enabled the expansion of rights for groups. Evaluate different goals and methods of groups who have advocated for access to greater rights (e.g., women, religious groups, civil rights groups, indigenous peoples, LGBTQ). Analyze the role of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) and nongovernment organizations (NGOs such as Save the Children or the Red Cross) in how human rights have been addressed in different countries.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify differences between a right, a responsibility, and a privilege.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the methods of rights groups and the role of the UDHR and NGOs in different countries.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how courts and groups restricted or expanded rights and the role of the UDHR and NGOs.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the role of one NGO in protecting human rights.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the differences between a right, a responsibility, and a privilege.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.PS3: Wisconsin students will analyze and evaluate the powers and processes of political and civic institutions. | PS3.a: Political participation
text: Create and evaluate solutions to increase voter participation. Evaluate their role in government at the local, state, tribal, and federal levels.
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify the roles and processes of political and civic institutions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create and evaluate solutions to increase participation in public decisions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create and evaluate solutions to increase voter or civic participation and evaluate my role in government.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can suggest one way to increase participation.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a way citizens participate.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the roles and processes of political and civic institutions.

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.PS3: Wisconsin students will analyze and evaluate the powers and processes of political and civic institutions. | PS3.b: Linkage institutions
text: Evaluate the role of various types of media in elections and functions of government. Analyze how the United States political system is shaped by political parties, elections and the election process, including the caucus and primary systems and procedures involved in voting. Evaluate civic institutions and explain how competing interests impact societal change (e.g., lobbying, citizens groups, special interest groups).
ee_text: Wisconsin students will identify the roles and processes of political and civic institutions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how media, parties, and interest groups compete to influence policy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the role of media in government and how civic institutions and competing interests shape change.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe how the media influence public opinion.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name a civic institution.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the roles and processes of political and civic institutions.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Social Studies (DPI, 2018); EE: Wisconsin Essential Elements for Social Studies (DPI, adopted 2021, published 2022)

subject: Social Studies
cluster: SS.PS3: Wisconsin students will analyze and evaluate the powers and processes of political and civic institutions. | PS3.c: Power in government
text: Evaluate the structure and functions of governments at the local, state, tribal, national, and global levels. descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe the role of one national and one global institution.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name levels of government.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the roles and processes of political and civic institutions.
